papers_seen.author: Harper
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Default, Flexible Engine for Practical Model Compression — Central but Conditional
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as part of a deliberate compression pipeline, KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs across vision and language tasks. Its mechanisms range from softened-output matching to intermediate-feature and relational objectives, and KD composes naturally with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on student capacity, teacher quality, the signals chosen for transfer, and the availability and provenance of distillation data. Reliable deployment therefore treats KD as the core of a broader, task-aware compression strategy rather than as a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Starting Point for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Scope, Complementary Needs, and Conditional Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, first-line method for compressing large deep models into deployable students in both vision and NLP. KD reliably delivers large efficiency gains with modest performance loss when applied as a flexible toolkit (soft targets, intermediate feature transfer, attention/relational objectives, online/self-distillation) and when integrated with data-aware practices and complementary compression techniques. At the same time, KD is not sufficient by itself: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, data availability and provenance, architecture and capacity alignment, and explicit interventions to preserve robustness, fairness, and privacy. Practical pipelines therefore begin with KD but must plan for targeted architectural adaptation, quantization/pruning, data strategies (filtering, synthesis, or data-free methods), and careful evaluation under domain shift and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to convert large, accurate models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning mismatched architectures, and addressing data constraints—KD can preserve most teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude improvements in latency, memory footprint, and deployability. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on representations transferred, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy or distributed training. Effective compression therefore treats KD as a core tool within a broader toolkit that includes feature-level alignment, data-aware strategies, online or multi-teacher setups, and data-free techniques when real data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level approach to compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, a consistent empirical picture has emerged: distillation signals that go beyond matching output probabilities—intermediate representation mimicry, attention or relational constraints, and task-aware or architecture-aware objectives—extended with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) yield compact models that often recover most of a teacher’s performance. Success depends strongly on aligning what is distilled with student capacity, ensuring appropriate data (or synthetic surrogates) for transfer, and managing risks such as transferred biases, robustness degradation, and teacher errors. Practical pipelines combine teacher preparation, targeted distillation losses, and deployment-aware choices to produce reliable compressed models, while open problems remain around principled curricula, data-scarce regimes, and theoretical understanding of the transfer mechanisms.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large neural networks so they can run efficiently in production and on resource-constrained devices. Recent work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, and that a range of complementary techniques—data augmentation, multi-teacher schedules, internal representation matching, layer alignment, meta-learning of teachers, and robustness-aware objectives—meaningfully improve student quality or transfer desirable properties. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on optimization, the choice of teacher/student architectures, and the distributional complexity of the training data. I argue that best practice for KD in deep learning and NLP is to treat it as a family of methods to be combined—augmenting data, distilling intermediate representations, leveraging multiple or adaptive teachers, and explicitly distilling robustness—rather than as a single fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Paradigm for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: when treated as a broad training paradigm it enables compact, robust, and deployable models across modalities and tasks. By integrating logit-level guidance, intermediate feature transfer, architecture-aware projectors, adaptive teacher selection, data- and domain-aware strategies, and robustness-aware objectives, KD pipelines can produce students that approach teacher performance while satisfying latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success requires designing what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous components, and how to shape inputs and curricula for the student—rather than relying on a single generic distillation recipe.

papers_seen.author: Blankenship
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for producing compact models from larger teachers across deep learning and natural language processing. Treated as a design‑sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD transfers different kinds of information (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), adapts to constrained data regimes (including data‑free or synthesized data), and composes with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) to produce deployable students. Its empirical success depends on careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity, thoughtful data and training curricula, and explicit evaluation for robustness, rare‑case behavior, and fairness. Persistent failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and sensitivity to distribution shift—mean KD is most reliable when embedded in an integrated compression pipeline and tuned to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: A Central, Practical Tool with Clear Limits and Engineering Requirements
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring information from larger teachers to smaller students. Empirical work across vision, speech, ranking, and natural language tasks shows KD can deliver large reductions in parameter count and latency while retaining much of a teacher’s predictive power. However, KD is not an automatic solution: its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how the teacher is prepared, student architecture and pretraining, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires engineering KD into a broader compression pipeline that addresses data, robustness, fairness, and optimization concerns.

papers_seen.author: Ruiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task-Aware Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical engine for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring information at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving most of the teacher’s predictive performance. However, distillation is design-sensitive: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability or privacy, and how to combine KD with complementary compression primitives determine real-world success. A task-aware workflow that selects distillation signals, adopts appropriate layer-mapping or multi-teacher schedules, and leverages data synthesis or domain adaptation yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Weber
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modality-agnostic strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable toolkit—not a single recipe—KD reliably yields major efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but it must be combined with complementary techniques and data-aware practices to address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and privacy constraints. Effective compression pipelines therefore begin with KD and then incorporate representation alignment, architecture-aware choices, quantization/pruning, and careful evaluation under domain shift and safety requirements.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students so that inference cost, memory, latency, or privacy requirements can be met while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD techniques operate at multiple levels—from softened output distributions to intermediate-feature, attention, and relational matching—and are commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or privacy-preserving protocols). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when design choices (what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the distillation data, and optimization schedules) are made deliberately. However, KD’s effectiveness is conditional: it depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and distribution, and careful handling of robustness, rare or long-tail behaviors, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gross
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under constraints of memory, latency, or privacy. KD operates at multiple levels — softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals — and is routinely combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (use of original, augmented, synthesized, or no data). Empirical work across speech, vision, and language shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when teacher–student alignment, appropriate distillation signals, and suitable training data are carefully chosen. However, KD has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, sensitivity to data heterogeneity) that require engineering choices and sometimes additional methods to obtain robust, fair, and hardware-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Across vision and NLP, KD transfers information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational structure) and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task‑aware data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data‑free methods). Empirical and conceptual work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but its success depends on teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and targeted evaluation of robustness, rare behaviors, and fairness. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, robustness under distribution shift or adversarial influence, privacy-aware distillation, and faithful preservation of long‑tail behaviors; addressing these requires pipeline-oriented distillation design, careful signal selection, and hybrid compression workflows.

papers_seen.author: Bender
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, adaptable approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, multimodal, generative, and federated settings. KD works through multiple channels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals—and is most effective when matched to student capacity, the available data, and deployment constraints. Treated as a core element of a broader compression pipeline (including pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies), KD regularly preserves much of teacher utility while delivering substantial improvements in latency, memory, and deployability. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on careful selection of teacher signals, architecture alignment, handling of limited or private data, and mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, and transfer of teacher biases. Practical deployment therefore requires task-aware distillation recipes, data-aware strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), and complementary compression or federated adaptations to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Meza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) encompasses a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Approaches include matching softened teacher logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, transferring relational structure, and exploiting multi-teacher or online schemes. KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search and can be adapted for low-data or data-free settings. Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines often recover much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures and capacities, how to manage or synthesize data, and how to mitigate robustness and fairness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: What We Know
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware approach for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. Across computer vision, language, generative, and combinatorial domains, KD variants—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and relation-level imitation, layer-wise and progressive schemes, multi-teacher fusion, and data-aware or data-free protocols—enable large reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Practical application typically combines KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and depends critically on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and layers, and how to curate or synthesize distillation data. Important limits remain: optimization gaps from capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases (especially for low-frequency phenomena), domain-shift fragility, and privacy or data-availability constraints. Task-aware design, multi-signal objectives, and targeted interventions for robustness and fairness are central to effective, responsible deployment.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. A broad repertoire of KD techniques transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate-feature or attention matching, and relational or layer-wise alignment, and these techniques are commonly combined with data augmentation, teacher schedules, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and distributional match, and optimization protocols. Best practice treats KD as a flexible toolkit to be adapted to deployment constraints rather than a single fixed recipe; key open challenges include theoretical understanding, robust distillation under data scarcity or privacy constraints, and preserving fairness and rare-behavior fidelity during compression.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and structural signals. A broad suite of distillation techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, relational and channel-wise transfers, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes, and data- or generator-based approaches—enables large reductions in parameter count and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness. Distillation is most effective when combined with task-aware design (student-aware teacher choices, layer alignment or projectors, and data strategies) and complementary compression primitives (architecture search, pruning, quantization). Important limitations include capacity mismatch, optimization instability, propagation of teacher errors or low-frequency behavior loss, and constraints from limited or private data; addressing these requires careful choice of signals, student architectures, and training curricula.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesized Evidence and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. A broad family of KD objectives and protocols—soft-target matching, feature and attention mimicry, relational losses, multi-teacher and online schemes—has been developed and empirically validated across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD is most effective when treated as a system that aligns teacher and student capacity, chooses what signals to transfer, and composes with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or low-precision numerics). Successful deployment depends on data strategies (real-data distillation, augmentation, or synthetic/data-free methods), student initialization or pretraining, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy constraints. Remaining research directions include principled layer mapping for large pre-trained models, reliable distillation without original data, preserving robustness and rare-event behaviors, and theoretical understanding of optimization dynamics under capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring behavioral or representational information from a teacher to a student. Across computer vision and NLP, distillation methods vary from matching output soft targets to aligning internal representations, performing self-distillation, and synthesizing or selecting data when original training examples are unavailable. Empirical work shows distillation can retain much of teacher performance while enabling domain adaptation, improved generalization, and deployment under latency or memory constraints. However, effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, layers, features), the availability and complexity of training data, regularization (e.g., label smoothing and augmentation), and fairness or privacy constraints. Open challenges include understanding when students can outperform teachers, balancing bias mitigation and utility, and combining distillation with pruning or hardware-aware compression for edge deployment.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Hybrid Tool for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple transfer signals and schedules that can recover much of a teacher’s performance when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. However, distillation is not sufficient on its own: combining KD with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), pretraining or adapting the student, and applying data-aware strategies improves robustness, domain transfer, and preservation of rare behaviors. A pragmatic, task-aware pipeline—choosing appropriate signals to transfer, preparing student models, augmenting or synthesizing data, and explicitly evaluating robustness and fairness—yields the most reliable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs for production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task‑Aware Pipeline for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be regarded as the practical core of model compression: a configurable, task-aware pipeline that transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large teachers into compact students. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware surgery), careful teacher–student alignment, and considered data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free), KD produces deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving most task performance. Real-world use requires attention to known failure modes—capacity and optimization mismatches, degraded rare-token or domain-specific behavior, and transfer of biases—and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and privacy. I argue for adopting KD as a flexible design space (signals, data, architecture, and optimization) and for integrating complementary practices to mitigate limits in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware, Conditional Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best framed not as a single trick but as the practical core of modern model-compression pipelines: a flexible set of signals and schedules that, when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, yields deployable students that preserve much of teacher utility. KD delivers strong empirical gains across modalities and tasks but its benefits are conditional on student capacity, data availability, teacher quality, and explicit handling of robustness, privacy, and domain-shift risks. A pragmatic KD-centered workflow emphasizes multiple distilled signals, careful layer/representation mapping, data-aware or data-free strategies when necessary, and integration with pruning/quantization or architecture search to produce reliable, efficient models for production.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context‑Aware Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical mechanism for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is most effective when treated as a configurable core of a broader compression pipeline: choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and which complementary compression primitives to apply all materially affect outcomes. I argue that KD should be the default backbone of model-compression workflows in deep learning and NLP but must be embedded in design‑sensitive, hybrid pipelines that explicitly address capacity mismatch, data availability, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, design-sensitive toolkit for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. It encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, transferring relational structure, and employing multi-teacher, online, or data-synthesizing strategies. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), when distillation signals are chosen to match student capacity and architecture, and when data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic) are used to address domain or privacy constraints. While KD routinely produces strong efficiency–performance trade-offs across modalities, its practical limits—capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, distributional shift, and difficulty preserving rare behaviors and robustness—motivate task-aware pipelines and continued research on reliable data-free and robustness-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Riley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central for deploying high-performing deep models under resource constraints. Methods range from transferring soft-output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mappings, and task- or domain-adaptive compression of large pretrained language models. Advances address practical concerns such as absence of original data, low-precision inference, cross-modal transfer, and faster training-time distillation workflows. Empirical work demonstrates that representation-level supervision and flexible layer alignment often outperform pure logit-based approaches, while theoretical analyses connect KD to regularization schemes like label smoothing and quantify when teacher signals are most beneficial. Remaining challenges include preserving rare-token behaviors, handling domain shift, and balancing privacy, compute, and accuracy in on-device scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Richard
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, using multiple or adaptive teachers, and operating with or without access to original training data. KD is typically integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful data and optimization protocols. Its empirical strengths and practical recipes are well established, but success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, the availability and match of distillation data, and deliberate handling of robustness, rare or long-tail behavior, and potential propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Engine for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a heuristic into a set of principled, modality-agnostic techniques that enable deployment of high-capacity models in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings. By transferring predictive behaviour and internal representations from large teachers to compact students, distillation preserves much of the teacher's utility while enabling large speed, memory, and communication gains. Recent advances show that combining representation-level matching, teacher–student co-design, data-free synthesis, and task-adaptive compression yields robust, practical pipelines for compressing models across vision, language, graph, and federated settings.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal toolkit for transferring the behavior and internal structure of large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a central component of compression pipelines KD routinely yields strong trade-offs between efficiency and performance when combined with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which complementary compression primitives and data strategies to apply. However, KD has systematic limits—capacity mismatch, optimization gaps, teacher error propagation, domain shift, and risks to robustness and fairness—that require targeted remedies and rigorous evaluation. This paper argues KD should be treated as the default first-line strategy for compression in production, but only as part of integrated, task- and data-aware pipelines that explicitly mitigate its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Context-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practically proven approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD encompasses soft-targets, intermediate representation matching, attention- and layer-aware mappings, multi- and online-teacher schemes, and data-aware protocols (including data-free and few-shot variants). KD delivers strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs when paired with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, but its benefits depend on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, adaptable component of compression pipelines while recognizing its limits and prescribing evidence-based design practices for robust, task-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, configurable mechanism for producing compact, deployable deep models. KD provides multi-level transfer signals that, when combined with student-aware architecture design and complementary compression primitives, reliably reduce inference cost while preserving most teacher performance. Effective and responsible compression requires explicit choices about transfer targets, layer alignment, data strategies, and mitigations for capacity mismatch, teacher errors, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. Effective KD requires selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), matching teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. When applied with task-aware objectives, projector or alignment modules, and careful treatment of data and teacher preparation, KD yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though capacity mismatch and data limitations remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. The approach includes aligning soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can operate with original, augmented, or synthesized data. In practice, distillation is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline—combining architecture-aware design, pruning, and quantization—and when distillation objectives are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows substantial reductions in inference cost and memory with modest performance loss, but predictable failure modes remain around capacity mismatch, data scarcity or mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degraded robustness on rare or shifted inputs. Ongoing challenges include principled teacher–student curricula, reliable distillation without original data, and theoretical understanding of why and when different signals transfer successfully.

papers_seen.author: Ruiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task-Aware Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical engine for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring information at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving most of the teacher’s predictive performance. However, distillation is design-sensitive: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability or privacy, and how to combine KD with complementary compression primitives determine real-world success. A task-aware workflow that selects distillation signals, adopts appropriate layer-mapping or multi-teacher schedules, and leverages data synthesis or domain adaptation yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Avila
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default first-line approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students. KD offers a flexible set of mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation transfer, attention/relational objectives, and online/self-distillation—that routinely yield large efficiency gains with modest performance loss. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, data availability and provenance, student capacity and architecture, and explicit measures to preserve robustness, fairness, and privacy. Practical pipelines therefore begin with KD but must plan for complementary architectural adaptation, pruning/quantization, data strategies (filtering, synthesis, or data-free methods), and careful evaluation under domain shift and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher in the form of softened outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has matured into a flexible toolkit that is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows KD can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, but success depends strongly on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data and optimization are handled. Remaining limitations include capacity and optimization mismatches, degradation on low-frequency or domain-specific behaviors, and risk of transferring teacher biases or vulnerabilities.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible, empirically driven set of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. A spectrum of distillation targets—softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals—and variants such as multi-teacher, online, self-distillation, and data-free methods have been developed. Distillation is frequently combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture design) and data strategies (augmented, synthesized, or private data) to produce compact models that often retain much of the teacher’s utility. Practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, choice of distilled signals, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data; remaining challenges include robustness, fairness, domain shift, and principled teacher selection, motivating research on privacy-preserving and federated variants as well as pretraining compact students prior to distillation.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output supervision, intermediate-representation alignment, teacher design, and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: outcomes depend on what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and targeted interventions to address robustness, fairness, and privacy. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as the core of a hybrid, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Tool Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible family of methods that, when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression techniques, enables deployment of compact models with strong utility. KD can transfer final-output behavior, intermediate representations, and structured relationships; it can operate with or without original training data, be adapted for privacy-sensitive or federated settings, and be combined with quantization or pruning to meet hardware constraints. Effective practice requires attention to what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how KD is integrated into the broader compression pipeline to avoid propagation of teacher biases or degradation on rare or shifted data.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. When integrated into a broader compression pipeline and adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints, KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving most of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability and domain match, and careful mitigation of transferred errors or rare-token behaviors. Treating KD as a configurable, multi-ingredient toolbox—combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies—yields the most reliable trade-offs for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Flexible Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a composable toolkit rather than a single recipe: by transferring teacher signals at multiple levels, combining input-side strategies, and integrating complementary compression methods, KD enables compact models that meet practical deployment constraints. Effective distillation requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, and task-aware choices about what to transfer. When deployed with these design principles, KD substantially narrows the performance gap between large teachers and efficient students while remaining adaptable to privacy, federated, and heterogeneous-device settings.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, practical toolkit for converting large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. A diverse set of distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure), combined with data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation), architecture-aware mappings, and staged or multi-teacher schedules, routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has well-documented limits: it can propagate teacher errors or biases, struggle under domain shift or data scarcity, and fail to preserve fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors without targeted interventions. Best practice treats KD as a composable pipeline—integrating representation-level objectives, careful data design, teacher selection, and complementary compression techniques—to achieve robust, task-aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output supervision with representation-level alignment, teacher design, and complementary compression techniques—KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD is not automatic: its success depends on what is distilled, student capacity, data availability, and targeted interventions to address robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Hart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical, but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students. When treated as an integrated pipeline—selecting appropriate distillation signals, preparing teacher and student models, choosing or synthesizing data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks. However, its success is conditional on careful design: student capacity, teacher artifacts, data mismatch, and optimization subtleties can limit gains unless explicitly mitigated. This paper argues KD should be the practical centerpiece of compression workflows while highlighting limits and concrete design principles for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple transfer mechanisms (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals) and is most effective when integrated into a larger compression pipeline that includes data strategies, student-aware architecture choices, and complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization. Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance, but predictable limits (student capacity mismatch, data or privacy constraints, teacher errors and biases, and domain-shift fragility) require careful engineering and evaluation for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Jennings
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be the default first‑line strategy for compressing large deep learning and NLP models because it provides a flexible, multi-signal toolkit that routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs. However, KD is not an automatic solution: its practical success depends on integrated, task- and data-aware pipelines that combine student-aware architecture design, complementary compression primitives, and explicit mitigations for capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, domain shift, and safety or privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students to meet deployment constraints. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, appropriate data strategies, and careful teacher–student design. While KD frequently yields compact models that retain most teacher performance and can improve robustness or enable low-precision inference, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data—making KD a powerful but context-sensitive tool rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile mechanism for transferring behavior from larger teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints in deep learning and NLP. KD provides multiple signals—softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure—and when combined with complementary compression primitives and task-aware data strategies it often yields deployable students that preserve much of teacher performance. However, KD has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy limits, and robustness or long-tail degradation) that require targeted adjunct techniques and careful evaluation. I argue that KD should be the central element of compression pipelines but must be integrated with architecture-aware design, data protocols, and robustness checks to be reliable in practice.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Adaptive Tool for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. KD's successes across vision, speech, and NLP show that careful choice of what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention), how to align teacher and student, and whether to rely on original data or generated/synthetic data determines outcomes. To be effective in real deployments, KD must be combined with complementary methods (data-free generation, federated protocols, targeted augmentation, and robustness-aware objectives) and applied adaptively to task and resource constraints. When used thoughtfully, KD enables substantial efficiency gains without wholesale architectural redesign; when used naively it can propagate teacher errors or exacerbate distributional and low-frequency lexical problems.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, high-leverage approach to compress large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied as the central element within a task-aware compression pipeline—tuned for student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints—KD routinely yields compact models that recover much of a teacher's performance. However, KD is not a universal recipe: predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, data scarcity or mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degraded rare-case or robustness behavior) require complementary techniques and explicit pipeline-level mitigations to produce reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a flexible paradigm that improves efficiency, robustness, privacy, and generalization across modalities and tasks. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight deployable models, transfer internal representations to preserve teacher behaviors, operate without original training data, and be adapted to distributed and privacy-sensitive settings. Recent methodological advances—layer- and attention-aware projection, multi-teacher schedules, meta-learned teachers, and techniques connecting KD to regularization—make distillation a practical and theoretically grounded tool for both research and production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Richardson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, multi-signal approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a flexible toolbox, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and can operate with original, augmented, synthesized, or data-free inputs. Empirical and methodological work shows KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs when paired with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware student preparation. Responsible deployment requires explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and scarcity, and robustness and fairness evaluation, so KD should be treated as the central element of a broader, design-sensitive compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Mata
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A mature toolkit now includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer-wise or relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-side strategies including data-free or synthetic-sample protocols. Best-practice compression pipelines treat distillation as a core component combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and with careful attention to teacher–student alignment, data provenance, privacy, robustness, and capacity constraints. While distillation frequently yields large practical gains in latency and memory with modest task-costs, open problems remain around principled teacher selection, distillation without access to original data, preserving robustness and fairness, and bridging optimization/capacity gaps between teachers and students.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.
