papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD can transfer information at multiple levels—from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure—and when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and task-aware data strategies, it routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on choices about distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagated teacher errors, and domain shift. A principled, pipeline-oriented use of KD—combining representation-level objectives, careful data protocols, and auxiliary compression methods—gives the most reliable path to deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Design‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical family of techniques that transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to achieve deployable efficiency gains. KD operates through multiple signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational maps) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (original, augmented, synthesized, or data‑free). Empirical and theoretical work show KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance under careful teacher–student design, but important limitations remain: capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, domain shift, and privacy/heterogeneity constraints. A design‑sensitive pipeline — choosing what and how to transfer, matching student capacity and architecture, mixing soft and hard targets when appropriate, and combining KD with other compression methods and data protocols — yields the most reliable and deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Incomplete Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a reliable, production-ready method for converting large neural models into smaller, deployable students, but it is not a standalone solution. KD excels at transferring predictive behavior and internal representations across modalities and supports many procedural variants; however, real-world deployment requires integrating KD with architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, data strategies (including synthesis or data-free methods), and targeted evaluation for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Treating KD as the core of an integrated compression pipeline — and designing safeguards for its known failure modes — yields the best balance of efficiency and retained performance.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central engineering paradigm for converting large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft‑target matching into a multifaceted toolkit that transfers logits, intermediate features, relational statistics, and training dynamics, and that can operate in standard, online, federated, or data‑free regimes. When combined with architecture‑aware design, pretraining, and complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization), KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss. However, its success depends on careful task‑aware choices: what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to mitigate capacity mismatch, teacher artifacts, and rare‑case degradation. This synthesis summarizes core methods, practical tradeoffs, known failure modes, and recommended pipeline elements for reliable KD in vision and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task‑Aware Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be the default, central tool in practical model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP because it provides flexible, information-rich signals that compact students can use to approximate large teachers. KD is most effective when treated as a modular, task-aware process—choosing what signals to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure), how to align teacher and student, and how to supply or synthesize distillation data—and when it is combined with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, distribution shift, and the risk of propagated teacher artifacts require deliberate design choices, monitoring, and sometimes alternative or additional compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single recipe for copying teacher logits into a central, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and behaviors of larger teachers. KD methods vary in what they transfer (soft labels, intermediate features, relational structure), how they handle data availability (data-rich, data-free, federated), and how they combine with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical deployments select and tune KD components to match modality, data-privacy constraints, and latency or memory budgets.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default starting point for compressing large deep and NLP models because it offers flexible, information-rich signals that compact students can use to approximate larger teachers. KD is most effective when implemented as a pipeline: choose what to transfer (soft targets, intermediate representations, relations), align teacher and student architectures, address data availability or privacy constraints, and combine distillation with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). However, KD is not a panacea; capacity mismatch, data scarcity, teacher imperfections, and robustness or fairness concerns require deliberate, task-aware remedies and monitoring.

papers_seen.author: Browning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, Practical Guidance, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student across multiple signal levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure). Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching into a flexible, task-aware toolkit that is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design), careful teacher–student alignment, and data strategies adapted to deployment constraints. Empirical and practical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but remaining limits include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, degraded rare-token or out-of-distribution behavior, and challenges in data-free or privacy-constrained regimes.

papers_seen.author: Barrett
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Modern KD spans softened-output (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and ensemble supervision, online/co-distillation, and data-aware protocols including data-free and federated variants. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require careful teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile, practically oriented set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure, and is most effective when combined with complementary practices such as pre-training compact students, careful selection or synthesis of distillation data, teacher scheduling, and architecture-aware alignment. Empirical work shows KD routinely enables meaningful latency and memory reductions with modest accuracy loss, but success depends on principled design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; these considerations motivate task-aware pipelines and ongoing research into robustness, fairness, privacy, and theoretical underpinnings.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression: A Conditional, Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible, modality-agnostic approach to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as the default starting point for compression, KD provides multiple complementary signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) that—when matched to student capacity and combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—produce strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, KD is not universally sufficient: practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, data availability and provenance, domain shift, teacher errors, and robustness/fairness constraints. A pragmatic compression pipeline therefore places KD at its center but integrates pretraining, architecture adaptation, data-aware distillation schedules, and explicit evaluation and mitigation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Practical Prescriptions for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment. While KD reliably reduces model size and inference cost, its effectiveness depends critically on choices around teacher design, the training signal (soft labels vs. representations), the data used for distillation, and additional constraints such as fairness and privacy. To realize reliable, high-quality compressed models in NLP and related domains, practitioners should treat KD as a system composed of complementary ingredients—data augmentation, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, representation-level objectives, and interventions for bias and privacy—rather than a single off-the-shelf loss.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Paradigm for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated not as a narrow compression trick but as a unifying, practical paradigm for producing compact, deployable models while preserving accuracy, robustness, and task-specific behavior. KD’s range—spanning soft-target supervision, intermediate representation matching, multi-teacher schedules, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and adversarial or curriculum-enhanced transfers—makes it uniquely suited to combine with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet real-world constraints. At the same time, KD requires careful design to handle teacher-student mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, and data-availability or privacy limits; following representation-aware objectives, adaptive teacher strategies, and hybrid compression pipelines yields the most reliable results.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Treat Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Compression — but Build a Task‑Aware Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high‑value approach for turning large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure using multiple signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) and often composes with pruning, quantization, or architecture changes. However, KD alone cannot guarantee preservation of rare behaviors, robustness under domain shift, or elimination of teacher biases; practical compression succeeds when distillation is the default first step within a carefully designed, task‑aware pipeline that includes projector design, data strategies, capacity alignment, and complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Practical Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a modular system — combining softened-output matching, intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), and complementary compression primitives such as pruning or quantization — KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. Success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, addressing data-availability constraints, and mitigating risks from imperfect teachers, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift. I argue KD should be the default component of production compression pipelines provided practitioners adopt task-aware recipes, incorporate data-aware and architecture-aware remedies, and monitor robustness and fairness outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple mechanisms (output matching, representation mimicry, and relational objectives), and when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, and teacher adaptation) it enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD is therefore best treated as a composable toolkit: powerful in practice but requiring careful choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or sensitive data.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware, Pipeline-Centric Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core of model compression for deep learning and NLP when it is implemented as an integrated, task-aware pipeline. KD’s flexibility — transferring logits, intermediate representations, or relational structure — makes it the natural default for producing deployable students under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its empirical strengths are greatest when combined with architecture-aware student design, many-to-many layer alignment, data strategies (including synthesis or data-free protocols when data are unavailable), and complementary compression (pruning, quantization). At the same time, KD is not a universal remedy: student capacity, teacher quality, data provenance, distribution shift, and safety or robustness concerns impose predictable limits that require engineering mitigations. This position recommends treating KD as the central, configurable engine of compression while explicitly designing pipelines to address these failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically proven approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. KD can operate at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure) and be combined with complementary compression techniques, data synthesis, or student-aware teacher training to meet deployment constraints in vision, language, and graph domains. However, its success depends on careful design choices — what to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, how to handle limited or private data, and whether to adapt the teacher — and practitioners should treat KD as part of a broader compression toolkit rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Estrada
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central but Insufficient — A Practical Position for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, high‑leverage approach for producing compact, deployable deep and NLP models. KD reliably reduces parameter count and latency by transferring teacher behavior to students, but its real-world effectiveness depends on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to prepare teachers and students, how to handle distillation data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be treated as the core of an integrated compression pipeline rather than an off‑the‑shelf recipe, with specific engineering practices to manage capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, data limitations, and distributional robustness.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for compressing large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students. Empirical practice treats KD as a configurable pipeline: choosing which teacher signals to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational structure), aligning teacher and student architectures and capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques and data strategies. KD reliably reduces memory and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance across modalities, but predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, optimization gaps, propagation of teacher errors and biases, domain shift, and degraded long-tail behavior—require careful design choices, complementary methods, and targeted evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. A spectrum of techniques — matching softened outputs, aligning features or attention, layer-mapping (including many-to-many mappings), multi-teacher or ensemble transfers, and data-free or generator-based synthesis — enables large reductions in size and latency while largely preserving task performance. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and training choices; but it faces practical challenges including capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and the potential transfer of teacher biases or adversarial vulnerabilities.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Necessary Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal structure via soft targets, intermediate-feature alignment, attention maps, and relational objectives. When integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful data and architecture design, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance and enable latency-, memory-, or privacy-constrained deployment. However, KD’s benefits are contingent on student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher artifacts, and distributional shift; addressing these requires deliberate, task-aware pipelines and evaluation tailored to real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Work across NLP and broader deep learning has developed multiple KD paradigms—soft-label (logit) matching, intermediate-representation matching, layer-to-layer and many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher aggregation, and data-free distillation—and combined KD with other compression methods such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. Empirical results show that well-designed distillation can yield compact models that approach the accuracy of large pre-trained models while offering substantial savings in parameters, latency, and computational cost. Remaining challenges include aligning heterogeneous teacher and student architectures, coping with limited or unavailable training data, and selecting or weighting multiple teachers per example. The literature suggests principled strategies—attention-based layer fusion, representation-level losses, teacher confidence or dynamic weighting, and synthetic-data generation—that mitigate these issues and enable effective deployment of compressed models in domain-specific and resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Design‑Sensitive Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile method for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD works across multiple signal types (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and data regimes, and routinely delivers substantial reductions in inference cost when its objectives, student design, and data strategies are matched to deployment constraints. At the same time, KD is conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and distributional mismatch impose predictable limits and require complementary techniques and careful evaluation to ensure robustness, fairness, and preservation of rare-event behavior.

papers_seen.author: Mcguire
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Across vision, language, retrieval, and graph domains, KD is a flexible toolkit that—when combined with data strategies and complementary compression techniques—enables substantial reductions in parameters, latency, and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical application requires careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of transferred errors or privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Moss
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical pathway to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable, task-aware toolkit—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, and pairing distillation with complementary methods and data strategies—KD routinely yields large efficiency gains while preserving most task performance. However, reliable deployment requires explicit handling of predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, data- and domain-mismatch, robustness and fairness regressions) and adoption of remedies such as student pretraining, architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, synthetic-data strategies, and careful evaluation. KD should therefore be the default component of compression pipelines, but only as part of integrated, task- and data-aware processes that mitigate its limits.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into compact, deployable students. KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure—and interoperates with complementary compression methods (pre-training of small models, architecture adaptation, pruning, and quantization). Practical deployment of KD requires matching the distillation signals and data strategy to student capacity and constraints (latency, memory, privacy, or heterogeneous architectures), deliberate handling of domain shift and low-frequency behaviors, and attention to teacher calibration or co-design. When these elements are chosen and tuned for the application, KD yields compact models that retain much of the teacher’s effectiveness while meeting real-world resource and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Griffith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As practiced across vision, speech, and NLP, KD extends beyond simple soft-target matching to include intermediate-representation and attention transfer, multi- and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware variants (including data-free or synthetic-data methods). KD typically forms the first-line component of broader compression pipelines that combine architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies; its empirical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and provenance, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and privacy. Practical deployment therefore treats KD as a central but conditional engine whose recipes must be adapted to the target task, data regime, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a versatile set of methods for producing compact, efficient models from large teachers. Techniques range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and are frequently combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. KD is applied across modalities and tasks—enabling on-device inference, domain specialization, privacy-aware releases, and adaptation under limited data—yet its effectiveness depends on choices about what teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and optimization challenges. Open problems include robustness and fairness transfer, capacity mismatch, data-free distillation, and reliably preserving low-frequency or out-of-domain behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Pollard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller, faster students and has become a practical foundation for model compression across vision and NLP. KD methods span softened-output matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-centric strategies including augmentation and synthesis. While KD often yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss, its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data, robustness, and privacy constraints. Combined pipelines that integrate KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design deliver the best deployment outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Richard

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, using multiple or adaptive teachers, and operating with or without access to original training data. KD is typically integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful data and optimization protocols. Its empirical strengths and practical recipes are well established, but success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, the availability and match of distillation data, and deliberate handling of robustness, rare or long-tail behavior, and potential propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single heuristic into a flexible, multi-signal engineering toolkit central to practical model compression. Success in practice depends on student capacity, teacher quality, availability and selection of distillation data, and careful alignment of objectives and architectures; important open problems remain in data-free distillation, robustness under distribution shift, avoiding propagation of teacher biases and rare-case failures, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression methods form a diverse toolkit for producing smaller, faster, or more deployable models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. Research spans soft-label and self-distillation strategies, layer- and representation-level transfers, architecture-aware and task-adaptive compression, and deployment-aware approaches that combine pruning, quantization, and distillation. Empirical work shows that careful choice of distillation signal (logits, intermediate representations, or feature maps), alignment strategy between teacher and student layers, data augmentation, and optimization scheduling materially affects student performance. Practical systems exploit these design choices to compress large pre-trained language models, accelerate inference, enable heterogeneous-device training, or improve low-precision networks. Despite progress, open questions remain about principled objective design, sample efficiency under limited data, and theory connecting transferred representations to generalization.

papers_seen.author: Bell

Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing parameters and latency, but effectiveness depends on choices of knowledge to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Remaining challenges include robustness under domain shift, fairness and bias transfer, privacy in distributed settings, and limits to compression for some generative tasks.

Real-world deployment requires principled pipelines that match distillation objectives to student constraints and that combine KD with other compression and data methods.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from one or more high-capacity teachers to smaller student models. Methods range from matching teacher soft-labels to aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and synthesizing surrogate data when original training sets are unavailable. Distillation is applied across modalities (language, vision, speech, graphs) and commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map layers, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate capacity and optimization mismatches. Recent work emphasizes task-aware layer selection, data-centric augmentation or synthesis, and integrating distillation into multi-stage or multi-teacher workflows to produce compact, robust models suitable for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Outcomes, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. A broad toolkit has emerged—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer- and relation-aware objectives, multi- or self-distillation schedules, and data strategies that range from using original training data to synthetic or data-free generation. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, architecture, and deployment constraints. Empirically, well-designed distillation pipelines recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but common failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, sensitivity to data mismatch or scarcity, and degraded robustness under distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression and Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a core engineering technique that enables deployment, adaptation, privacy, and robustness for large neural models in real-world systems. By treating distillation as a family of methods—ranging from output soft-target transfer to feature- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and privacy-aware protocols—practitioners can compress models while preserving task performance and satisfying latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. Thoughtful application of KD, combined with complementary methods (pretraining, projector design, multi-stage schedules, and careful handling of teacher imperfections), yields compact models that are practical for production while exposing clear avenues for further research.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Malone
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, and relational structure. When treated as a configurable toolkit and combined with complementary compression primitives and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance across modalities. Nevertheless, KD has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, internal representation misalignment, data limitations, and the potential propagation of teacher weaknesses—so successful deployment requires task‑aware design, alignment between teacher and student, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, general-purpose approach for translating large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Across architectures, modalities, and deployment constraints, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the teacher's performance; however, realizing those gains in practice requires matching the distillation formulation to data availability, model mismatch, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central-but-Insufficient Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, practical way to convert large teacher models into smaller students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is best treated as the core of a compression pipeline rather than a standalone recipe: its multiple transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) and flexible deployments (multi‑teacher, online, data‑free, federated) enable broad applicability, but predictable failure modes—student capacity limits, domain and data mismatch, transferred biases, and robustness degradation—require complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), data strategies, and teacher–student co‑design. For reliable production use, practitioners should adopt multi‑signal distillation, integrate compression primitives, and evaluate robustness and fairness across domains.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment. Beyond the classic teacher-logit supervision, modern distillation covers feature-level matching, task-adaptive architecture search, multi-teacher transfer, and data-free scenarios. KD can be combined with pruning and structured sparsity, adapted for domain shifts, and used to transfer ensemble or task-specific knowledge into compact models. The choice of distillation target, the availability of data, and the deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy, domain) determine which distillation recipe will be most effective.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing but large neural models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. Research has developed a spectrum of approaches — from matching logits to feature-level imitation, structural transformation of architectures, multi-teacher schemes, and task-specific adaptations — and has applied them across domains including detection, generative modeling, recommendation, retrieval, and multiple NLP tasks. Empirical work highlights both opportunities (substantial parameter reductions, faster inference, retained or modestly degraded accuracy) and pitfalls (propagation of teacher errors, sensitivity to data heterogeneity, robustness concerns), motivating targeted algorithmic adjustments such as selective distillation, projector modules, and adversarially-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Stephenson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design‑Sensitive Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, first‑line approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students when it is applied as a design‑sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe. A mature distillation workflow selects which teacher signals to transfer, aligns teacher and student architectures, leverages student pre‑training, and combines distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. When these design decisions are made systematically—accounting for capacity mismatch, data availability, and robustness/fairness constraints—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting real deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical, but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students. When treated as an integrated pipeline—selecting appropriate distillation signals, preparing teacher and student models, choosing or synthesizing data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks. However, its success is conditional on careful design: student capacity, teacher artifacts, data mismatch, and optimization subtleties can limit gains unless explicitly mitigated. This paper argues KD should be the practical centerpiece of compression workflows while highlighting limits and concrete design principles for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller students to meet deployment constraints. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, appropriate data strategies, and careful teacher–student design. While KD frequently yields compact models that retain most teacher performance and can improve robustness or enable low-precision inference, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data—making KD a powerful but context-sensitive tool rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Research has extended KD from simple soft-target matching to a toolbox of representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schedules, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture design. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance in practice, but success depends on choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, data availability, and optimization; open problems include principled teacher selection, handling limited or no data, robustness to teacher errors, and aligning compression with hardware and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Starting Point for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When used as the default first step in compression workflows and combined with task-aware signal selection, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives, KD often delivers strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs. However, its effectiveness is bounded by student capacity, data availability, and risks of transferring teacher artifacts; successful practice requires explicit mitigation strategies and integration with other compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Limits, and a Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with task-aware choices about what to transfer, pretraining of compact architectures, representation-level supervision, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has important failure modes — capacity mismatch, data and domain heterogeneity, and propagation of teacher biases — that must be addressed through careful teacher selection, data strategies, and evaluation. A pragmatic pipeline that pretrains students, distills both outputs and intermediate representations, and selectively composes KD with other compression steps yields robust trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy in practice.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods have become central tools for deploying large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Work in this area spans techniques that transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, approaches that operate without access to original training data, methods that preserve privacy or reduce communication in distributed settings, and specialized strategies for large pre-trained language and vision transformer models. Key themes include layer- and module-level mappings between teacher and student, task-aware selection of distilled signals, adversarial and generative approaches to synthesize training inputs, and the combination of pruning or architecture search with distillation. Practical trade-offs arise between fidelity to teacher behavior, student capacity, data availability, and robustness to distribution shifts or adversarial attacks. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous modalities and architectures, selecting what information to transfer for a given downstream task, and ensuring privacy and robustness while maintaining high compression ratios.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods form a flexible toolkit to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, and generative settings, practitioners use softened outputs, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher schedules, online co-distillation, and data-aware or data-free procedures. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data availability or privacy constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include capacity and optimization gaps, propagation of teacher errors or biases, robustness under adversarial or domain shift, and principled teacher selection. This synthesis summarizes common methods, empirical findings, practical tradeoffs, and recommended design patterns for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Conditional
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational signals) and is most effective when integrated with complementary practices such as pre-training, architecture-aware design, data-side strategies, and other compression techniques. However, its success is conditional on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or mismatched data, and how to mitigate propagation of teacher errors or biases. Treating KD as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe yields the best results for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level approach to compressing large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, a consistent empirical picture has emerged: distillation signals that go beyond matching output probabilities—intermediate representation mimicry, attention or relational constraints, and task-aware or architecture-aware objectives—extended with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) yield compact models that often recover most of a teacher’s performance. Success depends strongly on aligning what is distilled with student capacity, ensuring appropriate data (or synthetic surrogates) for transfer, and managing risks such as transferred biases, robustness degradation, and teacher errors. Practical pipelines combine teacher preparation, targeted distillation losses, and deployment-aware choices to produce reliable compressed models, while open problems remain around principled curricula, data-scarce regimes, and theoretical understanding of the transfer mechanisms.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened teacher outputs into a broad toolkit that includes logits transfer, intermediate-representation imitation, relational and attention-level losses, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data-side strategies ranging from original-data augmentation to synthetic or data-free approaches. In practice KD is most effective when matched to student capacity, combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and guided by task- and data-aware engineering. Remaining challenges include principled layer and signal alignment, reliable distillation without original data, and preserving robustness, long-tail and safety-critical behaviors under compression.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. The approach spans matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, relational and ensemble supervision, and a range of data strategies including augmentation and data‑free synthesis. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and requires careful teacher–student capacity alignment, layer mapping, and data consideration to preserve accuracy, robustness, and domain suitability. Persistent challenges include distillation without original data, robustness under distribution shift or adversarial attack, automated architecture-agnostic distillation, and avoiding transfer of teacher biases or long-tail failures.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring aspects of the teacher’s predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of methods—matching output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and data-free schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, data availability, privacy, and multimodal inputs. Empirical work shows that when the distillation recipe is matched to model architectures, data conditions, and deployment constraints, students can retain much of the teacher’s performance while offering practical efficiency gains; however, trade-offs and open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and faithful transfer of rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques form a flexible toolkit for turning large, accurate deep models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners transfer information at output (soft targets), intermediate representations (features or attention maps), or relational/ensemble signals and often combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and architecture-aware design. Success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, handling data availability (including data-free or synthesized inputs), and addressing risks such as propagation of teacher errors, fairness and robustness degradation, and performance loss on rare or distribution-shifted phenomena. Across vision and language, careful combinations of distillation objectives, student pretraining or co-design, and complementary compression techniques enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while retaining much of teacher performance.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. Effective KD requires selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), matching teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. When applied with task-aware objectives, projector or alignment modules, and careful treatment of data and teacher preparation, KD yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though capacity mismatch and data limitations remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) turns large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Practitioners combine multiple KD signals with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (use of original data, augmentation or synthesis, and data-free approaches) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Distillation often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity and appropriate data choices are made, but important challenges remain: capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, preserving rare/long-tail behaviors, robustness under domain shift, and operating with limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted training paradigm that enables compact, deployable models by transferring aspects of teacher models to smaller students. When treated as a central tool rather than a single recipe, KD supports a range of targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), deployment modalities (on-device, federated, data-limited), and complementary compressions (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to adapt data and curricula; with these considerations KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though optimization subtleties and robustness remain important caveats.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Backbone of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible, and empirically effective family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and deployment constraints, KD enables moving from research-stage, high-capacity architectures to resource-efficient models suitable for latency- and privacy-constrained production. Realizing KD's full potential requires attention to teacher quality, data and domain mismatches, and scalability; appropriate choices—representation-level objectives, multi-teacher signals, online protocols, and privacy-aware distillation—address these challenges and make KD a core tool for applied deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core—and Bounded—Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture search)—KD routinely enables deployment in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. However, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, available data, and evaluation of robustness and fairness; thus KD should be treated as a central element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Limited Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach that enables deploying large models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints by transferring knowledge from teacher to student models. KD extends beyond simple logit matching to include representation-level transfer, attention- and feature-guided objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search and pretraining. While KD reliably improves efficiency and can preserve many teacher behaviors, its success depends on choices of distillation targets, teacher preparation, student architecture, and data strategies; it can also amplify teacher errors or struggle under data heterogeneity, requiring complementary techniques and careful engineering for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Pollard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller, faster students and has become a practical foundation for model compression across vision and NLP. KD methods span softened-output matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-centric strategies including augmentation and synthesis. While KD often yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss, its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data, robustness, and privacy constraints. Combined pipelines that integrate KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design deliver the best deployment outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Ortega
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable method for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a task-aware, design-sensitive core of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and appropriate data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free approaches), KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs. However, its practical success depends on explicit choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to evaluate robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors. I argue that KD should be the default central mechanism in compression workflows, but always embedded within a hybrid, validated engineering pipeline that mitigates known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Washington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood and used not as a single recipe but as a flexible, multi-component toolkit for producing compact models that meet real-world deployment constraints. When designers choose what signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), align teacher and student architectures thoughtfully, and combine distillation with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, KD reliably produces students that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory use, and deployment complexity. Practical success requires attention to capacity mismatch, task-specific selection of signals, and safeguards for robustness and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Conditional Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods — from soft-target logit matching to feature- and relation-level transfer, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free or synthetic-data protocols — have repeatedly enabled substantial reductions in parameter count and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: predictable failure modes (student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy limits, and transfer of teacher errors or biases) mean KD must be engineered as part of an integrated compression pipeline that selects appropriate distillation signals, aligns architectures, adopts data strategies, and pairs KD with complementary compression primitives and rigorous deployment evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Practical Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a modular system — combining softened-output matching, intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), and complementary compression primitives such as pruning or quantization — KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. Success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, addressing data-availability constraints, and mitigating risks from imperfect teachers, capacity mismatch, and distribution shift. I argue KD should be the default component of production compression pipelines provided practitioners adopt task-aware recipes, incorporate data-aware and architecture-aware remedies, and monitor robustness and fairness outcomes.
