papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of techniques for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD variants include soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and attention-level mimicry, relational objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches. Empirical work across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing memory, latency, and inference cost. Effective deployment requires matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data availability or privacy constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression methods. Open challenges include robustness under distribution shift, propagation of teacher errors and biases, principled teacher selection, and reliable performance on low-frequency or rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. It is a practical toolkit used to reduce memory, compute, and latency for deployment, to enable low-precision inference, to adapt models across domains, and to support privacy-aware or federated settings. Empirical work across vision, speech, graphs, and language tasks shows that careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers are configured, and how training is regularized materially affect the trade-offs between efficiency and task performance.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring information from a teacher. Research over the past decade has explored a spectrum of KD variants — from soft-label logits transfer to feature-map matching, adversarial and online schemes, few-shot and privacy-preserving compression, and theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps. Empirical work shows KD improves deployment practicality across vision, speech, NLP, graph, and generative models, while recent studies examine robustness, data-efficiency, the role of pre-training, and the impact of teacher quality. Important open directions include principled methods for sample selection, cross-domain transfer, formal guarantees under limited data or adversaries, and integrating KD with compression primitives such as pruning and structured sparsity.

papers_seen.author: Li
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of task performance. A coherent body of work frames KD as a toolkit: matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention/relational structure, ensembling or multi-teacher transfers, and operating across data regimes from plentiful labeled data to fully data-free or privacy-constrained settings. KD is often composed with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation; real-world success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, managing data mismatch or scarcity, and explicitly validating robustness, calibration, and long-tail behavior. Remaining challenges include principled teacher–student alignment for heterogeneous architectures, reliable distillation without original data, and preserving fairness and rare-event behavior under compression.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring information from one or more high-capacity teachers to a smaller student model. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to rich objectives that align intermediate representations, exploit multiple teachers, search for task-specific student architectures, and generate or synthesize data when original training sets are unavailable. Distillation is applied across modalities (language, speech, vision, graphs) and combined with other compression techniques to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and recurring challenges — data availability, teacher–student heterogeneity, preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors, and principled objective design — and suggests strategies to mitigate them in deployed systems.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Across vision and NLP, effective distillation combines choices about what to transfer (soft outputs, features, relational signals), how teachers are designed or ensembled, and what data or surrogates are used. Practical pipelines increasingly pair distillation with architecture search, curriculum strategies, and distributed training to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often recovers much of a teacher's performance, success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data complexity, and optimization procedures; open problems include principled handling of imperfect teachers, robustness and fairness under compression, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Gutierrez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Integrations, and Conditional Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, deployment-oriented approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students. Treated as an integrated pipeline—choosing distilled signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, preparing or synthesizing data, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across tasks and modalities. However, its reliability depends on deliberate design choices: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and distribution, and optimization details must be addressed to avoid failure modes. I argue that KD should be treated as the practical centerpiece of compression workflows while being applied with explicit mitigations for its known conditional limits.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods have become central tools for deploying large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Work in this area spans techniques that transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, approaches that operate without access to original training data, methods that preserve privacy or reduce communication in distributed settings, and specialized strategies for large pre-trained language and vision transformer models. Key themes include layer- and module-level mappings between teacher and student, task-aware selection of distilled signals, adversarial and generative approaches to synthesize training inputs, and the combination of pruning or architecture search with distillation. Practical trade-offs arise between fidelity to teacher behavior, student capacity, data availability, and robustness to distribution shifts or adversarial attacks. Ongoing challenges include aligning heterogeneous modalities and architectures, selecting what information to transfer for a given downstream task, and ensuring privacy and robustness while maintaining high compression ratios.

papers_seen.author: Strong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware, Integrated Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile method for producing compact, deployable deep models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD succeeds when treated as an integrated, task-aware pipeline: select what to transfer (outputs, intermediate features, or relational structure) according to student capacity and task needs; combine KD with complementary compression primitives such as quantization, pruning, or architecture search; and address data availability, teacher imperfections, and deployment constraints (latency, privacy, fairness) through multi-signal distillation, data strategies, and careful evaluation. When applied in this way, KD should be the default compression engine for deep learning and NLP systems, while practitioners remain vigilant about its known failure modes and validate distilled models across distributions and metrics beyond accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching softened logits to a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Modern distillation transfers output behavior, intermediate representations, relational structure, or ensemble knowledge; can operate with limited or no access to original training data; and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. Practical application requires matching the distillation recipe to task requirements, student capacity, and data availability while managing teacher imperfections and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Modular Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default first-line approach for compressing large deep and NLP models because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and rich internal structure into compact students while remaining flexible to deployment constraints. As a modular pipeline, KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), data strategies (original, augmented, or synthesized), and integration with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture surgery). However, KD is not a universal cure: careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness are required to produce deployable, reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Techniques range from matching output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, feature maps, or distilled data. Applications span model compression for deployment (including transformer compression for NLP), multimodal model adaptation, federated and resource-constrained learning, and improving robustness or fairness. Practical strategies include layer-wise or attention-based projection, progressive module replacement, adversarial and data-free distillation, and task-specific adaptations that account for data heterogeneity and inductive bias.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practical Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of training techniques that transfer information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving predictive performance. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, transferring relational structure among examples or channels, multi- and self-distillation, and data-aware protocols including data-free and domain-adaptive approaches. Its practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and task constraints, handling data availability and privacy, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques. While KD often yields deployable students that retain much of teacher utility, important limitations remain around domain shift, capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, and robustness to rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Methods range from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Empirical results show distilled students often recover much of a teacher’s performance when distillation signals, student capacity, and data strategies are chosen deliberately, but outcomes depend on addressing capacity mismatch, data or privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework for shrinking large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure from teachers to students, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while retaining much of the original performance. Its effectiveness depends on aligning distillation signals to student capacity, handling data availability and privacy, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires explicit attention to known failure modes—capacity mismatch, domain shift, and propagation of teacher errors—and evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-token behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques include matching teacher output distributions, transferring intermediate representations or relational structure, and ensembling or online schemes. In practice KD is combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, and can serve beyond compression as an implicit regularizer, an enabler of domain adaptation, and a mechanism for privacy-aware release. Effectiveness depends on choices about teacher quality and design, student capacity and architecture mapping, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and targeted interventions to preserve robustness and mitigate undesirable transferred behaviors. A task- and deployment-aware KD pipeline that selects what and how to transfer—sometimes staged or hybridized with complementary compression primitives—yields the most reliable real-world outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations. Across modalities and tasks, distillation methods vary by what is transferred (logits/soft labels, intermediate features, attention, or structural knowledge), by whether they rely on original training data, and by how the teacher-student relationship is optimized. Practical goals include reducing inference cost, preserving accuracy under domain shift, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, and improving robustness or fairness. Empirical work shows that carefully chosen transfer targets, training curricula, and data strategies can recover much of the teacher performance in compact models, and that meta-level and task-adaptive approaches further improve transfer effectiveness. Key open concerns are how to best align heterogeneous inputs or architectures, how to retain desirable inductive biases (e.g., for domain-specific tasks), and how to ensure reliable student performance without access to teacher training data.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing appropriate distillation targets, preparing the student (often via pre-training), and addressing data, privacy, and robustness constraints—KD yields compact models that retain a substantial fraction of teacher performance across vision, speech, and language tasks. However, its success depends on design choices (what to distill and when), data availability, and mitigation of teacher errors; thus KD is best treated as a system of complementary techniques rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Trade-offs, and Task‑Aware Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Practically, distillation is a multi-signal toolkit—matching soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations or attention, and aligning relational or layer-wise structure—and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free distillation). Success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data provenance, and task constraints; careful engineering choices and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-behavior retention are essential for production-ready deployment.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, composable toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD methods transfer predictive behavior and internal structure using a range of signals and procedural variants. Well-designed distillation pipelines combine soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation alignment, and data strategies with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest task degradation when teacher–student capacity, data availability, and task structure are explicitly considered; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, data-free distillation, and preserving fairness and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Practices, Limits, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure so students can meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical KD combines choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention, relations), how to align teachers and students (layer mapping, pre-training, progressive replacement), and how to handle data (real, synthesized, or privacy-preserving) to retain much of teacher utility. While KD often yields substantial compression with modest performance loss, it faces predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, domain or data-shift, and propagation of teacher errors—so it is typically used together with complementary compression tools and careful data and training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Harper
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Design-Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When used as the central element of a deliberate compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely recovers a large portion of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Its effectiveness is conditional: success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and explicitly addressing robustness, long-tail behaviors, and the risk of propagated teacher errors or biases. Practical adoption therefore treats KD as the default compression engine but applies it as a configurable, task-aware process rather than a one-size-fits-all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD has matured beyond simple output-matching into a family of methods that transfer intermediate representations, attention or channel-wise signals, and task-specific inductive biases; it can operate under data scarcity or privacy constraints and can be combined with architecture search or other compression primitives to produce deployment-ready models. Successful application requires matching the distillation recipe to the task, student capacity, and deployment constraints and managing teacher imperfections and data mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep models across vision and natural language tasks. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning internal representations, leveraging multi-teacher or online schedules, and using data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). When combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods, KD often yields students that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student mismatch, data availability, robustness, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Morse
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention patterns, transferring relational or ensemble behaviors, and operating with real, augmented, or synthesized data. KD is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines—pretraining compact students, combining with pruning/quantization, and using task-aware data strategies—and when student capacity, teacher quality, and data provenance are explicitly managed. While KD can recover much of teacher performance and act as an implicit regularizer, its reliability depends on careful design choices and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-case behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: A Conditional, Pipeline‑First Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces inference cost and often preserves much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness is conditional on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and complementary compression steps. I argue KD should serve as the default, central component of compression workflows while being explicitly combined with targeted pretraining, data strategies, architecture-aware design, and robustness/fairness evaluation to produce reliable production models.

papers_seen.author: Cunningham
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically effective family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Modern KD extends beyond softened-output matching to include feature- and relation-level objectives, multi- and self-distillation schedules, data-aware and data-free protocols, and combinations with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical evidence shows KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities when practitioners attend to teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distilled signals, and data strategies; remaining challenges center on domain shift, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts, and reliable distillation without original data.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and structural signals. A broad suite of distillation techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, relational and channel-wise transfers, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes, and data- or generator-based approaches—enables large reductions in parameter count and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness. Distillation is most effective when combined with task-aware design (student-aware teacher choices, layer alignment or projectors, and data strategies) and complementary compression primitives (architecture search, pruning, quantization). Important limitations include capacity mismatch, optimization instability, propagation of teacher errors or low-frequency behavior loss, and constraints from limited or private data; addressing these requires careful choice of signals, student architectures, and training curricula.

papers_seen.author: Maxwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and in diverse protocols (offline teacher–student, online/multi-teacher, self-distillation). When embedded in a broader pipeline that aligns teacher and student architectures, selects appropriate distillation signals, and uses realistic or synthesized data, KD routinely produces models that approach teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. Practical deployment requires combining KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), explicit evaluation for robustness, and strategies to mitigate capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher artifacts, privacy risks, and degraded behavior on rare or out-of-distribution cases. Ongoing research targets principled teacher selection, reliable data-free distillation, preserving fine-grained behaviors, and deeper theoretical understanding of why and when KD succeeds.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Necessary Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal structure via soft targets, intermediate-feature alignment, attention maps, and relational objectives. When integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful data and architecture design, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance and enable latency-, memory-, or privacy-constrained deployment. However, KD’s benefits are contingent on student capacity, data availability and provenance, teacher artifacts, and distributional shift; addressing these requires deliberate, task-aware pipelines and evaluation tailored to real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Practical, but Necessarily Integrated into a Broader Compression Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for converting large, high-performance deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers substantial parameter and latency savings while preserving much of teacher performance, but its reliability depends on engineering choices about what to transfer, how to prepare teachers and students, data provenance and augmentation, and complementary compression methods. Responsible production use therefore treats KD as the core of a system-level compression pipeline—combined with architecture design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and targeted evaluations for robustness, fairness, and domain-specific behavior—rather than as a standalone remedy.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, higher-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). In practice KD has been applied to compress large pre-trained language models, enable fast inference in NLP, adapt models to new domains or tasks, support heterogeneous and federated settings, and enable data-free scenarios. Approaches differ in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how teachers and students are paired (single vs multi-teacher, jointly trained teachers), and how training data is used or synthesized. Empirical results show KD can substantially reduce model size and latency while preserving much of task performance, but success depends on choices around layer mapping, feature vs. logit supervision, data complexity, and training protocols. Open challenges include handling data heterogeneity, optimizing teacher-student pairings, and ensuring stable distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, often ensemble or over-parameterized teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across computer vision, graph, generative, and language tasks, distillation reduces storage and inference cost while often retaining most of the teacher's accuracy. Methods range from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations or using adversarial generators when training data are unavailable. Distillation has been applied successfully to compress transformers and other large pretrained language models, to speed up question answering and reading-comprehension systems, and to produce compact models suitable for deployment on edge devices. At the same time, distillation faces challenges including loss of certain types of teacher knowledge, sensitivity to which samples are distilled, potential transfer or amplification of undesirable biases, and concerns about robustness and privacy. Recent work addresses these issues by selective sample weighting, multi-teacher schemes, adversarial data-free approaches, and robustness-aware objectives, suggesting a rich design space for future improvement.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Practical, but Effective Only Within Integrated Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical family of techniques for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple transferable signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure) that often allow students to recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or privacy-preserving compression: its success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, handling data availability or synthesis, and combining distillation with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) plus targeted evaluation. I argue that KD should be treated as the central, configurable core of model-compression toolkits, but only as part of an integrated, task-aware pipeline that explicitly addresses capacity mismatch, data provenance, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Incomplete Engine for Practical Model Compression

Treating KD as the core of an integrated compression pipeline — and designing safeguards for its known failure modes — yields the best balance of efficiency and retained performance.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster models for deployment. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary methods (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), careful teacher–student alignment, and data strategies that address limited or private training data. KD yields strong empirical gains across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models) but has failure modes tied to student capacity, data mismatch, and propagation of teacher biases; production use therefore requires design-sensitive recipes and monitoring for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient ones while preserving accuracy. Beyond raw model size reduction, KD enables applications that require interpretable models, heterogeneous and privacy-preserving deployments, and multi-task or low-resource inference. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases (especially on rare tokens or classes) and can be sensitive to data availability and heterogeneity. Best practice therefore combines KD with careful sample selection, architectural mediators for feature transfer, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, or generator-based data synthesis) to achieve robust, deployable student models.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Mccann
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data (real, augmented, or synthesized). While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can serve additional roles such as regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware model release, it has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, domain shift, and propagation of teacher errors—that necessitate careful pipeline design and complementary methods for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation condenses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to map layers, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student capacity. Distillation routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest loss in accuracy, but open problems remain in preserving robustness and fairness, handling domain shift and data scarcity, and reliably distilling rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Torres

papers_seen.author: Cooke

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single training trick into a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for real-world deployment. KD can transfer output behavior, internal representations, and relational or structural knowledge; it can be adapted to constraints such as missing training data, privacy, distributed training, and domain shifts; and when combined with complementary techniques (architecture adaptation, pruning, task-aware layer selection) it produces compact models that retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical use of KD requires matching the distillation strategy to the application constraints (what to transfer, which data to use, and how to align heterogeneous architectures).

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning inputs and architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression (pruning, structured sparsity, quantization) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic samples, curriculum)—KD enables resource-efficient deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings. However, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student; addressing these constraints through multi-teacher designs, black-box adaptation, and feature-level alignment remains essential for robust, private, and high-performance compression.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Nuanced Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and production-oriented approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable, task-aware toolkit and combined with complementary techniques (pretraining of compact architectures, pruning, quantization, data augmentation or synthesis, and architecture-aware design), KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, distillation signals and data regimes, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Responsible deployment requires targeted remedies for capacity mismatch, rare-token and distribution-shift failures, and propagation of teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from soft-target logit matching into a multifaceted, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Modern KD methods transfer outputs, internal representations, relational structure, or ensemble behavior and are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis or privacy-aware protocols to meet deployment constraints. Successful application depends on matching distillation targets and training data to student capacity and task structure while addressing teacher imperfections, domain shift, and privacy or robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Hart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical, but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students. When treated as an integrated pipeline—selecting appropriate distillation signals, preparing teacher and student models, choosing or synthesizing data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks. However, its success is conditional on careful design: student capacity, teacher artifacts, data mismatch, and optimization subtleties can limit gains unless explicitly mitigated. This paper argues KD should be the practical centerpiece of compression workflows while highlighting limits and concrete design principles for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely applicable paradigm for compressing large models and transferring knowledge across architectures, tasks, and deployment constraints. A range of KD variants—data-free, federated, multi-teacher, meta-learned teachers, intermediate-feature transfer, and architecture-aware compression—have been developed to address realistic constraints such as data privacy, limited communication, teacher imperfection, and task-specific efficiency. By matching the KD strategy to the deployment constraint (e.g., privacy, compute budget, domain shift, or paucity of data) practitioners can obtain compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency and resource requirements.

papers_seen.author: Coffey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted paradigm for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students so as to reduce inference cost while retaining much of task performance. Over the last decade KD has grown from simple soft‑label matching into a flexible engineering pipeline that includes intermediate‑representation matching, relational and attention signals, data synthesis or public/unlabeled data use, and integration with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. Practical success depends on matching distillation targets to student capacity and data regime, and several open challenges remain around robustness, fairness, rare‑event preservation, and reliable data‑free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller students, combining approaches such as soft‑label supervision, layer-wise or representation matching, and architectural reduction (pruning, layer skipping, parameter sharing). Research has extended distillation beyond supervised classification to domains including language models, sequence tasks, generative models, federated settings, domain adaptation, and few-shot or data-scarce regimes. Key practical challenges include maintaining accuracy under dataset or domain shift, training without access to original data, handling heterogeneous compute across devices, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and improving training efficiency. Effective solutions mix algorithmic choices (loss design, example selection, curriculum), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or distilled data), and system-level integrations (joint optimization with pruning or layer removal).
