papers_seen.author: Lucas
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default but Conditional Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a design-sensitive pipeline—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and layers, how to access or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture changes—KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance. Its effectiveness is conditional on task, data, and deployment constraints; robust pipelines therefore begin with KD but incorporate complementary methods and explicit mitigations for known failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagated teacher errors, and degraded long-tail or fairness behavior.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Complementarities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teachers to smaller students or by combining compression methods. Work in this area spans practical recipe development for NLP and vision models, theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps, methods that go beyond soft logits to internal feature transfer, strategies for multi-teacher and ensemble compression, approaches for data-limited or data-free settings, and complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. Empirical results show that careful choices (e.g., which samples or layers to use, how to combine teachers, and how to map teacher-to-student layers) matter for final accuracy; theoretical results explain tradeoffs between soft and hard labels, and methods exist that make distillation feasible without teacher data or with constrained hardware.

papers_seen.author: Jennings
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable framework for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. As a first-line technique it reliably recovers much of teacher performance while enabling latency, memory, and privacy constrained deployments; however, KD alone is insufficient for many real-world requirements. Effective compression treats KD as the core of a broader, task-aware pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, complementary compression primitives, data strategies, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate features, attention patterns, or relational structure, and often combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled models can recover much of teacher performance on vision and language tasks, but success depends on what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, data availability and selection, and training protocols. Practical deployment requires addressing optimization challenges, teacher imperfection, domain shift, and distributional issues such as low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Bradley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (compute, memory, latency, privacy). KD spans matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate representations or attention, transferring relational structure, and using multi-teacher, online, or data-free protocols. It is most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when distillation choices are aligned with student capacity, available data, and downstream robustness or fairness requirements. Open problems include principled teacher selection and weighting, reliable zero-shot or data-free distillation, preserving rare-token and fine-grained behaviors, and avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Compression Strategy — Practical Strengths, Necessary Complementary Tools, and Concrete Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven to be a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. When treated as a design problem and combined with complementary methods and data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: success depends on matching teacher and student capacity, aligning inputs and internal representations, handling limited or absent data, and explicitly managing robustness, fairness, and transferred biases. I argue KD should be the default starting point for production compression pipelines, applied with explicit attention to complementary compression primitives, data synthesis or rehearsal methods, and evaluation safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multi-signal paradigm for turning large, accurate models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. Modern practice combines soft-target (logit) matching with intermediate-representation and relational-transfer objectives, often integrated with pretraining, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Effective pipelines account for data availability (including data-free or synthetic-data regimes), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., low-frequency token behavior or robustness under distribution shift). While KD routinely preserves much of teacher performance in applied settings, open problems persist around principled teacher selection, reliably transferring rare-event and robustness properties, and optimizing heterogeneous or privacy-constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool That Requires Integrated, Task-Aware Pipelines for Robust Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and widely applicable technique for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. While KD supplies a flexible set of signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention, and relational structure) that often preserves much of a teacher's performance, its practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and careful evaluation. KD alone does not guarantee robustness to distribution shift, immunity to propagated teacher biases, or preservation of rare-event behavior; achieving reliable deployment therefore requires integrated, task-aware workflows including pretraining, selective or confidence-weighted transfer, feature-mimicking choices, and architecture- or data-level interventions.

papers_seen.author: Whitney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. KD has evolved beyond simple softened-logit matching into a family of methods that transfer intermediate representations, relational structure, or curriculum/sampling strategies, and that operate in online, multi-teacher, or data-limited regimes. Practical success depends on aligning distillation signals with student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives to address robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Complementary Techniques
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior and internal representations across many tasks and modalities, enabling substantial reductions in parameters and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not sufficient by itself in all settings: its success depends on what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and mitigation of transferred biases or errors. For robust, deployable compression, KD should be treated as the central element of a broader pipeline that includes data synthesis or augmentation, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, or progressive module replacement), plus careful attention to privacy, fairness, and domain-shift risks.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Variants, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring aspects of the teacher’s predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of methods—matching output distributions, aligning intermediate features, progressive module replacement, multi-teacher and data-free schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, data availability, privacy, and multimodal inputs. Empirical work shows that when the distillation recipe is matched to model architectures, data conditions, and deployment constraints, students can retain much of the teacher’s performance while offering practical efficiency gains; however, trade-offs and open challenges remain around robustness, domain shift, and faithful transfer of rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Treat Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Compression — but Build a Task‑Aware Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high‑value approach for turning large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure using multiple signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) and often composes with pruning, quantization, or architecture changes. However, KD alone cannot guarantee preservation of rare behaviors, robustness under domain shift, or elimination of teacher biases; practical compression succeeds when distillation is the default first step within a carefully designed, task‑aware pipeline that includes projector design, data strategies, capacity alignment, and complementary compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Constraints, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models retain much of the utility of high-capacity systems. KD operates across levels of abstraction (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure) and is routinely combined with complementary compression strategies (quantization, pruning, architecture search) and data strategies (use of original data, augmentation, or synthesized inputs). Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance in many settings, but success is context-dependent: it depends on the choice of distilled signals, teacher preparation, student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as latency, privacy, or robustness. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, practical variants, and actionable recommendations for applying KD effectively in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Hart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical, but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students. When treated as an integrated pipeline—selecting appropriate distillation signals, preparing teacher and student models, choosing or synthesizing data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks. However, its success is conditional on careful design: student capacity, teacher artifacts, data mismatch, and optimization subtleties can limit gains unless explicitly mitigated. This paper argues KD should be the practical centerpiece of compression workflows while highlighting limits and concrete design principles for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. Beyond parameter reduction, KD provides learned regularization, enables transferring intermediate representations and relational structure, supports data-limited or data-free regimes, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success requires choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data, augmentation, and deployment constraints; remaining challenges include distributional mismatch, capacity and representation gaps, and preserving robustness and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modular approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Empirical practice shows KD yields substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy with modest accuracy loss when distillation signals, data strategies, and student architectures are aligned to deployment constraints. KD is most effective when treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that combines distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; its recurring failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, limited or private data, domain shift, and degraded long-tail behavior. Addressing those limits requires careful selection of distillation targets, data or synthesis strategies, multi-teacher or staged schedules, and evaluation of robustness and fairness in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mccarty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best framed as the core, composable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as a pipeline that selects appropriate distilled signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure), aligns teacher and student architectures, and combines distillation with complementary compression primitives and data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that recover most of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, realizing those gains in practice requires explicit attention to capacity mismatch, teacher bias and errors, data availability (including data-free and federated settings), and robustness to distributional shift. A principled, task-aware KD workflow—using multi-signal objectives, staged schedules, and targeted defenses—balances efficiency and fidelity and is the most reliable route to deployable compressed models in vision, language, and structured domains.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most pragmatic and versatile route to make large deep models usable in constrained settings. When treated as a flexible toolkit—not merely as soft-label matching—KD enables compact models that preserve student performance, transfer intermediate representations, and support deployment constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous devices, or low-precision inference. Real-world success requires combining KD with task-aware layer mapping, multi-teacher or ensemble signals, data-generation or adversarial synthesis when original data are unavailable, and joint use with quantization or precision-reduction. These combinations produce students that are both efficient and robust enough for production use.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable efficient deployment. Beyond simple logit matching, KD methods include intermediate-feature alignment, attention- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance when distillation objectives, student capacity, and data strategies are carefully matched; however, success depends on addressing optimization and representation mismatch, data availability, teacher imperfections, and fairness or robustness concerns. Effective pipelines combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware training schedules to balance efficiency and fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a composable engineering toolkit rather than a single loss or recipe. Effective compression combines representation-level transfer, student pretraining, data-side interventions (real, augmented, or synthetic), progressive or self-distillation schedules, and explicit robustness- and privacy-aware objectives. When these components are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints, distilled models can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements; careless application, by contrast, risks capacity mismatch and propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and a Design-Sensitive Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, highly practical approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and integrates naturally with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and architecture search. Its consistent empirical success across vision and language tasks makes KD a default technique for many deployment pipelines. However, KD is not automatic: reliable compression requires careful choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, how distillation data are chosen or synthesized, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and domain-shift risks. A pragmatic, system-level KD workflow combines pretraining of compact architectures, targeted distillation objectives, complementary compression primitives, and evaluation focused on rare and out-of-domain behaviors.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so the latter can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The toolkit includes matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate representations and attention, relational or contrastive objectives, multi- and online-teacher schedules, and data-aware protocols (including synthetic or data-free inputs). KD is most effective when treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that includes student pretraining, architecture-aware design, pruning or quantization, and careful selection or synthesis of distillation data. Practical deployment must attend to predictable failure modes — capacity mismatch, data or domain shift, teacher artifacts, and long-tail behavior loss — which motivates hybrid, task-aware distillation strategies and continued research on robustness, fairness, and privacy-preserving distillation.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques form a flexible toolkit for turning large, accurate deep models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners transfer information at output (soft targets), intermediate representations (features or attention maps), or relational/ensemble signals and often combine distillation with pruning, structured sparsity, and architecture-aware design. Success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, handling data availability (including data-free or synthesized inputs), and addressing risks such as propagation of teacher errors, fairness and robustness degradation, and performance loss on rare or distribution-shifted phenomena. Across vision and language, careful combinations of distillation objectives, student pretraining or co-design, and complementary compression techniques enable substantial reductions in compute and memory while retaining much of teacher performance.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit that enables compact student models to inherit much of the performance of large teacher models. Treated as a modular, design-sensitive component of compression workflows, KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational patterns), can be adapted to constrained data regimes (real, augmented, or synthesized), and composes effectively with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). At the same time, KD is not a universal remedy: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and distributional/robustness concerns place clear limits on its effectiveness. Responsible, production-ready compression therefore treats KD as the core of an integrated pipeline and couples it with targeted engineering choices, evaluation, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Valentine
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple soft-label matching into multi-level pipelines that include logits transfer, feature and attention imitation, relational losses, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-constrained variants (data-free, few-shot, privacy-aware). Empirical work shows KD frequently yields deployable models that retain much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data strategies. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, degraded behavior on rare or out-of-distribution examples, principled sample selection, and formal guarantees under limited data or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while often preserving — and in some settings improving — task performance. KD methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations or relational structure, and they are frequently combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture transformation) and with data-aware strategies (multi-stage distillation, multi-teacher schedules, or data synthesis) to meet deployment constraints. KD’s benefits arise both from transferring predictive behavior and from inducing useful regularization, but practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to map teacher and student layers, the provenance or synthesis of distillation data, and explicit attention to robustness, rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Toolkit for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. When treated as a system—deciding what signals to transfer (soft outputs, internal representations, relations), how to prepare or synthesize data, how to design teachers and students, and how to combine KD with complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization—KD enables deployable models that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on capacity matching, data availability, and task-aware objectives; addressing robustness, fairness, and privacy requires targeted interventions and monitoring.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted set of techniques that reliably helps compress large deep models into smaller, deployable students, but it is neither a single recipe nor a universal remedy. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what knowledge to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to manage distillation data and deployment constraints. When designed as part of a broader compression workflow—combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and other compression primitives—KD frequently yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs; however, practitioners must also anticipate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and optimization difficulties.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Its practical value arises from a broad set of signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational structure), multiple training schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data strategies (data-aware, data-free, and synthetic augmentation). However, KD’s success is conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and distributional match, and careful choice of what to transfer determine outcomes. For reliable deployment, KD should be treated as the central starting point of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (pretraining, architecture-aware mapping, pruning, quantization), explicit mitigation of bias and robustness risks, and data-provenance strategies that reflect the target environment.

Despite broad empirical success, open problems remain in preserving low-frequency behaviors, robustness and fairness, and in designing principled curricula and teacher-student interfaces for diverse deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single training trick into a broadly applicable, design‑sensitive toolkit for producing compact student models from larger teachers. KD methods operate at multiple signal levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational structure), work with diverse data regimes (original, augmented, synthesized or data‑free), and are most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful teacher–student alignment. Empirical and conceptual work shows KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–performance tradeoffs but has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, transfer of teacher errors, degraded rare‑token or long‑tail behavior, and sensitivity to distribution shift—that require task‑aware engineering, explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness, and targeted research on data synthesis and representation objectives.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible suite of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The KD toolkit includes matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, multi‑teacher and online schedules, and synthesizing or selectively using data; these methods are frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical evidence shows that, when KD is treated as a system—matching distillation signals to student capacity, aligning inputs and architectures, and using complementary compression primitives—students often recover much of teacher performance while delivering large efficiency gains. Important open problems remain in robustness, fairness, low-frequency or long‑tail behavior, reliable distillation without original data, and principled curricula for multi-source transfer.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single training trick into a versatile, context-aware toolkit that enables deployment of large neural models in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. By transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure from one or more teachers into a smaller student — and by combining these transfers with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware adaptation, and data synthesis — KD makes it possible to produce compact models that retain most of a teacher’s capabilities. Effective use of KD requires choosing what information to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle data limitations or domain shifts, treating distillation as a design problem rather than a one-size-fits-all remedy.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade KD has evolved from matching softened outputs to a multi-signal toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware strategies (including data-free synthesis). In practice KD is most effective when composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design), and when distillation choices are matched to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. However, predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, optimization instability, and degraded long-tail or out-of-distribution behavior—require explicit mitigations, careful evaluation, and continued methodological work to preserve robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Levine
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. KD can transfer information at multiple levels—from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure—and when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and task-aware data strategies, it routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on choices about distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability or synthesis, and mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagated teacher errors, and domain shift. A principled, pipeline-oriented use of KD—combining representation-level objectives, careful data protocols, and auxiliary compression methods—gives the most reliable path to deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a logits-matching trick into a broad set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large neural teachers. Modern KD variants transfer soft predictions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structure; they are combined with data-centric practices (augmentation, synthetic and zero-shot data) and complementary compression (pruning, architecture search) to meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains in NLP (notably transformer compression) as well as vision, graphs, and federated settings, while theoretical and empirical studies reveal optimization challenges, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and distributional/heterogeneity limitations. Practical pipelines favor pretraining or progressive replacement, representation-level matching, task-adaptive data strategies, and awareness of privacy and robustness trade-offs.
