papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical family of methods for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. KD has diversified beyond simple logit matching to include feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-alignment and projector-based mappings, multi- and self-teaching schedules, and data-aware protocols (including data-free or synthetic-data strategies). When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful data and teacher–student design, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher utility; persistent limits relate to student capacity, teacher errors, distribution shift, and robustness or privacy concerns. Empirical work across vision, generative modeling, and NLP illustrates both principled mechanisms and practical trade-offs for designing reliable distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Richardson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, multi-signal approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a flexible toolbox, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and can operate with original, augmented, synthesized, or data-free inputs. Empirical and methodological work shows KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs when paired with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware student preparation. Responsible deployment requires explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and scarcity, and robustness and fairness evaluation, so KD should be treated as the central element of a broader, design-sensitive compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from soft-target logit matching into a multifaceted, task-aware toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Modern KD methods transfer outputs, internal representations, relational structure, or ensemble behavior and are routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis or privacy-aware protocols to meet deployment constraints. Successful application depends on matching distillation targets and training data to student capacity and task structure while addressing teacher imperfections, domain shift, and privacy or robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural teachers into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision and language, KD methods include matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, ensembling or multi-teacher schemes, self- and online-distillation, and data-free or synthetic-data approaches. Empirical work shows that properly designed KD pipelines can produce compact models that retain most teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, distillation success depends on teacher–student compatibility, choice of distillation targets, data availability, and training dynamics; open challenges include preserving robustness and fairness, understanding which teacher signals matter for which tasks and architectures, and distilling under strict data or privacy limitations.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Cole
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad family of objectives and protocols has emerged—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational or contrastive losses, multi- and self-distillation schedules, and data strategies that range from using original training data to synthesizing inputs or operating data‑free. In practice, distillation is most effective when integrated into a task- and architecture‑aware compression pipeline that addresses student capacity, data availability and privacy, and robustness to distribution shift; complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architectural adaptation are frequently combined with distillation to meet deployment constraints. Key open problems include preserving rare or fine-grained behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher errors and biases, and designing robust, privacy‑aware distillation protocols for heterogeneous and low-data regimes.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is established as a central, practical approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. A broad family of distillation signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free) together with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher’s effectiveness. Success depends on task- and student-aware design choices, including what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to manage limited or private data, and how to mitigate teacher-induced errors or robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Fernandez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD operates at multiple levels — softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational or structural signals — and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, and data handling. Although KD enables practical deployment across vision and language tasks (including data-free and privacy-sensitive scenarios), its effectiveness depends strongly on design decisions and faces limits such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and data or domain mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the core of a compression pipeline—combined with architecture-aware design, pretraining of compact students, pruning, quantization, and careful data strategies—KD routinely yields substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability (or the ability to synthesize appropriate surrogates), and attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional shift. Responsible deployment therefore treats KD as an essential but bounded tool that must be designed and evaluated in the context of complementary compression primitives and task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Morton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for converting large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD methods transfer teacher behavior via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals, and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency and memory constraints. Practical deployment requires matching what is distilled to student capacity, addressing data availability (including data-free or privacy-aware strategies), and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, propagated teacher errors, and degraded rare-case behavior. Empirical work shows that when KD is treated as a system—choosing teacher signals, aligning inputs and architectures, and integrating complementary compression methods—students frequently recover most of the teacher’s performance while achieving large efficiency gains, but important open problems remain in robustness, fairness, and reliably distilling under absent or private data.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Across vision and natural language tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, selective sample transfer, multi-teacher and data-free strategies—enable substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Practical success depends on matching what is distilled to student capacity, managing data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and addressing harms such as transferred biases or degraded rare-token behavior. A pragmatic pipeline mixes pretraining, representation-aware losses, targeted data manipulations, and teacher-aware design to achieve favorable trade-offs among efficiency, accuracy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and natural language tasks. KD encompasses a family of transfer signals—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure—and is typically combined with data strategies (original, augmented, or synthesized data) and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture modification). Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but outcomes depend on choices of distillation targets, student capacity, data provenance, and teacher quality. Effective deployment adapts KD to task constraints, often integrating pretraining, multi-stage distillation, or multi-teacher schedules; outstanding challenges include teacher–student mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases (notably on rare tokens), domain shift, and privacy or federated heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Weber
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modality-agnostic strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable toolkit—not a single recipe—KD reliably yields major efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but it must be combined with complementary techniques and data-aware practices to address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and privacy constraints. Effective compression pipelines therefore begin with KD and then incorporate representation alignment, architecture-aware choices, quantization/pruning, and careful evaluation under domain shift and safety requirements.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large, high-capacity deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. KD encompasses a range of signals and procedures—matching softened teacher outputs, imitating intermediate representations or attention, transferring relational or contrastive structure, and using multi-stage or ensemble teachers—and it composes with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical results show distilled students frequently recover a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing memory, compute, and latency, but outcomes depend on choices about what to transfer, student capacity, availability of (or access to) distillation data, and concerns about robustness, privacy, and propagated biases. Ongoing directions emphasize robustness under distribution shift and adversaries, data- or privacy-constrained distillation, principled teacher selection, and integrated pipelines that jointly optimize architecture and distillation objectives.

papers_seen.author: Rodgers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Practices, Mechanisms, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language. Effective KD combines soft-target transfer with representation-level alignment, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and data strategies (including augmentation and synthesis) while often being integrated with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. The benefits of KD are conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and careful teacher–student alignment; common failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, and degraded robustness or rare-behavior fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Starting Point for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When used as the default first step in compression workflows and combined with task-aware signal selection, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives, KD often delivers strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs. However, its effectiveness is bounded by student capacity, data availability, and risks of transferring teacher artifacts; successful practice requires explicit mitigation strategies and integration with other compression methods.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression across Modalities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft logits to a rich family of techniques that enable deployment of large models in resource-constrained settings. Across NLP, vision, generative modeling, and cross-modal systems, distillation methods that match intermediate representations, adapt teacher signals to student inputs, exploit many-to-many layer correspondences, and combine with pruning or ensemble guidance consistently produce compact models with near-teacher performance. KD is also effective for domain adaptation and continual learning, making it a practical foundation for producing small, fast, and robust models for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System: Practical Strengths, Limits, and Prescriptions for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a modular system—combining soft-target supervision, representation-level objectives, data augmentation, multi-teacher signals, and complementary compression methods—KD reliably yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. Effectiveness depends on handling data availability, architecture mismatches, and undesirable teacher artifacts; these constraints are manageable when KD is designed with domain adaptation, input alignment, and augmentation-aware strategies. I argue KD should be the default toolchain for producing production-ready compact models, applied with explicit attention to what knowledge is transferred and how it is matched to student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Simpson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Toolkit for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a configurable toolbox it can transfer softened outputs, internal features, and relational signals; enable compression with limited or synthesized data; and combine with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD reliably improves student efficiency in many settings, but its success depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data, robustness, and fairness concerns. I argue KD should be the default core of compression pipelines while being applied conditionally and in concert with complementary methods and careful validation.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and multifaceted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as an engineered pipeline—selecting appropriate distillation signals, preparing teacher and student models (including pre-training the student), choosing or synthesizing training data, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptations—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success is conditional: careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to generate or filter data for transfer, and how to mitigate robustness, fairness, and capacity-mismatch risks are required for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile mechanism to compress large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central component of compression pipelines and matched to task constraints, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Success with KD depends on deliberate choices about what knowledge to transfer (logits, features, relations), how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or missing teacher data, and how to protect robustness and fairness. I argue KD should be the default compression engine for modern deep learning and NLP systems, but its safe and effective use requires task-aware design and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with complementary methods such as student pretraining, progressive replacement, data synthesis, and fairness- or privacy-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing deep models and transferring capabilities across architectures and modalities. KD has enabled large speedups and model-size reductions while preserving or even improving downstream task performance when carefully applied. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher–student alignment, and distributional heterogeneity, and it can transmit teacher biases or errors. Combining logit-based supervision with feature- and relation-focused objectives, aligning intermediate representations, and adapting distillation strategies to task and data constraints yields the best trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while preserving much of their predictive performance. KD has matured beyond simple output-matching into a family of methods that transfer intermediate representations, attention or channel-wise signals, and task-specific inductive biases; it can operate under data scarcity or privacy constraints and can be combined with architecture search or other compression primitives to produce deployment-ready models. Successful application requires matching the distillation recipe to the task, student capacity, and deployment constraints and managing teacher imperfections and data mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Phelps
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable core of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, and the provenance or scarcity of distillation data. Responsible deployment therefore requires task-aware selection of distillation targets, mitigation of propagated teacher errors, and explicit evaluation for robustness and rare-token behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or more private models. Across vision, speech, and NLP tasks, a consistent set of practices has emerged—logit/soft-label transfer, intermediate-layer matching, and task- or domain-specific adaptation—augmented by variants that address missing data, distributed training, privacy, and teacher-student mismatch. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while enjoying large gains in inference speed and memory, and recent work clarifies when and why distillation acts as an effective regularizer.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central and Practical, but Necessarily Integrated into a Broader Compression Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for converting large, high-performance deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD delivers substantial parameter and latency savings while preserving much of teacher performance, but its reliability depends on engineering choices about what to transfer, how to prepare teachers and students, data provenance and augmentation, and complementary compression methods. Responsible production use therefore treats KD as the core of a system-level compression pipeline—combined with architecture design, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and targeted evaluations for robustness, fairness, and domain-specific behavior—rather than as a standalone remedy.

papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically driven paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. In practice KD functions as a configurable toolkit: practitioners choose which teacher signals to transfer (soft logits, features, attention, relational structure), how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, and how to source or synthesize data for distillation. KD has enabled substantial reductions in model size and latency across vision, speech, graph, and NLP tasks (including pretrained Transformer models), but its success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and attention to robustness, privacy, and distributional shift. Practical pipelines therefore combine KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and targeted procedures (multi-teacher aggregation, student-friendly teacher training, data augmentation, or data-free distillation) to close the gap to teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool That Requires Integrated, Task-Aware Pipelines for Robust Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and widely applicable technique for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. While KD supplies a flexible set of signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention, and relational structure) that often preserves much of a teacher's performance, its practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and careful evaluation. KD alone does not guarantee robustness to distribution shift, immunity to propagated teacher biases, or preservation of rare-event behavior; achieving reliable deployment therefore requires integrated, task-aware workflows including pretraining, selective or confidence-weighted transfer, feature-mimicking choices, and architecture- or data-level interventions.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods compress large deep models into smaller, faster, or more private models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature shows a spectrum of KD signals (soft logits, intermediate features, layer mappings), enhancements via data interventions and architecture search, and combinations with pruning or low-precision inference. Practical success depends on task- and deployment-aware choices (which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, what augmentations or synthetic data to use) as well as attention to privacy and robustness. The field has produced effective recipes for compressing pretrained language models, vision transformers, and generative models, while ongoing work clarifies limits and complementary techniques for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Villarreal
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Task‑Aware Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably compresses large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. When treated as a central, composable element of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely yields strong trade-offs between efficiency and task performance. However, its success is conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and provenance, optimization dynamics, and fairness/robustness concerns limit what KD can accomplish on its own. Practical pipelines therefore make KD the default backbone but explicitly mitigate known failure modes through task-aware signal selection, teacher calibration, and integration with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When implemented beyond simple soft-label matching — e.g., via intermediate-feature alignment, layer-mapping, task-aware objectives, curriculum-driven sample selection, or privacy-preserving synthesis — KD can preserve much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost and enabling on-device, federated, or low-latency deployment. However, KD is not a universal solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability or synthesis strategy, and attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift. Best practice treats KD as one element in a compression pipeline that also uses pruning, quantization, architecture search, and targeted evaluation for adversarial and distributional failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD operates at multiple levels — softened outputs (logits), intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and sometimes architectural or module-wise mappings — and is typically used as part of a broader compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data regimes). Empirically, well-designed distillation pipelines recover a large portion of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and memory; however, KD’s effectiveness depends strongly on teacher–student capacity alignment, the choice of distilled signals, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and explicit handling of robustness, rare-event behavior, and fairness issues. Remaining research challenges include principled teacher selection, preserving robustness and long‑tail behaviors, reliable layer- or module-mapping for large pre-trained models, and distillation under strict privacy or data‑scarce constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware data strategies, KD frequently yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. However, its success is conditional on student capacity, data regime and domain match, teacher quality, and explicit attention to robustness, privacy, and fairness; therefore KD should be applied as an adaptive pipeline element rather than a one-size-fits-all algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Tool Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible family of methods that, when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression techniques, enables deployment of compact models with strong utility. KD can transfer final-output behavior, intermediate representations, and structured relationships; it can operate with or without original training data, be adapted for privacy-sensitive or federated settings, and be combined with quantization or pruning to meet hardware constraints. Effective practice requires attention to what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how KD is integrated into the broader compression pipeline to avoid propagation of teacher biases or degradation on rare or shifted data.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. It functions as a multi-signal toolbox—softened output matching, intermediate representation alignment, relational or attention-level transfer, and data-side strategies—that is often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Distillation routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs in vision and language tasks, but its success is conditional on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and provenance, and mitigation of teacher error or bias. Practical deployments therefore treat distillation as one component of an integrated compression pipeline, using task-aware objective design, data strategies (including privacy-preserving or synthesized surrogates), and careful evaluation on rare or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) converts large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A diverse toolkit has emerged—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, transferring relational or ensemble signals, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware strategies (including data-free synthesis). KD is typically composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student design to meet latency, memory, privacy, and deployment constraints. While KD regularly yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, its effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability and provenance, alignment of signals, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central tools for shrinking large deep models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable models while retaining much of their performance. Research has expanded beyond the original logit-based teacher-student paradigm to include feature mimicking, self-distillation, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, multi-teacher and adaptive-teacher strategies, and task- or hardware-aware compression. These methods have been applied across modalities — including vision, graphs, generative models, and a broad set of NLP tasks — and are increasingly combined with architecture search and pruning to meet deployment constraints. Despite empirical successes, important questions remain about what knowledge is most useful to transfer, how to select or adapt teachers, and how to operate under data, compute, or privacy limitations.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. The approach includes aligning soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can operate with original, augmented, or synthesized data. In practice, distillation is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline—combining architecture-aware design, pruning, and quantization—and when distillation objectives are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows substantial reductions in inference cost and memory with modest performance loss, but predictable failure modes remain around capacity mismatch, data scarcity or mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degraded robustness on rare or shifted inputs. Ongoing challenges include principled teacher–student curricula, reliable distillation without original data, and theoretical understanding of why and when different signals transfer successfully.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Task-Aware Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level approach for compressing large deep models into smaller students that can meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. As a flexible toolkit, KD transfers information through softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and can operate with or without original training data. However, KD alone is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of biases, low-frequency behaviors, and privacy concerns. A reliable compression pipeline treats KD as the central, task-aware component and combines it with complementary techniques (pretraining of compact architectures, pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, and privacy-aware protocols) and evaluation procedures targeted to deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Bounded Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention patterns, and relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher–student alignment, student capacity, the availability and nature of data, and attentive handling of robustness, domain-shift, and privacy risks. A production-ready compression protocol treats KD as one core component within a broader pipeline that includes pre-training of compact architectures, careful choice of distillation signals, data strategies (including privacy- or data-free methods), and complementary compression operations such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Pipelines, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central and practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. A mature toolkit now includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational objectives, multi- and self-teacher schedules, and data-side strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free methods). KD is most effective when integrated into a pipeline that aligns student architecture and capacity with distilled signals, leverages student pretraining, and composes with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Nonetheless, predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, data scarcity, and robustness/fairness degradation—mean KD must be applied with task-aware design, careful evaluation, and mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Glass
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure). KD is most effective when treated as a component of a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness. Empirical and theoretical work show distilled students often recover a substantial fraction of teacher performance, but success hinges on teacher–student capacity alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and targeted mitigation of failure modes such as propagation of teacher errors, domain shift, and loss of rare or safety-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. The literature establishes a broad family of distillation objectives (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational and contrastive losses), training schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher, and self-distillation), and data protocols (original-data, augmented/synthetic data, and data-free or privacy-aware approaches). Empirical work shows KD typically recovers a substantial fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but its success depends on careful teacher–student design, student capacity, data availability and quality, and integration with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. Key limitations remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and preserving robustness under distributional shift, motivating task-aware, data-aware, and hybrid pipelines for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. KD methods span soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, attention- or relation-based objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware approaches including data-free or synthetic-data distillation. In practice KD is usually integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and task-aware training schedules to meet latency, memory, privacy, and robustness constraints. While KD often yields strong empirical trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy, its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, the availability and nature of distillation data, and specific optimization choices; these dependencies motivate hybrid pipelines and targeted remedies for capacity mismatch, domain shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transforms large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring behavioral and representational information. Across vision, language, graph, and federated settings, KD variants—ranging from softened-output matching to intermediate-feature imitation, relational objectives, and multi‑teacher or online schedules—enable practical deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation pipelines, often combined with pre-training and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), produce compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting application-specific requirements. However, effective distillation depends on student capacity, data or synthetic-data strategies, teacher quality, and attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift; these limitations motivate hybrid pipelines and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-target (logit) matching to include intermediate-feature and attention-level supervision, multi-teacher and online protocols, data-aware strategies (including data-free synthesis), and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware training. Effective distillation depends on careful choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle data and robustness constraints; when treated as a design problem rather than a single recipe, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of the teacher's utility while meeting practical deployment requirements. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors (especially on long-tail or low-frequency phenomena), domain shift, and privacy-sensitive scenarios, which motivate hybrid pipelines and task-aware prescriptions for distillation.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal toolkit for turning large neural teachers into smaller, deployable students. KD operates by transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational statistics, and can be combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free approaches). When used in task-aware pipelines and matched to student capacity and data constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve a substantial fraction of teacher performance; however, its success is conditional on careful teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and explicit evaluation for robustness, rare-case behaviors, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a set of teacher→student techniques that produce smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure from larger models. KD has evolved from simple logit matching into a diverse toolkit that includes feature- and attention-level imitation, multi-teacher and online schedules, data-aware and data-free protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success requires matching distillation signals, data strategies, and student capacity to deployment constraints while guarding against teacher error propagation, domain mismatch, and robustness or fairness regressions. When embedded in a design-sensitive compression pipeline, KD routinely yields compact models suitable for real-world use, but important open problems remain in automating signal selection, preserving rare-behavior/generalization, and ensuring privacy and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Richardson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, multi-signal approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a flexible toolbox, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and can operate with original, augmented, synthesized, or data-free inputs. Empirical and methodological work shows KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs when paired with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware student preparation. Responsible deployment requires explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and scarcity, and robustness and fairness evaluation, so KD should be treated as the central element of a broader, design-sensitive compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large neural networks so they can run efficiently in production and on resource-constrained devices. Recent work shows KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, and that a range of complementary techniques—data augmentation, multi-teacher schedules, internal representation matching, layer alignment, meta-learning of teachers, and robustness-aware objectives—meaningfully improve student quality or transfer desirable properties. At the same time, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on optimization, the choice of teacher/student architectures, and the distributional complexity of the training data. I argue that best practice for KD in deep learning and NLP is to treat it as a family of methods to be combined—augmenting data, distilling intermediate representations, leveraging multiple or adaptive teachers, and explicitly distilling robustness—rather than as a single fixed recipe.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from matching softened teacher logits to a broad, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable models in vision, speech, and natural language processing. Modern KD methods transfer information at multiple levels (outputs, intermediate representations, attention/relations), operate in varied data regimes (full-data, few-shot, data-free/zero-shot), and are frequently combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD reliably reduces inference cost and enables on-device and low-latency deployments when practitioner choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and complementary compression are task- and capacity-aware. However, KD is not a universal cure: capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, limited or private data, and distribution shift create failure modes that require careful objective design, student pretraining, and evaluation under deployment conditions.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Task‑Aware, and Complementary Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically effective mechanism for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system-level practice rather than a single algorithm, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths arise from multi-level signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), adaptable data strategies (original, augmented, synthetic, or data-free), and compatibility with complementary compression tools (pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on student capacity and initialization, the choice of distilled signals, data provenance, and explicit mitigation of transferred errors, fairness risks, and robustness under distributional shift. Practitioners should adopt KD as the default starting point but design distillation recipes that are task-aware, data-aware, and integrated with other compression primitives to meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression and Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a core engineering technique that enables deployment, adaptation, privacy, and robustness for large neural models in real-world systems. By treating distillation as a family of methods—ranging from output soft-target transfer to feature- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and privacy-aware protocols—practitioners can compress models while preserving task performance and satisfying latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. Thoughtful application of KD, combined with complementary methods (pretraining, projector design, multi-stage schedules, and careful handling of teacher imperfections), yields compact models that are practical for production while exposing clear avenues for further research.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Pathways for Compressing Large NLP Models: Pre-train the Student, Distill Carefully, and Guard for Data & Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach to compress large deep learning models for NLP and related tasks. When the student model is itself pre-trained, distillation yields especially strong and consistent gains; complementary methods — including data augmentation during distillation, progressive module replacement, ensemble teachers or teacher adaptation, and data-free or privacy-aware distillation — address common deployment constraints such as limited task data, inference cost, data access, and adversarial robustness. Combining these techniques and choosing distillation targets and schedules with theoretical and empirical guidance yields compact models that retain much of the original performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from a teacher. A broad family of distillation objectives has been developed—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational or ensemble transfers, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware approaches. Distillation is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Practical limits remain around teacher–student mismatch, preservation of low-frequency behaviors in language tasks, robustness and adversarial vulnerabilities, and privacy/communication trade-offs in federated or data-limited settings. Addressing these requires student-aware teacher design, feature- and attention-aware objectives, careful data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), and combined compression pipelines tailored to the production environment.

papers_seen.author: Avila
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default first-line approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students. KD offers a flexible set of mechanisms—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation transfer, attention/relational objectives, and online/self-distillation—that routinely yield large efficiency gains with modest performance loss. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, data availability and provenance, student capacity and architecture, and explicit measures to preserve robustness, fairness, and privacy. Practical pipelines therefore begin with KD but must plan for complementary architectural adaptation, pruning/quantization, data strategies (filtering, synthesis, or data-free methods), and careful evaluation under domain shift and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a configurable toolkit—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, how to align architectures, and which complementary compression methods to apply—KD routinely yields efficient models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, its success depends on student capacity, data availability and domain match, and careful mitigation of transferred errors or biases; therefore KD should be adopted as a central component of compression pipelines while being combined with task-aware design, data strategies, and robustness and fairness evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output supervision, intermediate-representation alignment, teacher design, and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: outcomes depend on what is distilled, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and targeted interventions to address robustness, fairness, and privacy. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as the core of a hybrid, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Rowe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Benefits, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile engineering paradigm for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision and language tasks KD has been instantiated as softened output (logit) matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, relational or contrastive objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware strategies including data-free synthesis. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful design choices about teacher signals, layer mapping, and distillation data, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on addressing capacity mismatch, teacher errors and biases, distribution shift and long-tail behaviors, and data- or privacy-driven constraints; treating KD as a configurable toolkit rather than a single recipe is the prevailing recommendation for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Herman
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD is multifaceted—ranging from logit/soft-target matching to feature- and relation-level mimicry, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-free or synthesized-data protocols—and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Its success is conditional on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to mitigate capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and propagation of teacher artifacts. Open challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, robust and privacy-preserving zero-shot distillation, preserving low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and balancing compression with fairness and robustness.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior via softened outputs, align intermediate representations or attention, and incorporate multi-teacher, data-free, or privacy-aware protocols. When integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and matched to student capacity and data constraints, KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a panacea: capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, data mismatch, and robustness or fairness concerns limit outcomes unless addressed by careful design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible mechanism for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When used as the core of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, pretraining, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives, KD frequently yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, KD has clear limits—capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, propagation of teacher errors or biases, low-frequency token failures, and data- or privacy-driven constraints—that require task-aware remedies. A pragmatic recommendation is to treat KD as the default compression engine but to design hybrid, adaptive pipelines that address these conditional failure modes through pretraining, multi-signal transfer, data synthesis or augmentation, multi-teacher strategies, and integration with pruning/quantization and fairness- or privacy-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Morton

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for converting large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD methods transfer teacher behavior via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals, and are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency and memory constraints. Practical deployment requires matching what is distilled to student capacity, addressing data availability (including data-free or privacy-aware strategies), and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, propagated teacher errors, and degraded rare-case behavior. Empirical work shows that when KD is treated as a system—choosing teacher signals, aligning inputs and architectures, and integrating complementary compression methods—students frequently recover most of the teacher’s performance while achieving large efficiency gains, but important open problems remain in robustness, fairness, and reliably distilling under absent or private data.

Practical success depends on aligning distillation signals with student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives to address robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic for shrinking large models into a fundamental, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models across vision, speech, and natural language processing. Empirical work shows distilled students often recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under strict latency, memory, or privacy constraints, but success depends on choices about teacher quality, student capacity, data selection or synthesis, and training protocols. Current directions emphasize multi-stage distillation, data- and architecture-aware objectives, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and pre-training; open problems remain around principled teacher selection, robust cross-domain transfer, low-resource and data-free scenarios, and preserving fairness and calibration under compression.
