papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Conditional Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-oriented toolkit that can reliably shrink large models into smaller, deployable students when embedded in a deliberate compression pipeline. In practice KD frequently recovers a large share of teacher performance while enabling latency, memory, and privacy improvements, but its success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability or synthesis, and complementary compression steps. Real-world deployment therefore requires task-aware signal choices, student-aware design and pretraining, data strategies (including data-free or augmented synthesis when needed), and explicit evaluation of robustness, long-tail behavior, and privacy trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Beyond in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a flexible paradigm that improves efficiency, robustness, privacy, and generalization across modalities and tasks. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight deployable models, transfer internal representations to preserve teacher behaviors, operate without original training data, and be adapted to distributed and privacy-sensitive settings. Recent methodological advances—layer- and attention-aware projection, multi-teacher schedules, meta-learned teachers, and techniques connecting KD to regularization—make distillation a practical and theoretically grounded tool for both research and production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning internal representations or attention, and using relational or ensemble signals; when combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, it routinely yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on careful teacher–student design, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), capacity alignment, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy concerns. Treating KD as a multifaceted toolkit—applied with task- and deployment-aware choices—produces the most reliable compression outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are mature, diverse strategies to reduce the computational and memory costs of large deep models while retaining much of their task performance. Approaches span architecture-level methods that search or prune for compact student networks, training-time methods that transfer dark knowledge via logits or intermediate representations, and data-centric methods that operate when original training data are unavailable. Empirical work shows success compressing large language models into lightweight networks for NLP tasks, highlights task- and data-specific pitfalls (notably for low-frequency tokens in sequence tasks), and motivates specialized extensions in federated and domain-adaptive settings. Theory and interpretive analyses have begun to clarify why distillation helps generalization and optimization, and recent work advocates shaping teachers to be more student-friendly or designing student-aware compression procedures. Overall, the literature shows a practical toolkit of complementary techniques—task-adaptive architecture search, feature- and attention-based matching, adversarial or synthetic-data distillation, and teacher-student co-training—each with trade-offs between efficiency, robustness, and fidelity to teacher behavior.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured relationships. Across deep learning and NLP, KD enables deployment of performant models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability and design of distillation data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and training protocols that mitigate capacity and distribution mismatches. Open challenges include robust teacher selection, data- and domain-mismatch, and scaling distillation methods to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression and Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a core engineering technique that enables deployment, adaptation, privacy, and robustness for large neural models in real-world systems. By treating distillation as a family of methods—ranging from output soft-target transfer to feature- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and privacy-aware protocols—practitioners can compress models while preserving task performance and satisfying latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. Thoughtful application of KD, combined with complementary methods (pretraining, projector design, multi-stage schedules, and careful handling of teacher imperfections), yields compact models that are practical for production while exposing clear avenues for further research.

papers_seen.author: Kramer
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods extend beyond matching teacher output probabilities to include intermediate-representation and relational transfers, multi- and self-distillation, and protocols that operate with limited or synthesized data. In practice KD is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines that consider student architecture, complementary primitives (pruning, quantization), and data strategies. Despite strong empirical benefits, KD has predictable failure modes—capacity and optimization mismatch, degradation on low-frequency or domain-specific behaviors, and transfer of teacher biases or vulnerabilities—which motivate continued work on alignment methods, data-free distillation, and robustness-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a system-level tool it routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but its reliability depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how the student is initialized, how distillation data are provided or synthesized, and how robustness, fairness, and rare-case behaviors are evaluated. I argue KD should be the default starting point for compression pipelines but must be applied conditionally and combined with complementary techniques and explicit evaluation to produce production-ready compact models.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for producing compact models from large teachers that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses a family of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention mimicry, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free synthesis—that routinely yield substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD has practical limits (data and domain mismatch, student capacity gaps, and safety/robustness concerns) that make it most effective when combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware search, and robustness-aware objectives. Practitioners should treat KD as the core of a broader compression toolkit and adapt which knowledge is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and what auxiliary procedures (data augmentation, adversarial training, teacher design) are required to meet specific deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core practical approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of the original performance. Multiple distillation mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adversarial/ensemble-based transfer, and data-free or selective-sample techniques—allow KD to address constraints such as limited data, heterogeneous deployment, low-precision hardware, and domain shift. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a transfer of representational structure and as a regularizer; its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, how training data (real or synthetic) are used, and which complementary compression methods are applied. Remaining practical challenges include distributional mismatch, heterogeneity of architectures and devices, and principled teacher selection and optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable technique for producing smaller, faster models from large pretrained teachers. KD operates through multiple signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and yields substantial efficiency gains when paired with complementary methods and task-aware design. However, KD alone cannot guarantee robustness, fairness, or optimal hardware utilization: achieving production-grade compression requires matching distillation objectives to data availability, architecture mismatch, privacy constraints, and combining KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the core of a multi-tool compression pipeline—central to practical deployment but reliant on deliberate system-level choices to realize its benefits reliably.

papers_seen.author: Herman
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD is multifaceted—ranging from logit/soft-target matching to feature- and relation-level mimicry, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-free or synthesized-data protocols—and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Its success is conditional on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to mitigate capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and propagation of teacher artifacts. Open challenges include principled teacher selection and weighting, robust and privacy-preserving zero-shot distillation, preserving low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, and balancing compression with fairness and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Serrano
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied as an engineering practice that selects which signals to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure), matches teacher and student capacities, and integrates complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD enables substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its reliability depends on data availability, student capacity, teacher quality, and careful protocol choices; thus practitioners should integrate KD with task-aware design, data strategies, and robust evaluation to realize dependable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Integrations, and Conditional Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible pathway to convert large, high-performing deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture-aware surgery to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its empirical strengths include preserving much of teacher performance while enabling large efficiency gains; its limitations arise from teacher–student mismatch, data availability constraints, possible propagation of teacher defects, and robustness or fairness trade-offs. Effective deployment treats KD as the core of a hybrid compression toolkit and requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align layers and capacities, how to handle scarce or private data, and when to combine KD with low-precision numerics or structured pruning.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. The practice encompasses matching teacher logits, imitating intermediate representations or attention patterns, aligning layers across architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) or data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, data-free training). Success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, availability or synthesis of distillation data, and task-aware design; remaining challenges include robustness under domain shift, preserving long-tail or rare behaviors, and operating under privacy or federated constraints. Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and generative models shows that when these elements are matched to deployment constraints, distillation can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost and memory footprint.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring aspects of teacher behavior. The field has expanded from soft-label (logit) supervision to diverse strategies including feature- and representation-level imitation, flexible layer mapping, online/co-distillation, data- and domain-aware augmentation, and multimodal-to-mono-modal transfer. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but success depends on what is transferred (soft targets, features, relations), how teacher and student architectures are aligned, the availability and quality of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy, domain shift, and compute budget. Open challenges include selecting the right distillation targets for task and capacity gap, ensuring robustness and fairness post-compression, and automating adaptive distillation pipelines for heterogeneous production settings.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: A Conditional, Pipeline‑First Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces inference cost and often preserves much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness is conditional on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and complementary compression steps. I argue KD should serve as the default, central component of compression workflows while being explicitly combined with targeted pretraining, data strategies, architecture-aware design, and robustness/fairness evaluation to produce reliable production models.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Olson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. KD operates across multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, relational structure) and pairs naturally with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Its practical success depends on careful design choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, what distillation data to use (including synthetic or data‑free protocols), and explicit handling of capacity limits, robustness, and fairness. KD routinely yields compact models that recover a large fraction of teacher performance in vision and language tasks, but predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, domain shift, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and degraded rare‑token behavior) motivate task‑aware pipelines that combine distillation with complementary steps and targeted evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while preserving much of the teacher performance. KD spans simple logit-based supervision to richer representation-, relation-, and adversarial-level transfers and is used to enable on-device inference, multi-task models, domain specialization, privacy-aware releases, and data-limited deployments. Best outcomes arise when KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), task-aware design, careful sample or synthetic-data strategies, and interventions for bias and privacy. KD has clear empirical benefits across modalities but also well-documented limits—sensitivity to data availability and heterogeneity, potential propagation of teacher errors or biases, and the need for architectural and optimization care—motivating principled adaptations and further study.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Beyond Compression: Roles, Limits, and Best Practices for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly framed as a route to compress large models into smaller deployable students, but its benefits and pitfalls extend well beyond mere parameter reduction. KD acts as a form of learned regularization, can be applied in self-distillation and teacher-free regimes, and enables transferring properties such as robustness, privacy-preserving signals, and task-specific intermediate knowledge. At the same time, KD faces optimization and representation-mismatch challenges and can propagate undesirable biases from teacher to student. This paper argues that practitioners should treat KD as a flexible toolbox: combine soft-label supervision with internal-representation matching, flexible layer-mapping, attention-guided feature alignment, and targeted interventions for fairness, privacy, and robustness to get consistent benefits in both vision and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques condense information from larger or more complex models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable ones. Across vision, speech, recommendation, generative models, and natural language processing, practitioners use a mix of logit-based soft-label supervision, feature imitation, data distillation, multi-teacher fusion, curriculum strategies, and architecture-aware search to trade accuracy for latency, memory, or interpretability. Empirical work shows distilled students can often approach teacher accuracy while enabling deployment in latency- or resource-constrained settings; theoretical and empirical analyses attribute much of KD’s effectiveness to the regularizing properties of soft targets, while recent extensions explicitly address adversarial robustness, decision-boundary transfer, domain adaptation, continual learning, and task-specific constraints. Remaining challenges include preserving robustness and fine-grained behaviors (e.g., low-frequency phenomena), designing teacher-free or data-free alternatives, and building principled curricula and multi-source transfers that maximize student utility in downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for transferring predictive behavior and representational structure from large teacher models to smaller student models. Across modalities, KD combines soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, relational or attention-aware objectives, and data-side strategies (including multi-teacher and data-synthesis protocols) to produce compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Best results arise when KD is embedded in hybrid pipelines (student pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when distillation recipes are adapted to student capacity, available data, and deployment requirements. Open problems include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases or errors, domain shift and data scarcity, and principled automation for heterogeneous architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Barton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression — Powerful but Incomplete
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable approach for transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a core component of compression pipelines, KD often yields substantial reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a standalone cure: its success depends on what signals are distilled, student capacity and initialization, data availability and distributional match, and safeguards against propagating teacher errors or biases. For reliable deployment, KD should be treated as the default starting point that must be combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware mapping), robust data strategies, and careful evaluation of edge cases and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Poole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented toolkit for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD unifies a family of training objectives and workflows—soft-output matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher schedules, adversarially chosen examples, and privacy- or task-aware pipelines—that can be composed with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. When designed with attention to teacher–student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD enables practical, high-quality compression across NLP and vision tasks while exposing research needs around robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) converts large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A diverse toolkit has emerged—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, transferring relational or ensemble signals, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware strategies (including data-free synthesis). KD is typically composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful teacher–student design to meet latency, memory, privacy, and deployment constraints. While KD regularly yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, its effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability and provenance, alignment of signals, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practically effective family of techniques for producing compact models from large teachers. When treated as a central, configurable component of compression pipelines—combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), data and augmentation strategies, and careful teacher–student alignment—KD routinely yields large reductions in latency and footprint while retaining most of the original performance. Its practical success is conditional on explicit handling of capacity mismatch, data availability, distributional robustness, and the risk of transferring teacher errors or biases; therefore KD should be the default starting point for compression but applied deliberately and in hybrid pipelines tailored to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Toolkit for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, representation-level matching, data augmentation, selective sample strategies, and multi-teacher or federated adaptations—KD can produce efficient models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, KD has known failure modes (teacher error propagation, data- and device-heterogeneity, and sample-wise regularization effects) that require explicit remedies and system-level design choices to ensure robust transfer.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-faceted set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students to reduce compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD methods operate at multiple levels—softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure—and are most effective when paired with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture search), careful data handling (real, augmented, or synthesized), and architecture-aware alignment between teacher and student. Practical application requires decisions about which signals to transfer, how to bridge capacity gaps, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to validate robustness, fairness, and rare-token behavior; unresolved issues include principled handling of teacher imperfections, domain shift, privacy, and faithful transfer of calibration and fairness properties.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) converts large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural knowledge. Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD methods range from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level alignment, multi-teacher and meta-learned teacher schemes, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical deployment requires careful choices about which teacher signals to transfer, how to prepare and align students, and how to handle data limitations, distributional shift, and robustness. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance at dramatically reduced cost, persistent gaps (capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, rare-token and adversarial robustness) motivate hybrid pipelines and targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Mccormick
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When KD is embedded in a task-aware compression pipeline that aligns distillation signals with student capacity, uses data-aware strategies (including synthesis when necessary), and combines distillation with complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization), practitioners can produce compact models that retain much of teacher utility while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, KD’s benefits are conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, architecture mismatch, and distribution-shift vulnerabilities limit outcomes unless addressed through deliberate pipeline choices and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Component of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for converting large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can operate with real, augmented, or synthesized data. In practice, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while retaining much of a teacher's performance, but its reliability depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signals, data availability and provenance, and explicit mitigation of robustness, fairness, and privacy risks. Effective deployment treats KD as the core element of an integrated compression pipeline—paired with architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, data strategies, and targeted evaluation—rather than a standalone recipe.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Practices, Mechanisms, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level toolkit for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Methods include matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data strategies ranging from augmentation to data-free synthesis; KD is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Empirical evidence shows KD can recover much of teacher performance when treated as a system—choosing appropriate distillation signals, aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining complementary compression primitives—while persistent challenges remain in robustness, fairness, rare-case behavior, and reliable distillation without original data.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit for converting large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. Techniques span matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives such as pruning and quantization. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, the role of pre-training for compact models, and data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized). While KD can preserve most teacher performance and enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, open issues include teacher–student capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, robustness under domain shift, and reliable distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Costa
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The field has matured from simple soft-label matching into a diverse, modular toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-centric strategies (including data-free and synthetic-data approaches). KD is most effective when treated as a design-sensitive process—selecting which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance and can improve deployability across modalities, practical limits remain around capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, domain shift, rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and robustness/privacy concerns, motivating continued empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation unifies multiple strategies for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models while preserving performance. It supports a range of goals — parameter and latency reduction, robustness, interpretability, and privacy-aware deployment — by transferring information from a teacher to a student via soft outputs, intermediate representations, or structural/architectural guidance. Practical and research advances show that combining distillation modes (feature-level, output-level, progressive module replacement), data augmentation, and adaptive teacher training yields compact models that approach teacher performance even under limited data, heterogeneous devices, or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for converting large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Across vision and natural language tasks, KD variants (soft-target matching, feature- and relation-level imitation, multi-teacher schedules, online or adversarial schemes, and data-side strategies including synthetic or data-free generation) have enabled substantial reductions in inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. Empirical and applied work shows that KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful teacher–student design, and explicit handling of data, robustness, and fairness concerns. Remaining challenges include capacity and architecture mismatch, limited or private data for distillation, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and reliably preserving long-tail behaviors under compression.

papers_seen.author: Garrett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational structure, and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization) and with data- or curriculum-driven strategies. Across vision, language, generative models, and policy settings, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory; however, it has clear limits related to capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors and biases, data availability, and optimization instability. Real-world deployment therefore treats KD as a configurable engineering toolkit rather than a single recipe, combining careful choice of transfer signals, teacher–student alignment, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, multi-faceted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in both vision and natural language processing. Modern KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft output distributions, intermediate representations, and relational structure—and is often integrated with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to map teacher and student architectures, which data or synthetic samples to use, and when to apply multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules. Remaining challenges include optimization difficulties that limit exact matching, teacher–student mismatch under domain shift or heterogeneity (e.g., federated settings), and the need to preserve robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behaviors in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Lynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and an Integrated Roadmap
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers behavior at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals) and can both improve efficiency and provide additional benefits such as domain adaptation, privacy-aware training, and interpretability. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on aligning teacher and student capacity and architecture, on data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized), and on combining distillation with complementary compression primitives to preserve robustness and rare-case behavior. Treating KD as the central element of an integrated compression pipeline—with deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students, and when to combine other methods—achieves the best practical trade-offs for deployment.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: A Central, Practical Tool with Clear Limits and Engineering Requirements
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for producing compact, deployable deep models by transferring information from larger teachers to smaller students. Empirical work across vision, speech, ranking, and natural language tasks shows KD can deliver large reductions in parameter count and latency while retaining much of a teacher’s predictive power. However, KD is not an automatic solution: its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how the teacher is prepared, student architecture and pretraining, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires engineering KD into a broader compression pipeline that addresses data, robustness, fairness, and optimization concerns.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current Practices, Mechanisms, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other learned structure. Across vision and natural language processing, KD has become a flexible toolkit—combining logits/soft-targets, feature- or layer-level matching, data-side strategies (augmented or synthetic data), and architecture-aware student design—to produce compact models that often recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. Empirical work demonstrates meaningful efficiency gains in settings ranging from BERT compression to non-autoregressive translation, but success depends on choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or mismatched data. Practical deployment benefits from combining KD with complementary compression (architecture search, pruning, quantization) and from addressing optimization, privacy, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Paradigm for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: when treated as a broad training paradigm it enables compact, robust, and deployable models across modalities and tasks. By integrating logit-level guidance, intermediate feature transfer, architecture-aware projectors, adaptive teacher selection, data- and domain-aware strategies, and robustness-aware objectives, KD pipelines can produce students that approach teacher performance while satisfying latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success requires designing what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous components, and how to shape inputs and curricula for the student—rather than relying on a single generic distillation recipe.

papers_seen.author: Ramsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Conditional Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep and NLP models. When integrated into compression pipelines it reliably reduces latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of teacher performance. However, distillation’s benefits are conditional: success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, and mitigation of propagated teacher errors or biases. A pragmatic KD-centered workflow composes multiple distilled signals, architecture-aware alignment, complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free methods) to produce robust, production-ready students.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: a Position and Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core of model compression for deep learning and NLP: it is the most flexible, task-aware mechanism for transferring a teacher’s predictive behavior and internal structure into a deployable student. KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), appropriate signal selection (logits, features, relations), and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free samples). However, KD is not a universal panacea — its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and careful handling of robustness and fairness concerns. Thus, engineering KD as a configurable, multi-stage pipeline that integrates representation-level objectives, data-aware protocols, and complementary compression primitives offers the best route to reliable, real-world model compression.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for shrinking large models into a principled and versatile toolkit for compressing, adapting, and scaling deep models in NLP. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure from a teacher to a student, KD enables high-quality, resource-efficient models that meet latency and capacity constraints while preserving task performance. Recent work demonstrates KD variants that are task-adaptive, layer-aware, many-to-many, online, and even teacher-free, making KD applicable across domain adaptation, multi-tasking, multimodality, and large-scale distributed training. This paper argues that KD should be viewed not merely as a compression trick but as a unifying framework that links theoretical insights, practical training strategies, and system-level considerations for deploying compact NLP models.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Cornerstone of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for transferring soft targets into a unifying toolkit that enables model compression, deployment on constrained devices, privacy-aware release, and modality transfer. By combining architectural mapping, contrastive and adversarial objectives, and data-free or federated setups, KD can preserve much of a teacher model's performance while drastically reducing footprint and computation. This makes KD essential for translating state-of-the-art large models into real-world, resource-limited, and privacy-sensitive applications.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central but Complementary Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible method for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure, and combined with data strategies and other compression primitives—KD enables substantial reductions in latency and footprint while retaining much of teacher performance. Real-world success depends on careful teacher–student alignment, appropriate distillation signals and data, and explicit handling of limits such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred biases. I argue KD should be the default core of compression pipelines but must be used deliberately and in combination with complementary methods to meet deployment, robustness, and fairness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Johnston
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task‑Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. Treated as a configurable toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD enables strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy when its objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives are chosen to match task and deployment constraints. At the same time, KD has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, data or domain shift, and propagation of teacher artifacts—that must be mitigated through careful design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Beyond Compression: Roles, Limits, and Best Practices for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly framed as a route to compress large models into smaller deployable students, but its benefits and pitfalls extend well beyond mere parameter reduction. KD acts as a form of learned regularization, can be applied in self-distillation and teacher-free regimes, and enables transferring properties such as robustness, privacy-preserving signals, and task-specific intermediate knowledge. At the same time, KD faces optimization and representation-mismatch challenges and can propagate undesirable biases from teacher to student. This paper argues that practitioners should treat KD as a flexible toolbox: combine soft-label supervision with internal-representation matching, flexible layer-mapping, attention-guided feature alignment, and targeted interventions for fairness, privacy, and robustness to get consistent benefits in both vision and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Methods, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or costly models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade shows multiple complementary mechanisms for effective distillation—soft-target supervision, feature and representation mimicking, layer-wise alignment, and task-aware selection of teacher knowledge. Practical advances adapt distillation to domain constraints (few-shot data, modality mismatch, federated or latency-constrained deployment) and model families (transformers, convolutional nets, graph neural networks, generative models). Empirical work demonstrates that thoughtful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features vs. relations), how to align layers, and how to prepare data and pretraining substantially affect student performance, sometimes enabling students to match or even surpass teachers under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hayden
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Central, Practical, but Task‑Aware and Complementary
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Its flexibility—transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure—explains wide empirical success across vision, language, and graph domains. However, KD is not a universal solution: student capacity, choice of distillation signals, availability and provenance of data, and inherited teacher biases or errors constrain outcomes. Reliable deployment therefore treats KD as a core component within an integrated compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, data strategies (including privacy- or data-free variants), and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Mccall
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods include matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, transferring relational structure, and using multi-teacher or self-distillation schedules. In practice, KD is most effective when integrated into a compression pipeline that includes student-aware pretraining or adaptation, data selection or synthesis, and complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. The effectiveness of KD depends on careful teacher–student co-design, appropriate distillation signals, and strategies for limited or private data; persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift and robustness, privacy and federated settings, and the risk of propagating teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Settings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing deep models in latency- or resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from larger “teacher” models or ensembles to smaller “student” models. Work in this area spans methods that match final outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure; approaches that adapt teacher signals through meta-learning or task-aware filters; and specializations for settings such as vision–language, graph learning, federated or distributed training, and data-free scenarios. Empirical results show KD can yield large efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success depends on handling domain shift, architectural mismatch, heterogeneous data and devices, and the quality or calibration of teacher outputs. Important theoretical and statistical analyses have begun to clarify when and why distillation helps, but open problems remain around robust, privacy-preserving, and architecture-agnostic distillation for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Central, Practical, but Conditional
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD operates at multiple levels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational signals) and is most effective when integrated with complementary practices such as pre-training, architecture-aware design, data-side strategies, and other compression techniques. However, its success is conditional on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or mismatched data, and how to mitigate propagation of teacher errors or biases. Treating KD as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe yields the best results for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques convert large, accurate neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for constrained inference environments. Approaches vary from transferring soft-label outputs to aligning intermediate representations, progressively replacing modules, augmenting or synthesizing data during teacher–student training, and compressing ensembles. Empirical results across speech, language, vision, and graph tasks show that well-designed distillation can preserve most of a teacher's performance while reducing parameter count and inference cost; task-adaptive compression and careful design of teacher–student interactions (including training teachers to be student-friendly) further improve student effectiveness. Practical choices—what to distill (logits, features, or structure), how to align mismatched architectures, and how to augment data or leverage ensembles—determine final trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies condense large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision students suitable for deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. Research has produced a taxonomy of approaches—soft-target (logit) supervision, intermediate/feature imitation, relational or attention-based losses, multi-teacher fusion, data-free and zero-shot protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work demonstrates that properly designed distillation pipelines can preserve most teacher performance across vision and language tasks while enabling substantial gains in inference speed and memory; theoretical analyses attribute much of KD’s benefit to regularization from soft targets and the transfer of inductive biases. Remaining challenges include handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, preserving robustness and fine-grained behaviors, operating without original training data, and designing adaptive, task-aware distillation signals.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practice, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transforms large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. Modern KD is a multi-signal, task-aware toolkit that includes soft-target/logit matching, intermediate feature and attention alignment, relational or contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation schedules, and data-side strategies (original-data, augmented, synthetic, or data-free). In practice KD is combined with complementary compression primitives—pruning, quantization, or architecture search—and benefits from pretraining or architecture-aware student design. While KD routinely preserves much of teacher utility in applied settings, reliable transfer of rare-event behavior, robustness under distribution shift, principled teacher selection, and privacy-sensitive deployment remain active challenges that guide current research and engineering practice.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Takeaways
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-faceted toolkit for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy) while retaining much of task performance. KD methods include soft-target (logit) matching, alignment of intermediate representations, attention- or relation-based objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free strategies. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation recipe is tailored to student capacity, data regime, and downstream robustness or fairness requirements. Open problems include reliable distillation without original data, principled handling of teacher errors and biases, and transferring robustness and rare-behavior performance to compact students.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-driven family of techniques for converting large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster students suitable for constrained inference. KD methods transfer information at multiple levels—from softened output distributions to intermediate representations, attention and relational patterns—and are routinely combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). Empirical work across vision, language, speech, and 3D tasks shows that well-designed distillation pipelines can retain most teacher utility while substantially reducing parameter count and inference cost; however, practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, architecture alignment, and explicit handling of robustness, long-tail behaviors, and potential bias propagation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, modular approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has evolved from softened-logit matching to a multifaceted toolkit that transfers information at output, representation, and relational levels; supports single, ensemble, self- and multi-teacher workflows; and composes with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical success depends on deliberate choices about which teacher signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures and capacities, what data or augmentations to use (including synthesized or data-free inputs), and how to evaluate robustness, fairness, and privacy. When embedded in a task-aware, pipeline-oriented process, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher utility, but predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, domain shift, teacher errors, and risks to calibration or fairness) require additional safeguards and complementary techniques.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible pathway to convert large, high-performing deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates at multiple levels (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure) and can be combined with complementary compression techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture-aware surgery to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its empirical strengths include preserving much of teacher performance while enabling large efficiency gains; its limitations arise from teacher–student mismatch, data availability constraints, possible propagation of teacher defects, and robustness or fairness trade-offs. Effective deployment treats KD as the core of a hybrid compression toolkit and requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align layers and capacities, how to handle scarce or private data, and when to combine KD with low-precision numerics or structured pruning.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single training trick into a central, flexible toolkit for producing smaller, faster, and deployable models across vision and language. KD methods transfer information from large teacher models to compact students via multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational mappings) and are most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task‑aware design. Practical success depends on deliberate teacher selection, alignment of teacher and student capacity/architecture, data strategies (including data augmentation or data‑free protocols), and explicit evaluation for robustness, rare or out‑of‑domain behaviors, and privacy considerations. papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective mechanism for producing compact models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while retaining much of the original performance. When treated as the central component of a compression pipeline and adapted to task needs—by choosing appropriate distillation signals, pretraining students, leveraging multi-teacher or staged schedules, and addressing data or rare-token issues—KD yields reliable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. However, its benefits are conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data alignment, and safeguards against propagated errors; therefore KD should be the default starting point for compression, used together with complementary techniques and evaluation practices to ensure robustness in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Evidence, Limits, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, practical toolkit for converting large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and NLP. A diverse set of distillation signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure), combined with data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation), architecture-aware mappings, and staged or multi-teacher schedules, routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has well-documented limits: it can propagate teacher errors or biases, struggle under domain shift or data scarcity, and fail to preserve fine-grained or low-frequency behaviors without targeted interventions. Best practice treats KD as a composable pipeline—integrating representation-level objectives, careful data design, teacher selection, and complementary compression techniques—to achieve robust, task-aware compression.
