papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hubbard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure) and routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs. However, KD alone cannot guarantee robustness, fairness, or optimal hardware utilization: reliable deployment requires task-aware choices about what to distill, how to align teachers and students, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. I argue KD should be treated as the central component of a multi-tool compression pipeline—indispensable in practice but conditional on careful system-level design to meet production constraints and mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD works at multiple levels — soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, and ensemble behaviour — and is most effective when combined with data strategies, teacher–student co-design, and complementary compression such as pruning or quantization. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance and can regularize student training, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align capacities, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; careful, task-aware protocols are therefore essential for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modular approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a design problem—choosing which signals to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data and capacity constraints—KD can produce compact models that retain much of a teacher's performance. Success is conditional: data availability, teacher quality, architecture mismatch, robustness, and long-tail behaviors impose limits that require hybrid pipelines and careful method choices.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable toolkit—choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data or synthesis strategies to use—KD frequently yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss. Its practical success depends on pairing distillation with complementary compression methods, careful data and curriculum design, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness; KD is therefore best used as the core of hybrid compression pipelines rather than a universal, one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a practical toolkit for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The toolkit includes soft-output (logit) matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational and contrastive objectives, data-side interventions (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free protocols), and hybrid pipelines that combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Empirical work shows that well-designed distillation frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance, but success depends on careful teacher–student pairing, signal selection, data strategies, and attention to capacity, robustness, and distribution-shift failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students in both deep learning and NLP. KD is not a single recipe but a modular toolkit: practitioners must choose what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and which complementary compression methods to combine. When designed as a system and tuned for task and deployment constraints, KD reliably yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Methods, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational signals from teachers. KD includes diverse techniques — soft-target supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, layer-mapping strategies, online and ensemble-to-single transfers, and selective sample or data-aware procedures — that are adapted to task, architecture, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and appropriate data strategies, KD can yield compact models that retain most teacher performance; however, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student compatibility, and data availability.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, System-Level Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary, system-level strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into compact, deployable students. When KD is designed as a modular pipeline—combining soft-target supervision, intermediate-representation matching, selective data strategies, multi-teacher aggregation, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture surgery)—it reliably produces small models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of transferred biases and domain shifts. Practical deployments therefore require principled choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data strategies to apply.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical paradigm for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching softened teacher outputs to a rich toolkit that transfers logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, and inductive biases; it is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies that range from using original training sets to synthetic or data-free approaches. Empirical work shows KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while substantially reducing inference cost, but its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and initialization, the choice of distillation targets and layer mappings, and how data constraints and robustness/fairness concerns are handled. Remaining research directions center on principled layer alignment, preserving rare-token and safety-critical behaviors, data-free distillation, and fairness/robustness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core and a Bounded Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with task-aware objectives, intermediate representation alignment, appropriate data strategies (including synthetic-data approaches), and architecture-aware design, KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance and enable deployment in resource-constrained or heterogeneous environments. However, KD has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, propagation of teacher errors, and optimization fragility—that demand complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful protocol design to realize reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and accelerates large neural models by transferring information from one or more teacher models into a smaller student. Across vision and language, KD variants extend from logit-matching to feature- and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher ensembling, online/co-distillation, privacy-aware and federated setups, and combinations with quantization or structured pruning. Practical pipelines combine KD with architecture-aware transformations, domain adaptation, and task-specific pretraining to obtain compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Despite empirical success across modalities and deployment settings, trade-offs remain in teacher selection, information type to transfer, stability for heterogeneous architectures, and theoretical interpretation of what is transferred; these motivate further research into adaptive teacher weighting, feature alignment layers, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi‑ingredient approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The KD toolkit includes softened-output (logit) supervision, intermediate representation and attention matching, relational objectives, multi- and self-distillation, and data strategies that range from augmentation to data-free synthesis. When integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with careful teacher–student design and data selection, KD often produces compact models that recover most of the teacher’s performance. Remaining limitations arise from capacity mismatch, limited or private data, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and sensitivity to domain shift and rare-token behaviors; practical pipelines therefore favor multi-objective distillation, tailored data strategies, and explicit robustness or privacy interventions.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. It reliably reduces parameter counts and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with task-aware design choices and complementary compression techniques. However, distillation’s success is conditional on choices about what to transfer (logits, representations, relations), how to align teacher and student architectures, access to data or synthetic surrogates, and mitigation of optimization, robustness, and fairness failure modes. Effective deployment therefore treats distillation as a toolkit—combined with pre-training, data augmentation, and other compression primitives—rather than a single one-size-fits-all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical paradigm for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is effective because it is multifaceted: it can transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational or structural signals, and ensemble knowledge; it works with or without access to original training data; and it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies. However, KD’s benefits are conditional — success requires matched objectives, sensible student preparation, careful handling of imperfect teachers and data limitations, and attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift. Framing KD as a system-level toolkit rather than a single recipe yields the most reliable path to compact, performant models across modalities and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Conditional Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods — from soft-target logit matching to feature- and relation-level transfer, multi- and self-distillation, and data-free or synthetic-data protocols — have repeatedly enabled substantial reductions in parameter count and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: predictable failure modes (student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy limits, and transfer of teacher errors or biases) mean KD must be engineered as part of an integrated compression pipeline that selects appropriate distillation signals, aligns architectures, adopts data strategies, and pairs KD with complementary compression primitives and rigorous deployment evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile tool for transferring functionality from large, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones across modalities. When properly applied, KD can enable deployment of compact models with competitive accuracy, but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, selection of distilled signals, and complementary compression strategies. This paper synthesizes empirical findings and method-level advances to argue for principled, task-aware KD workflows that mitigate common pitfalls while maximizing compression gains.

papers_seen.author: Richardson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, multi-signal approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a flexible toolbox, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and can operate with original, augmented, synthesized, or data-free inputs. Empirical and methodological work shows KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs when paired with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware student preparation. Responsible deployment requires explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data provenance and scarcity, and robustness and fairness evaluation, so KD should be treated as the central element of a broader, design-sensitive compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deploying large pretrained models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students. Methods include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate features or attention maps, layer- and task-aware alignment, online and mutual distillation, and data-free approaches that synthesize surrogate inputs. Empirical evidence across vision and language tasks shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size, latency, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Remaining challenges center on preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior in sequence models, avoiding transfer of biases or adversarial vulnerabilities, and jointly optimizing compression for hardware and task constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed to match student capacity, task requirements, and available data, distillation reliably reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Its practical success depends on selecting appropriate distilled signals (logits, features, relations), combining KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, architecture search, quantization), and addressing open problems such as data scarcity, teacher error transfer, and robustness across distributions.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multi-faceted, practical strategy for producing compact models from larger teachers in deep learning and NLP. Across many tasks and modalities, KD can transfer information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention patterns, relational structure) and is most effective when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture design, pruning, quantization, and appropriate data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic). Empirical evidence shows KD often recovers much of teacher performance while enabling substantial gains in latency and deployability, but predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and challenges when original data are unavailable—require targeted mitigations. Practical recommendations center on matching distilled signals to student capacity and architecture, using projectors or layer mappings to align representations, combining KD with complementary compression primitives, and applying privacy-aware or data-free techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Butler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Composable Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible method for producing compact neural models from larger teachers. KD supplies multiple transferable signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational patterns) and, when combined with complementary compression primitives and careful data and architecture choices, enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD alone does not eliminate capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, data scarcity, or robustness and fairness risks; reliable compression therefore treats KD as the central component of a broader, task‑aware pipeline that includes explicit evaluation and mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods form a flexible toolkit to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, and generative settings, practitioners use softened outputs, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher schedules, online co-distillation, and data-aware or data-free procedures. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data availability or privacy constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Remaining challenges include capacity and optimization gaps, propagation of teacher errors or biases, robustness under adversarial or domain shift, and principled teacher selection. This synthesis summarizes common methods, empirical findings, practical tradeoffs, and recommended design patterns for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students in both deep learning and NLP. KD is not a single recipe but a modular toolkit: practitioners must choose what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and which complementary compression methods to combine. When designed as a system and tuned for task and deployment constraints, KD reliably yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. The literature documents a spectrum of KD objectives (soft-output matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational losses), protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi-teacher, and teacher-free), and data strategies (original-data distillation, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, architecture heterogeneity, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can retain much of a teacher’s performance across modalities, but persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Hubbard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure) and routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs. However, KD alone cannot guarantee robustness, fairness, or optimal hardware utilization: reliable deployment requires task-aware choices about what to distill, how to align teachers and students, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. I argue KD should be treated as the central component of a multi-tool compression pipeline—indispensable in practice but conditional on careful system-level design to meet production constraints and mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of task performance. KD operates through multiple transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational/attention structure), and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods, careful teacher–student design, and data strategies that reflect deployment constraints. Empirical practice and reviews show KD’s utility across modalities and tasks, while also exposing limitations such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, degraded rare-token behaviors, and sensitivity to domain shift—motivating pipeline-oriented, design-sensitive approaches for reliable compression.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deployment of high-performing but large neural models in resource-constrained settings by transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. Research has developed a spectrum of approaches — from matching logits to feature-level imitation, structural transformation of architectures, multi-teacher schemes, and task-specific adaptations — and has applied them across domains including detection, generative modeling, recommendation, retrieval, and multiple NLP tasks. Empirical work highlights both opportunities (substantial parameter reductions, faster inference, retained or modestly degraded accuracy) and pitfalls (propagation of teacher errors, sensitivity to data heterogeneity, robustness concerns), motivating targeted algorithmic adjustments such as selective distillation, projector modules, and adversarially-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Jennings
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, high‑leverage approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central, task‑aware toolkit and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), appropriate data strategies, and careful teacher–student alignment, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, KD’s practical success is conditional on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to handle limited or mismatched data, how to align capacities and architectures, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as propagation of teacher errors, capacity mismatch, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses large teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD is a multifaceted toolkit—covering soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, relational objectives, and online or multi-teacher schedules—and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and appropriate data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized). Practical deployment requires careful teacher–student alignment, deliberate selection of distillation signals, attention to data provenance and domain shift, and targeted evaluation of robustness, long-tail behaviors, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across multiple signal levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational structure) and is most effective when embedded in hybrid, task-aware pipelines that include student pretraining, architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic). Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data and distributional shifts, and explicitly evaluating robustness and fairness; several recurring open problems remain in capacity mismatch, data-free distillation, and preserving long-tail or safety-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Huang
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used engineering framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has grown from softened-logits matching to a multifaceted toolbox that transfers output behavior, intermediate representations, and relational structure; it is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. KD’s practical effectiveness depends on task- and capacity-aware design choices, careful management of distillation data (including synthetic or data-free strategies when needed), and explicit evaluation of robustness, rare-behavior preservation, and potential bias transfer. While KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs, predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or domain-specific artifacts, and degraded long-tail behavior—necessitate pipeline-level mitigations and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature has expanded beyond soft-label matching to include intermediate representation imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and adaptive-teacher schemes, data- and domain-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve a large fraction of teacher performance across vision and language tasks, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when distillation helps, how teacher quality and data regimes affect outcomes, and what practical trade-offs remain. Open problems center on robustness to domain shift and adversaries, distillation without original data, and automated, architecture-agnostic pipelines for production systems.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. It can transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, structured relational signals, or ensemble knowledge, and supports data-side strategies including data-free and augmentation-aware schemes. In practice, KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance when its formulation is matched to task constraints, data availability, and student capacity. However, distillation alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or privacy-preserving compression: practitioner success hinges on selecting appropriate distillation signals, addressing teacher–student and data mismatches, and combining KD with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure). Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple logit matching to a toolkit that includes feature- and attention-level imitation, relational objectives, multi- and reinforced multi-teacher strategies, data-free and augmentation-driven protocols, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architectures, and how to handle data availability and distributional shifts. Important limitations remain—propagation of teacher errors or biases, degraded rare- or out-of-domain behavior, and data- or privacy-constrained regimes—which motivate targeted algorithmic and data strategies to make distillation reliable in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Buchanan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a modular pipeline, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational objectives, and other signals, and is routinely combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic). Empirical work across speech, vision, and language shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while dramatically reducing size and inference cost, but its success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and distribution, architecture alignment, and careful optimization. Practical deployment therefore relies on task-aware design choices, staged schedules, and integrations (e.g., data-free distillation or multi-signal objectives) to mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and fragility under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Richardson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, task-aware toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and structured-data domains. The core idea is to transfer predictive behavior or internal structure from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student via multiple possible signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure). In practice, KD is most effective when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that aligns teacher and student capacity, chooses distillation targets and data strategies to match deployment constraints, and pairs distillation with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). Common failure modes include teacher–student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or heterogeneous data provenance, propagation of teacher errors and biases, and degraded robustness under distribution shift; these motivate practical remedies such as multi-teacher schemes, student pre-training, synthetic or data-free distillation, and targeted evaluation for robustness and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, modality-agnostic approach that enables conversion of large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When treated as a composable toolkit—combining soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, relational or structural signals, data augmentation/synthesis, and multi-stage teacher–student schedules—KD yields compact models that retain much of the teacher's effectiveness. Real-world success requires attention to teacher quality, data provenance, architecture alignment, and safeguards for robustness and fairness; with these design choices, KD is a practical backbone for deploying efficient deep learning and NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core of Model Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to which teacher signals are transferred, how the student is initialized, and how complementary compression methods are integrated, KD reliably reduces inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a magic bullet: theoretical and empirical work highlights optimization gaps, failures under heterogeneous data or federated settings, and robustness and rare-token fidelity issues. Realistic deployment therefore requires task-aware distillation recipes, student pre-training, data strategies (including data-free synthesis when necessary), and explicit evaluation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Pathways for Compressing Large NLP Models: Pre-train the Student, Distill Carefully, and Guard for Data & Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach to compress large deep learning models for NLP and related tasks. When the student model is itself pre-trained, distillation yields especially strong and consistent gains; complementary methods — including data augmentation during distillation, progressive module replacement, ensemble teachers or teacher adaptation, and data-free or privacy-aware distillation — address common deployment constraints such as limited task data, inference cost, data access, and adversarial robustness. Combining these techniques and choosing distillation targets and schedules with theoretical and empirical guidance yields compact models that retain much of the original performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression: A Conditional, Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible, modality-agnostic approach to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as the default starting point for compression, KD provides multiple complementary signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) that—when matched to student capacity and combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—produce strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, KD is not universally sufficient: practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, data availability and provenance, domain shift, teacher errors, and robustness/fairness constraints. A pragmatic compression pipeline therefore places KD at its center but integrates pretraining, architecture adaptation, data-aware distillation schedules, and explicit evaluation and mitigation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured beyond a single recipe for copying soft labels: it is a flexible set of techniques that address model compression, domain and task transfer, privacy-constrained scenarios, distributed training, and continual learning. Practical KD variants operate at different levels (logits, features, layers), use data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are unavailable, and adapt training schedules to the target application. When chosen to match the constraints of the deployment setting—data availability, compute budget, task type, and model architecture—KD consistently enables smaller or more specialized students to approach or sometimes exceed teacher performance while offering operational benefits such as faster inference, lower memory, and more reproducible training.
