Across vision and language applications, KD is typically integrated into broader compression pipelines that include pretraining of compact students, pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware redesign. Practical success depends on matching the distillation signals and data strategy to student capacity and deployment constraints; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, limited or private data, and degraded robustness under distribution shift. Effective deployment treats KD as a configurable, task-aware toolkit rather than a single recipe, combining appropriate transfer objectives, teacher–student alignment, and careful empirical evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

KD is a flexible toolkit—transferring softened outputs, internal representations, attention, or relational signals—that delivers strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs when combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful teacher–student co-design, and appropriate data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized). Practical deployment requires explicit handling of capacity mismatch, transferred biases, robustness under distribution shift, and privacy constraints; when treated as a modular pipeline rather than a single recipe, KD reliably enables compact models suited to real-world constraints.

papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), aligning inputs and architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression (pruning, structured sparsity, quantization) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic samples, curriculum)—KD enables resource-efficient deployment across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings. However, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student; addressing these constraints through multi-teacher designs, black-box adaptation, and feature-level alignment remains essential for robust, private, and high-performance compression.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relations. A variety of KD objectives—matching teacher logits (soft targets), aligning features or attention maps, transferring relational or contrastive structure, and self- or multi-teacher schemes—have been adapted across vision, language, multimodal, and structured prediction tasks. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data to use or synthesize for distillation. Although KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, open challenges remain including optimization hardness, propagation of teacher errors, domain and device heterogeneity, data- or privacy-constrained settings, and preserving robustness under distributional shift. Effective deployment commonly combines KD with complementary techniques (pre-training students, pruning, quantization, or data augmentation) and task-aware design choices.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured beyond a single recipe for copying soft labels: it is a flexible set of techniques that address model compression, domain and task transfer, privacy-constrained scenarios, distributed training, and continual learning. Practical KD variants operate at different levels (logits, features, layers), use data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are unavailable, and adapt training schedules to the target application. When chosen to match the constraints of the deployment setting—data availability, compute budget, task type, and model architecture—KD consistently enables smaller or more specialized students to approach or sometimes exceed teacher performance while offering operational benefits such as faster inference, lower memory, and more reproducible training.

papers_seen.author: Glass
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure). KD is most effective when treated as a component of a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness. Empirical and theoretical work show distilled students often recover a substantial fraction of teacher performance, but success hinges on teacher–student capacity alignment, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and targeted mitigation of failure modes such as propagation of teacher errors, domain shift, and loss of rare or safety-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Empirical, Theoretical, and Practical Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools to reduce the size and latency of large deep models while retaining much of their performance. Research has produced a diverse set of KD variants — offline teacher-student distillation, multi-teacher and two-stage schemes, online/distillation-in-training, self-distillation, and combinations with pruning — and has demonstrated practical impact across NLP (e.g., translation, question answering, language modeling) and other domains. Work has also begun to explain when and why distillation helps, pointing to effects on data complexity, bias–variance tradeoffs, and the distribution of learned representations across network layers. Implementation-oriented studies emphasize efficient pipelines (to avoid repeated teacher forward passes), dataset-level filtering, and the complementary role of structured pruning for deployment on constrained hardware. Together, these findings show KD is both a pragmatic engineering tool and a growing subject of theoretical understanding, with ongoing research addressing teacher imperfection, optimal training signal mixes, and scalability to very large datasets or distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a logits-matching trick into a broad set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large neural teachers. Modern KD variants transfer soft predictions, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structure; they are combined with data-centric practices (augmentation, synthetic and zero-shot data) and complementary compression (pruning, architecture search) to meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains in NLP (notably transformer compression) as well as vision, graphs, and federated settings, while theoretical and empirical studies reveal optimization challenges, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and distributional/heterogeneity limitations. Practical pipelines favor pretraining or progressive replacement, representation-level matching, task-adaptive data strategies, and awareness of privacy and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Bailey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a configurable core of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful data practices (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation), KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs. Its reliability in production depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and architecture, adopting appropriate data strategies, and explicitly monitoring limits such as transferred teacher errors, degraded robustness under distribution shift, and harms to rare-token or long-tail behavior. Consequently, KD should be the default starting point for compression efforts, but only as part of engineered, task-aware pipelines that mitigate its conditional risks.

papers_seen.author: Strickland
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically effective family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, speech, and generative tasks, KD reduces inference cost and memory and can preserve much of teacher performance when combined with architecture-aware design, representation-level supervision, and complementary compression primitives. Practical application of KD requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, what distillation data to use (real, augmented, or synthetic), and how to evaluate robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behavior. While KD enables many deployment scenarios — including on-device, privacy-sensitive, and federated settings — its limitations (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, data mismatch, and occasional failure on rare behaviors) motivate integrated, task-aware pipelines rather than one-shot application.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Bender
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, adaptable approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, multimodal, generative, and federated settings. KD works through multiple channels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals—and is most effective when matched to student capacity, the available data, and deployment constraints. Treated as a core element of a broader compression pipeline (including pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies), KD regularly preserves much of teacher utility while delivering substantial improvements in latency, memory, and deployability. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on careful selection of teacher signals, architecture alignment, handling of limited or private data, and mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, and transfer of teacher biases. Practical deployment therefore requires task-aware distillation recipes, data-aware strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches), and complementary compression or federated adaptations to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When framed as a composable pipeline—choosing which teacher signals to transfer, aligning architectures, managing or synthesizing distillation data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and domain-shifted inputs. Best practice treats KD as one essential component of a broader, task-aware compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Klein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task‑Aware Hybrid Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, modality-agnostic technique that reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of a teacher model's performance when applied thoughtfully. KD is most effective when treated as the central element of a broader, task-aware compression pipeline that includes representation alignment, architecture-aware design, and complementary methods such as pruning and quantization. Success requires explicit attention to student capacity, data strategies, and robust evaluation under domain shift and safety constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring information from a teacher model. Across computer vision, language, graph, and healthcare applications, KD variants augment or replace naive logit matching with feature/hint matching, data augmentation, layer mapping strategies, and data-free or privacy-aware mechanisms. Practical work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment for pre-trained transformers, and the use of synthetic or mixed inputs to improve student generalization. At the same time, theoretical and empirical studies highlight limitations under data heterogeneity and imperfect teachers, motivating hybrid losses that mix soft and hard labels and methods that control privacy leakage during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to convert large, accurate models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what teacher signals to transfer, aligning mismatched architectures, and addressing data constraints—KD can preserve most teacher performance while enabling orders-of-magnitude improvements in latency, memory footprint, and deployability. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on representations transferred, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data, and deployment constraints such as privacy or distributed training. Effective compression therefore treats KD as a core tool within a broader toolkit that includes feature-level alignment, data-aware strategies, online or multi-teacher setups, and data-free techniques when real data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured relationships. Across deep learning and NLP, KD enables deployment of performant models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align teacher and student architectures, the availability and design of distillation data (real, augmented, or synthetic), and training protocols that mitigate capacity and distribution mismatches. Open challenges include robust teacher selection, data- and domain-mismatch, and scaling distillation methods to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive deployments.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Escobar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: A Conditional, Pipeline‑Level Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, composable element of practical model‑compression workflows: it reliably transfers useful predictive structure from large teachers into smaller, deployable students when its signals, data, and capacity assumptions are chosen deliberately. However, KD is not a universal fix—its benefits are conditional on student capacity, data availability and provenance, and explicit handling of failure modes such as propagation of teacher errors, long‑tail/rare‑token degradation, and distributional shift. A pragmatic approach is to make KD the backbone of a compression pipeline while combining it with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design), task‑aware signal selection, and targeted evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Simmons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade‑offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of methods for transferring useful behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, ranking, and reading-comprehension tasks, practitioners use softened output matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational objectives, multi- and self-teaching schedules, and data-aware or data-free procedures. KD is most effective when distillation signals, student capacity, and data strategies are chosen together and when KD is combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Important open problems include closing capacity and optimization gaps, avoiding propagation of teacher errors or biases, preserving robustness under domain or adversarial shifts, and designing principled teacher selection and data-synthesis strategies.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task-Aware Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best viewed not as a single algorithm but as a multifaceted, task-aware toolbox that enables practical model compression across modalities. When used thoughtfully—selecting what signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student architectures, choosing or synthesizing distillation data, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search)—KD produces compact students that often preserve most of a teacher’s performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing these gains requires explicit attention to teacher imperfections, capacity gaps, domain or data mismatch, and deployment constraints; addressing those concerns with multi-teacher schedules, data-agnostic generators, curriculum/annealing strategies, and interpretable or task-adaptive student designs yields the most reliable outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System-Level, Task-Aware Tool for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system—combining careful choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including data-free generation), and complementary compression primitives—KD reliably preserves much of teacher utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal cure: effectiveness depends on student capacity, data regime, and teacher quality, and distillation can propagate teacher errors or degrade robustness unless paired with careful evaluation and complementary interventions. I argue KD should be used as a task-aware, pipeline-level component of compression workflows rather than a single recipe, and I outline practical recommendations that follow from recent empirical and methodological advances.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, multi-level approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information ranging from softened output distributions to intermediate representations and relational structure. Across vision and language applications, KD is typically integrated into broader compression pipelines that include pretraining of compact students, pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware redesign. Practical success depends on matching the distillation signals and data strategy to student capacity and deployment constraints; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, limited or private data, and degraded robustness under distribution shift. Effective deployment treats KD as a configurable, task-aware toolkit rather than a single recipe, combining appropriate transfer objectives, teacher–student alignment, and careful empirical evaluation.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural relationships. Methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate features or attention, synthesizing surrogate training data when originals are unavailable, and designing architecture-aware layer mappings. KD is often combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and used across modalities (vision, language, generative models) to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and mitigation of failure modes such as teacher–student capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and propagation of biases.

papers_seen.author: Cole
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Aware Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as an integrated component of a compression pipeline and paired with complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies), KD frequently delivers strong efficiency–performance tradeoffs. However, its effectiveness depends on task- and student-aware choices about what signals to transfer, how to manage distillation data, and how to mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, degraded rare‑token behavior, teacher errors, and robustness or fairness concerns. I argue that KD should be the default engine in compression workflows but must be used with careful, context‑dependent design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, practical toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep models across vision and natural language tasks. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning internal representations, leveraging multi-teacher or online schedules, and using data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). When combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods, KD often yields students that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges center on teacher–student mismatch, data availability, robustness, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for transferring capabilities from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. A broad toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning internal representations or attention maps, relational objectives, multi-teacher/online schedules, and data-centric strategies including data-free synthesis—enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success requires aligning distillation signals to student capacity, selecting appropriate data and augmentation strategies, combining KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), and explicitly addressing limits such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, distributional shift, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Bennett
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted collection of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD combines output-level supervision with internal-representation matching and data strategies to produce compact models that retain much of the teacher’s effectiveness while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data or synthesis methods, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives and careful evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful but Incomplete
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible and practical set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. It supports multiple transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and integrates naturally with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). When KD is treated as the central element of a task-aware compression pipeline — i.e., when the distillation recipe is matched to data availability, student capacity, architecture heterogeneity, and deployment constraints — it yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. Nevertheless, distillation alone does not guarantee robustness, fairness, or preservation of low-frequency behaviors in language tasks; careful design choices, data strategies, and combination with other compression primitives are required for reliable production deployment.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Design‑Sensitive Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models from larger teachers. Treated as a modular, design‑sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer different kinds of information (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), be adapted to constrained data regimes (including data‑free or synthetic data), and compose with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) to produce deployable students. KD has predictable failure modes—capacity mismatch, transfer of teacher errors, and sensitivity to distribution shift—that demand explicit engineering choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness. When KD is embedded in a broader compression pipeline and tuned to student capacity and deployment constraints, it reliably yields favorable tradeoffs between efficiency and performance.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Strengths, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—selecting what knowledge to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and integrating complementary compression methods and data strategies—KD typically yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss and can provide implicit regularization and improved calibration. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: it faces predictable failure modes (student capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, and transfer of teacher errors or biases) that require task-aware design choices and evaluation. This paper argues KD should be the central, composable element of modern compression pipelines while highlighting practical adjustments to make distillation reliable in real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a family of techniques that transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and data constraints. KD is not a single algorithm but a design-sensitive toolkit: practitioners choose what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, what data to use or synthesize, and which complementary compression methods to combine. When these design choices are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints, KD frequently produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance; however, several open problems remain, including propagation of teacher errors (notably on rare or low-frequency phenomena), robustness under distributional shift, and principled distillation when data are limited or private.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a set of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students) so the students retain much of the teacher utility while fitting deployment constraints. Research has produced a variety of distillation paradigms: logit- and soft-target matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise and channel-wise alignment, progressive module replacement, self-supervised distillation, multi-teacher ensembles and domain-aware adaptation. Empirical work shows that combining pre-training for compact architectures with distillation, using task-aware selection of teacher signals, and tailoring distillation to modality- or task-specific structure leads to stronger compressed models. Important open issues include distillation without access to original data, preserving fairness and privacy in compressed models, and closing the capacity gap between teacher and student without over-constraining the student.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students so that inference cost, memory, latency, or privacy requirements can be met while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD techniques operate at multiple levels—from softened output distributions to intermediate-feature, attention, and relational matching—and are commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or privacy-preserving protocols). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when design choices (what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, the distillation data, and optimization schedules) are made deliberately. However, KD’s effectiveness is conditional: it depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and distribution, and careful handling of robustness, rare or long-tail behaviors, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques reduce model size and inference cost by transferring information from larger or more informed models to smaller ones. Methods vary from soft-label supervision and layer mapping to data-free generation, adversarial sample selection, federated and privacy-preserving protocols, and task- or domain-aware adaptation. Empirical results across vision, language, recommendation, and generative modeling show that distillation can preserve much of teacher performance while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, but performance depends sensitively on what information is transferred, how samples are selected, and whether pretraining or task adaptation is used. Practical use favors hybrids that combine architectural search, selective or weighted distillation, and generation or rehearsal strategies when original data are unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Phelps
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable core of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, and the provenance or scarcity of distillation data. Responsible deployment therefore requires task-aware selection of distillation targets, mitigation of propagated teacher errors, and explicit evaluation for robustness and rare-token behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Uses, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely applied paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students for deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. A spectrum of techniques—from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—supports a range of practical trade-offs. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing footprint, but success depends on student capacity, data availability, and careful design choices; important open problems remain around robustness, principled teacher selection, and reliable distillation under heterogeneous or private data regimes.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It transfers predictive behaviors and internal representations using a range of signals and protocols, and is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that includes data strategies, architecture-aware design, and complementary methods (pruning, quantization, or structured sparsity). Practical deployment requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, the provenance and augmentation of distillation data (including data-free options), and mitigation of transferred biases, robustness regressions, and distribution-shift failures.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structured signals. A wide variety of KD strategies—matching softened logits, aligning features or attention maps, multi-teacher schedules, and data- or task-aware augmentation—enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on what is distilled, student capacity and architecture alignment, availability and provenance of data, and task-specific constraints (e.g., robustness or federated heterogeneity). Carefully designed pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing resource cost, but KD also has important failure modes that motivate complementary techniques and careful engineering.

papers_seen.author: Moon
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Design-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. When integrated with complementary compression methods and tailored to student capacity, data constraints, and deployment objectives, KD routinely produces deployable models that retain most of a teacher's utility. Effective deployment requires explicit choices about what information to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle limited, private, or out-of-distribution data.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible suite of techniques for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the core of a compression workflow but adapted to task, architecture, and data constraints, KD routinely yields substantial improvements in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Its utility spans logits-based supervision, intermediate-representation matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free pipelines. KD is not a turnkey solution: reliable deployment requires complementary methods (pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful handling of teacher imperfections and limited or private data, and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Beard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students for deployment in latency-, memory-, or privacy-constrained environments. KD encompasses transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and structural or layer-wise mappings. Its practical success depends on matching the distillation signals and protocols to teacher and student architectures, the availability and nature of distillation data, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search). While KD can preserve much of teacher performance and sometimes improve generalization, common failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, degraded robustness under domain shift, and optimization challenges that require task-aware design and careful engineering.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for turning large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond matching softened outputs to a toolkit that transfers logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure, and ensemble behavior; operates with limited or no original training data via data synthesis or data-free methods; and composes naturally with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on matching the distillation recipe to task needs, student capacity, and data constraints while explicitly managing teacher imperfections, distributional shift, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Mcintyre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Design-Sensitive Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, multi-signal approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a design-sensitive toolkit—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, preparing or pretraining students, shaping the distillation data, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on managing capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, data availability (including data-free regimes), robustness, and fairness. Practical pipelines therefore start with KD but explicitly integrate representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and targeted remedies for known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Tool: Beyond Compression to Privacy, Robustness, Fairness, and Theory
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation began as a technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models, but its utility now spans privacy-preserving training, robustness transfer, fairness mitigation, domain generalization, and theoretical insights about learning. Distillation can (1) produce compact models that retain most of a teacher's performance, (2) transfer nontrivial inductive biases and robustness properties, and (3) be adapted to settings with privacy constraints or imperfect teachers. However, distillation is not a panacea: teacher errors, choice of distilled data, and sample-level effects can harm the student unless carefully managed. This perspective synthesizes empirical and theoretical evidence to argue that knowledge distillation is a central, flexible methodology for modern deep learning, while highlighting practical constraints and directions for responsible application.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Nuanced Path to Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques to transfer knowledge from large teacher models into smaller students, enabling deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary strategies — such as pre-training compact architectures, data augmentation, selective sample transfer, and module-level compression — KD can yield compact models that retain much of the teacher's utility. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on what is transferred, the availability and nature of data, teacher–student design, and optimization choices. Responsible deployment requires understanding both the practical strengths (efficiency, adaptability, applicability to privacy settings) and the limitations (data dependence, optimization gaps, possible degradation on rare or shifted inputs) of distillation methods.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Conditional Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals) and—when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives—yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs. Its practical use is, however, conditional: success depends on careful signal selection, teacher–student capacity and layer alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of propagated teacher errors, robustness and fairness issues. KD should be treated as the default starting point for compression workflows but must be embedded in a holistic, task-aware pipeline to meet real deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad ecosystem of KD variants has emerged—matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate features or attention, transferring relational structure, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware techniques. In practice KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data-management strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD routinely enables large reductions in parameters and inference cost with modest drops in accuracy, challenges remain in handling domain shift, limited or private data, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and avoiding propagation of teacher errors and biases.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Design-Sensitive Toolkit for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster models by transferring information from larger teacher models to compact students. When treated as a system—deciding what signals to transfer (soft outputs, internal representations, relations), how to prepare or synthesize data, how to design teachers and students, and how to combine KD with complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization—KD enables deployable models that retain much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on capacity matching, data availability, and task-aware objectives; addressing robustness, fairness, and privacy requires targeted interventions and monitoring.
