papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation condenses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, or lower-precision student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision and language, a common set of mechanisms—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, transferring relational structure, and synthesizing or reusing data—forms a modular toolkit that is typically combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. Practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to map layers, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student capacity. Distillation routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest loss in accuracy, but open problems remain in preserving robustness and fairness, handling domain shift and data scarcity, and reliably distilling rare or fine-grained behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Potts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and effective approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple transferable signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational structure) and composes well with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its practical success depends on student capacity and architecture, the choice of distillation signals, availability and provenance of distillation data, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Reliable deployment therefore treats KD as the default first-line mechanism embedded in an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline that selects signals, data strategies, and complementary methods to match constraints and validate real-world behavior.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Wolf
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints. Across modalities, KD methods include matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention, and transferring relational or contrastive structure. Distillation is most effective when integrated with architecture-aware design and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, or neural architecture search), and when data strategies (original-data, augmented, or synthesized/data-free) and teacher–student alignment are explicitly addressed. While KD routinely yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss, its benefits depend on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy, motivating task-aware distillation workflows and continued research into representation-level objectives and data-synthesis techniques.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Hybrid Tool for Reliable Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple transfer signals and schedules that can recover much of a teacher’s performance when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. However, distillation is not sufficient on its own: combining KD with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), pretraining or adapting the student, and applying data-aware strategies improves robustness, domain transfer, and preservation of rare behaviors. A pragmatic, task-aware pipeline—choosing appropriate signals to transfer, preparing student models, augmenting or synthesizing data, and explicitly evaluating robustness and fairness—yields the most reliable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs for production NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Bradley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (compute, memory, latency, privacy). KD spans matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate representations or attention, transferring relational structure, and using multi-teacher, online, or data-free protocols. It is most effective when integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when distillation choices are aligned with student capacity, available data, and downstream robustness or fairness requirements. Open problems include principled teacher selection and weighting, reliable zero-shot or data-free distillation, preserving rare-token and fine-grained behaviors, and avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, multi-faceted approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models while preserving much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logits matching, distillation can be adapted to transfer inductive biases, deploy in federated or privacy-constrained settings, operate without access to original training data, and improve robustness and domain specialization. When combined with techniques such as feature mimicking, careful soft-label regularization, and online or ensemble-based training regimes, distillation provides a flexible toolkit to meet the efficiency, privacy, and deployment constraints of modern deep learning and NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Contextual Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed to match student capacity, task requirements, and available data, distillation reliably reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Its practical success depends on selecting appropriate distilled signals (logits, features, relations), combining KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, architecture search, quantization), and addressing open problems such as data scarcity, teacher error transfer, and robustness across distributions.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolkit—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression and data strategies—KD routinely yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its success depends on student capacity, data availability and provenance, and careful handling of robustness and bias; therefore KD is best used as an integrated, task-aware pipeline rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Flexible Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible toolkit: it can transfer logits, internal representations, or structured relational knowledge; it can be combined with architecture search, multi-teacher schemes, or data synthesis; and it can be adapted with task-aware filtering or teacher-aware training to address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. Carefully chosen distillation targets, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression components produce small, deployable models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Practical Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A broad family of distillation objectives—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise supervision, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search or data augmentation—enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical successes span classification, object detection, machine translation, and language-model compression, but practical deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to curate or synthesize distillation data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. The method’s effectiveness arises partly from the regularizing properties of soft targets and richer teacher signals, yet distillation can propagate teacher errors and struggle with capacity, data heterogeneity, and robustness unless augmented by task-aware design or additional engineering.

papers_seen.author: Tyler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted, empirically driven set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. KD transfers information at multiple levels—from softened output distributions to intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structure—and is often integrated with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Practical KD pipelines also depend on data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic), student–teacher alignment, and attention to robustness, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. While KD routinely yields favorable efficiency–performance trade-offs across modalities, outstanding challenges remain around capacity mismatch, reliably preserving rare or robustness-related behavior, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Uses, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for compressing large, high-performing neural models into smaller, faster, or more privacy-preserving students. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, KD transfers information at multiple levels—teacher output distributions, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure—and is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware search. Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to evaluate robustness, fairness, and privacy. Empirical and methodological work emphasizes treating KD as a task-aware toolkit embedded in broader compression pipelines rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of teacher→student techniques used to produce smaller, faster, or more deployable models while retaining much of the performance of larger teachers. The field has evolved from simple logit-matching to rich toolkits that include feature- and representation-level transfer, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and federated variants, and combinations with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across modalities, but practical success depends on signal selection, teacher–student compatibility, data strategies, and targeted interventions for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Austin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When embedded in a deliberate compression pipeline and matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs; however, its success is conditional and requires complementary compression primitives, careful teacher–student alignment, and explicit attention to data, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a System: Practical Strengths, Limits, and Prescriptions for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a modular system—combining soft-target supervision, representation-level objectives, data augmentation, multi-teacher signals, and complementary compression methods—KD reliably yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. Effectiveness depends on handling data availability, architecture mismatches, and undesirable teacher artifacts; these constraints are manageable when KD is designed with domain adaptation, input alignment, and augmentation-aware strategies. I argue KD should be the default toolchain for producing production-ready compact models, applied with explicit attention to what knowledge is transferred and how it is matched to student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Combs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a configurable toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD excels when combined with architecture-aware student design, complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization), and deliberate data strategies (real-data, augmentation, or synthesis). Its practical value is conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and domain shift determine when KD will produce reliable, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression approaches transform large, high-performance neural models into smaller, faster models suitable for constrained deployment while attempting to preserve task performance. Methods range from transferring softened output distributions to matching intermediate representations, designing task-aware layer mappings, synthesizing or augmenting data for training, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Applications include compressing pretrained transformers for NLP, improving robustness under domain shift, enabling on-device inference and federated learning with heterogeneous devices, and training non-autoregressive sequence models. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both practical gains and limitations: distillation can yield compact models with strong accuracy but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, availability or synthesis of data, and handling low-frequency or domain-specific phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models and transferring their capabilities to smaller or specialized models. KD can operate at multiple levels (logits, intermediate layers, and features), can be combined with model pruning and precision reduction, and can support domain adaptation and on-device deployment. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on how teacher knowledge is represented and transferred, the choice of data and augmentations used during distillation, and the deployment context (e.g., heterogeneous federated environments). When methods for intermediate-layer alignment, feature mimicking, data-side regularization, and architecture-aware mapping are combined thoughtfully, KD yields compact, efficient models that retain much of the teacher’s performance while enabling practical deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic for shrinking large models into a fundamental, flexible family of techniques for producing compact, efficient models across vision, speech, and natural language processing. Methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure; variants address constraints such as lack of original data, domain shift, low-precision hardware, and heterogeneous architectures. Empirical work shows distilled students often recover much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under strict latency, memory, or privacy constraints, but success depends on choices about teacher quality, student capacity, data selection or synthesis, and training protocols. Current directions emphasize multi-stage distillation, data- and architecture-aware objectives, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and pre-training; open problems remain around principled teacher selection, robust cross-domain transfer, low-resource and data-free scenarios, and preserving fairness and calibration under compression.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and empirically effective paradigm for producing compact, resource-efficient models from larger teachers across computer vision, language, graph, and speech tasks. As a modular system, KD supports multiple information-transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, and architecture search). Real-world deployment requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or no access to teacher data, and how to address robustness and fairness concerns. When KD is applied as a deliberate toolchain—selecting task-aware objectives, incorporating multi-teacher or synthetic-data protocols, and combining with data- and model-level compression—practical students can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Open problems remain around preserving rare-event behaviors, domain shift, and student-aware teacher shaping, which motivate focused research on curricula, data synthesis, and representation-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Mann
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Limits, and Practical Pipeline
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central and flexible approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, transferring intermediate representations, attention- and relation-based signals, online and self-distillation, and data strategies that include using original data, augmentations, or synthesized examples. While KD often recovers most of a teacher’s performance and composes with pruning, quantization, and architecture search, it is not a universal solution: practical success depends on careful choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to prepare or synthesize distillation data, and how to mitigate capacity mismatch, domain shift, and propagated teacher errors. A task-aware, pipeline-oriented approach—pretraining or otherwise preparing the student, selecting appropriate distillation signals, choosing data protocols, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques—yields the most reliable efficiency–performance tradeoffs for real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Schmitt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most productively framed not as a single heuristic but as a configurable, task-aware component of model-compression pipelines. When practitioners treat KD as a multi-signal workflow—selecting what to transfer (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational structure), aligning teacher and student capacity and architecture, and combining distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, or federated protocols)—it reliably produces compact, deployable models that recover much of a teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its benefits depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (including data-free and federated regimes), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional shift. Responsible deployment therefore requires designing KD as part of a broader engineering pipeline with targeted evaluation and safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Its practical strengths derive from multiple mechanisms—soft-target transfer, intermediate representation matching, relational objectives, and data-side strategies—that together enable substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, domain shift, propagation of teacher errors) and design choices (what to transfer, how to align layers, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to select or weight teachers) substantially affect outcomes. The most reliable deployments treat KD as one component of an integrated compression pipeline that combines task-aware loss design, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic approaches), architecture-aware mapping, and complementary compression techniques such as pruning or quantization.

papers_seen.author: Ruiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task-Aware Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical engine for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring information at multiple levels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving most of the teacher’s predictive performance. However, distillation is design-sensitive: choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability or privacy, and how to combine KD with complementary compression primitives determine real-world success. A task-aware workflow that selects distillation signals, adopts appropriate layer-mapping or multi-teacher schedules, and leverages data synthesis or domain adaptation yields the most reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Maxwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, task-aware approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and in diverse protocols (offline teacher–student, online/multi-teacher, self-distillation). When embedded in a broader pipeline that aligns teacher and student architectures, selects appropriate distillation signals, and uses realistic or synthesized data, KD routinely produces models that approach teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. Practical deployment requires combining KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), explicit evaluation for robustness, and strategies to mitigate capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher artifacts, privacy risks, and degraded behavior on rare or out-of-distribution cases. Ongoing research targets principled teacher selection, reliable data-free distillation, preserving fine-grained behaviors, and deeper theoretical understanding of why and when KD succeeds.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses information from large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The approach has diversified from soft-label matching into a toolkit that transfers logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or combinations thereof; it can be adapted to settings with limited or no access to original training data, and it is often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate distillation data, and integrating KD into a broader compression pipeline that validates robustness and fairness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, Practical Benefits and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a simple teacher–student logit-matching trick into a broad, practical toolkit for compressing large models and adapting their knowledge to resource- and data-constrained settings. Effective distillation operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, relational signals), interacts strongly with data and augmentation choices, and is most useful when combined with complementary compression methods and careful teacher–student design. While KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, its success depends on dealing with data availability, domain shift, teacher quality, and optimization dynamics—areas that remain active research directions.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Pathways for Compressing Large NLP Models: Pre-train the Student, Distill Carefully, and Guard for Data & Robustness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach to compress large deep learning models for NLP and related tasks. When the student model is itself pre-trained, distillation yields especially strong and consistent gains; complementary methods — including data augmentation during distillation, progressive module replacement, ensemble teachers or teacher adaptation, and data-free or privacy-aware distillation — address common deployment constraints such as limited task data, inference cost, data access, and adversarial robustness. Combining these techniques and choosing distillation targets and schedules with theoretical and empirical guidance yields compact models that retain much of the original performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide a broad, practically oriented toolkit for shrinking large neural models while retaining most of their performance. Methods include transferring soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, adapting teacher or student architectures, using adversarial or data-free sample generation, and combining distillation with quantization or pruning. Empirical results across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks show substantial latency and memory gains; success depends on what signals are transferred, how layers are matched, data availability and augmentation, and the deployment constraints that shape algorithmic choices.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Versatile Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable compression paradigm that transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students. When carefully applied, KD enables deployment of performant, efficient models across tasks and modalities, addressing constraints such as inference cost, memory, data availability, and privacy. However, effectiveness depends on what is distilled (outputs vs. internal representations), the availability of training data, and training dynamics; understanding these aspects guides practical decisions that combine KD with quantization, architecture design, and training curricula to produce reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD operates at multiple levels — softened outputs (logits), intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and sometimes architectural or module-wise mappings — and is typically used as part of a broader compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies (including data-free or synthetic-data regimes). Empirically, well-designed distillation pipelines recover a large portion of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in inference cost and memory; however, KD’s effectiveness depends strongly on teacher–student capacity alignment, the choice of distilled signals, availability or synthesis of suitable data, and explicit handling of robustness, rare-event behavior, and fairness issues. Remaining research challenges include principled teacher selection, preserving robustness and long‑tail behaviors, reliable layer- or module-mapping for large pre-trained models, and distillation under strict privacy or data‑scarce constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level methodology for shrinking large, high‑performance models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of the teacher’s utility. The approach covers transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can operate offline, online, with multiple teachers, or without original training data. In practice KD is most effective when combined with architecture-aware student design, data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), and complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, language, recommendation, and federated settings, but it faces challenges including capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, degraded rare-token performance, and robustness under distribution shift. The literature offers practical design principles and targeted algorithmic tools to mitigate these limitations and to adapt KD to heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive environments.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-signal toolkit for transferring the behavior and internal structure of large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. As a central component of compression pipelines KD routinely yields strong trade-offs between efficiency and performance when combined with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which complementary compression primitives and data strategies to apply. However, KD has systematic limits—capacity mismatch, optimization gaps, teacher error propagation, domain shift, and risks to robustness and fairness—that require targeted remedies and rigorous evaluation. This paper argues KD should be treated as the default first-line strategy for compression in production, but only as part of integrated, task- and data-aware pipelines that explicitly mitigate its known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, System-Level Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational or attention structure), and it composes naturally with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. However, its effectiveness is conditional: success depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data strategies (including data-free or augmented examples), and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift. When treated as a system-level component of a compression pipeline rather than a single recipe, KD routinely yields compact models that meet deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Design‑Sensitive Toolbox for Reliable Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile method for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD works across multiple signal types (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and data regimes, and routinely delivers substantial reductions in inference cost when its objectives, student design, and data strategies are matched to deployment constraints. At the same time, KD is conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and distributional mismatch impose predictable limits and require complementary techniques and careful evaluation to ensure robustness, fairness, and preservation of rare-event behavior.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression: when applied as an integrated, task-aware system it enables compact students that preserve much of a teacher’s utility while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware surgery), careful data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free protocols), and explicit attention to teacher–student capacity alignment and robustness evaluation. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its benefits are conditional on signal selection, data and initialization choices, and evaluation for fairness and domain-shift resilience. I argue for treating KD as a configurable pipeline (signals, data, architecture, optimization) and for adopting specific practices that mitigate common failure modes in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Configurable Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated framework for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. When paired with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and task-aware choices about what to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, relational structure), KD routinely preserves much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of training data, alignment of distilled signals to task needs, and mitigation of teacher artifacts and distribution shift. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable system—combining representation-aware objectives, staged curricula, data- or privacy-aware synthesis, and hybrid compression—to maximize real-world utility while acknowledging open limitations.

papers_seen.author: Hopkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A flexible toolkit of distillation signals—soft logits, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational or contrastive objectives—and training schedules (offline, online, multi-teacher, or staged) is combined with data strategies (original data, augmentation, synthesized or data-free approaches) and complementary compression primitives (pretraining, pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines routinely recover much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but success depends on aligning distilled signals to student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate data, and addressing robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns. Practical deployment therefore treats distillation as a central, but context-dependent, component of compression systems rather than a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. The approach includes aligning soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can operate with original, augmented, or synthesized data. In practice, distillation is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline—combining architecture-aware design, pruning, and quantization—and when distillation objectives are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows substantial reductions in inference cost and memory with modest performance loss, but predictable failure modes remain around capacity mismatch, data scarcity or mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degraded robustness on rare or shifted inputs. Ongoing challenges include principled teacher–student curricula, reliable distillation without original data, and theoretical understanding of why and when different signals transfer successfully.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, and Evolving Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core engineering and research paradigm for compressing large models into efficient students while preserving accuracy and desirable behaviors. KD encompasses soft-target transfer, intermediate representation alignment, ensemble-to-single compression, and complementary data- and architecture-aware techniques. When treated as a design problem—choosing which signals to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data constraints—KD enables deployment across resource-limited and domain-shifted settings, but open challenges remain in preserving rare-token behaviors, coping with imperfect teachers, and operating without original data.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal signals. A diverse toolkit of KD objectives and protocols has emerged—matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, using relational or contrastive objectives, and operating with real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free surrogate data. Practical pipelines combine KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require task- and data-aware design to manage capacity mismatch, preserve robustness, and mitigate propagation of teacher errors or biases. Empirical and methodological work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when these design choices are made carefully, while ongoing challenges remain around reliable data-free distillation, preserving long‑tail behaviors, and principled layer/representation mapping for large pre-trained models.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a system—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity and architecture, choosing or synthesizing distillation data, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD frequently yields students that recover a large fraction of teacher performance while meeting latency and memory constraints. However, KD’s benefits are conditional on design choices and data provenance; predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, domain shift, and degraded rare-token or safety-critical behavior) require explicit mitigation and careful evaluation in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at multiple levels (outputs, intermediate representations, relations). Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a toolbox that includes representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and augmentation-driven protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data strategy, and optimization; when integrated into a broader compression pipeline, KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Remaining challenges include reliably preserving rare or out-of-domain behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases or errors, and operating under data- or privacy-constrained regimes.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a core component of compression pipelines, KD can transfer information via softened logits, intermediate representations, relational signals, or synthesized data, and it is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and careful data strategies. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, the provenance and quantity of distillation data, and explicit evaluation for robustness, long-tail behavior, and fairness. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable, task-aware system and adopt multi-stage, data‑aware, and privacy-conscious techniques to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deploying large pretrained models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students. Methods include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate features or attention maps, layer- and task-aware alignment, online and mutual distillation, and data-free approaches that synthesize surrogate inputs. Empirical evidence across vision and language tasks shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size, latency, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Remaining challenges center on preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior in sequence models, avoiding transfer of biases or adversarial vulnerabilities, and jointly optimizing compression for hardware and task constraints.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a multifaceted toolkit for shrinking large neural models while retaining much of their accuracy. Approaches include matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, transforming architectures to be resource-efficient, and designing teacher–student curricula or multi-teacher aggregations. KD is applied across supervised, self-supervised, few-shot, federated, and privacy-constrained scenarios and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers and capacity, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; when designed carefully, KD enables deployment of compact models for diverse NLP and vision tasks while exposing open questions about robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Task‑Aware Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood and applied as a configurable, task‑aware core of model compression pipelines rather than as a single recipe. Treated as a modular toolkit—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to align architectures—KD routinely produces compact students that recover much of teacher performance when combined with complementary techniques and explicit evaluation for robustness and rare‑case behaviors. Responsible deployment requires deliberate handling of capacity mismatch, data constraints, and propagated teacher artifacts through targeted adaptations such as multi‑teacher aggregation, data‑free or privacy‑aware protocols, and architecture‑aware student design.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. KD can preserve predictive performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its strengths derive from a variety of mechanisms — soft-label matching, internal-feature alignment, layer-mapping, and task-adaptive architecture design — and from being combinable with complementary compression techniques. However, realizing consistent gains requires careful choice of distilled targets, attention to representation alignment between teacher and student, and explicit handling of data-, fairness-, and robustness-related risks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a toolbox of targeted interventions rather than a single recipe, and provides concise, evidence-based recommendations for practitioners compressing models in vision and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Henry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring learned behavior at the level of outputs, intermediate representations, or relational structure. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching to a flexible toolkit that includes representation- and layer-wise alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical and theoretical work shows distilled students can often recover much of a teacher's performance, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, the teacher–student capacity relationship, data availability, and optimization strategy. Practical deployment benefits from treating KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs distillation signals with student preparation, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression methods to mitigate predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, optimization barriers, and propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Fox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: A Conditional, Pipeline‑First Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective toolkit for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces inference cost and often preserves much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness is conditional on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and complementary compression steps. I argue KD should serve as the default, central component of compression workflows while being explicitly combined with targeted pretraining, data strategies, architecture-aware design, and robustness/fairness evaluation to produce reliable production models.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Benefits, Limits, and a Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with task-aware choices about what to transfer, pretraining of compact architectures, representation-level supervision, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, distillation has important failure modes — capacity mismatch, data and domain heterogeneity, and propagation of teacher biases — that must be addressed through careful teacher selection, data strategies, and evaluation. A pragmatic pipeline that pretrains students, distills both outputs and intermediate representations, and selectively composes KD with other compression steps yields robust trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy in practice.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD operates across multiple signal types (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational maps) and is most effective when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware student design, pretraining, and complementary primitives such as pruning and quantization. Its empirical success is conditional on careful teacher–student alignment, appropriate distillation signals, data strategies (including data-free or synthetic approaches when necessary), and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behavior. Best practice treats KD as a configurable core of compression workflows rather than a single recipe, combining careful signal selection, data handling, and staged evaluation to produce reliable, efficient students.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from large, high-performing models to smaller, efficient models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature has diversified beyond simple teacher→student logit-matching to include feature- and representation-level transfer, online and federated protocols, teacher-free and data-free variants, and architectural co-design. Empirical work across vision, speech, 3D perception, and NLP demonstrates that carefully chosen distillation signals, layer mappings, and training practices (e.g., pretraining, projected feature matching, selective sample weighting) produce compact models that preserve much of teacher performance; remaining challenges include data heterogeneity, privacy, robustness, and automating teacher–student pairing and signal selection.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for creating smaller, faster models from larger ones while retaining much of their functionality. When combined with representation matching, architecture-aware surgery, selective sample strategies, and privacy-aware protocols, KD enables deployment of high-quality models across modalities and constrained environments. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; without such care, distillation can underperform or transfer undesirable behaviors. This paper argues that KD should be treated as the central, composable tool in compression toolkits, and outlines concrete methodological priorities that practitioners should follow to realize reliable, efficient distilled models.
