papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or more private models. Across vision, speech, and NLP tasks, a consistent set of practices has emerged—logit/soft-label transfer, intermediate-layer matching, and task- or domain-specific adaptation—augmented by variants that address missing data, distributed training, privacy, and teacher-student mismatch. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while enjoying large gains in inference speed and memory, and recent work clarifies when and why distillation acts as an effective regularizer.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Task-Aware Core of Model Compression: A Practical Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be the default, central mechanism in model-compression workflows for deep learning and NLP because it provides a flexible, multi-signal way to transfer useful behavior from large teachers to smaller students. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on explicit choices about which teacher signals to transfer, how to match teacher and student capacity, what data or synthetic proxies to use, and how to combine distillation with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Responsible, high-fidelity compression therefore treats KD as a configurable, task-aware core embedded in a validated engineering pipeline that addresses capacity mismatch, domain shift, robustness, privacy, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large models (teachers) to smaller models (students). Treated as a central component of compression pipelines and adapted to task constraints, KD can produce compact, deployable models that retain much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Effective application requires careful choices about what knowledge to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to manage data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques. Persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of rare or fine-grained behaviors, and avoidance of transferred biases or robustness regressions; addressing these motivates hybrid, task-aware engineering and further research into evaluation and theory.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Capabilities, Limitations, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, language, multimodal, and graph domains, KD variants enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, speed up training at scale, and allow transfer of robustness or domain expertise when carefully designed. However, successful distillation depends on alignment of teacher and student inputs/representations, the choice of distilled signals (logits, features, attention, or contrastive embeddings), and careful handling of privacy, robustness, and domain shift. Best practice combines representation-level matching, adaptive teacher strategies, confidence-aware multi-teacher fusion, and privacy- or robustness-aware objectives to meet practical constraints while maximizing student performance.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable transferring performance from large, often pre-trained or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster student models for practical deployment. The literature converges on a flexible toolkit: matching softened outputs (logits), aligning intermediate representations or relations, using data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or generated data), and combining KD with complementary compression methods (architecture search, pruning, quantization). Empirical work shows KD can recover a large fraction of teacher performance across modalities and tasks when designers choose appropriate distilled signals, align heterogeneous architectures, and address data constraints; remaining challenges include optimization gaps between teacher and student, distilling under no- or limited-data regimes, preserving robustness and low-frequency behavior, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Insufficient Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable method for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides multiple complementary transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure) and—when combined with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware student design—enables strong efficiency–performance trade-offs across vision and NLP. Its practical success depends on careful teacher–student capacity alignment, the provenance and handling of distillation data (including selective or synthesized examples), and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare/shifted behaviors. KD should therefore be treated as the central element of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Contemporary Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-level approach for producing compact deep and NLP models by transferring information from larger teacher models into smaller students. KD techniques range from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations and relational structures. When integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and data-aware training practices, KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss. However, its effectiveness is conditional on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and provenance, and careful optimization; accordingly, KD is best treated as a central, composable element of a broader compression toolkit rather than a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deploying large deep models by transferring their predictive behavior or internal structure to smaller, faster models. Research has progressed from soft-label teacher-student training toward richer objectives that match internal representations, feature spaces, and decision boundaries; from data-dependent distillation to data-free and privacy-preserving approaches; and from one-size-fits-all compression to task-adaptive, architecture-aware methods. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance across speech, vision, and language tasks when distillation objectives, training data (real or synthetic), and search for efficient architectures are carefully tailored. Remaining challenges include optimization barriers that prevent perfect teacher matching, balancing regularization and fidelity, and handling heterogeneous or absent data during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Villarreal
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Task‑Aware Component of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reliably compresses large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. When treated as a central, composable element of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely yields strong trade-offs between efficiency and task performance. However, its success is conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and provenance, optimization dynamics, and fairness/robustness concerns limit what KD can accomplish on its own. Practical pipelines therefore make KD the default backbone but explicitly mitigate known failure modes through task-aware signal selection, teacher calibration, and integration with other compression primitives.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints by trading modest amounts of accuracy for substantial reductions in compute and footprint. When treated as an engineering toolkit—combining output-level supervision, intermediate-representation transfer, multi-teacher fusion, and data-aware strategies—KD reliably produces compact models that meet real-world constraints; success requires careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity and attention to optimization, data selection, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Mccormick
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When KD is embedded in a task-aware compression pipeline that aligns distillation signals with student capacity, uses data-aware strategies (including synthesis when necessary), and combines distillation with complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization), practitioners can produce compact models that retain much of teacher utility while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, KD’s benefits are conditional: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, architecture mismatch, and distribution-shift vulnerabilities limit outcomes unless addressed through deliberate pipeline choices and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. While classic distillation focuses on matching teacher output probabilities, practical compression across modalities and tasks benefits from richer transfer mechanisms: aligning internal representations, selecting task-relevant signals, leveraging data augmentation or synthetic data when real data are scarce, and using adversarial or ensemble strategies to expose diverse and robust teacher knowledge. When combined thoughtfully these methods enable students that are much smaller and faster while retaining or even improving accuracy and robustness on downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical set of techniques to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Across computer vision, generative modeling, retrieval, and natural language processing, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt models to new domains or privacy constraints. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), how teacher and student are aligned (layer mapping, attention-weighted projection, task-aware filters), and whether original training data are available (data-free and zero-shot approaches). Success depends on careful choices of teacher preparation, student capacity and architecture, signal selection, and data or synthetic-sample strategies; when designed appropriately, KD combined with complementary compression (pruning, architecture transforms) yields compact models with strong empirical performance, while important limitations remain (representation mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, low-frequency token coverage).

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-faceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), can be adapted to scenarios with limited or private data, and is typically combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves most teacher performance and can provide implicit regularization and better calibration, but its success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and careful design choices. Effective pipelines treat KD as a central, task-aware component integrated with pretraining, data strategies, and deployment-aware validation to manage trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and resource use.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Task-Aware Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective engine for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. KD’s flexibility—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-teacher schedules, and operating with or without original data—makes it the practical backbone of compression pipelines. However, distillation can amplify teacher biases, struggle with rare-token or long-tail behavior, and depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; practitioners should therefore adopt integrated, task-aware KD workflows combined with complementary compression techniques and explicit evaluation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a flexible, multi-faceted approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in both vision and natural language processing. Modern KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft output distributions, intermediate representations, and relational structure—and is often integrated with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to map teacher and student architectures, which data or synthetic samples to use, and when to apply multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules. Remaining challenges include optimization difficulties that limit exact matching, teacher–student mismatch under domain shift or heterogeneity (e.g., federated settings), and the need to preserve robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behaviors in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible, task-aware family of techniques for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates at multiple signal levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure) and composes naturally with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Practical success depends on careful alignment of teacher and student capacity, selection or synthesis of appropriate distillation data, and integration of KD into a broader, task‑aware pipeline that explicitly evaluates robustness, fairness, and performance on rare or out-of-distribution behaviors. While many empirical results show that KD can recover most of a teacher’s performance and deliver substantial efficiency gains, open challenges remain around capacity mismatch, transfer of undesirable teacher behavior, reliable data-free distillation, and robust operation under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Palmer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi‑level toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller students for deployment in latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. KD transfers information through softened outputs, intermediate representation alignment, relational/attention-level objectives, and data-side strategies (including data augmentation and synthesis). When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task- or data-aware choices, KD frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while enabling efficient on-device and domain-specialized models. Effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and provenance, and careful optimization and evaluation to avoid predictable failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, degraded rare-token behavior, and distribution-shift fragility.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and richer internal signals. A diverse toolkit of KD objectives and protocols has emerged—matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, using relational or contrastive objectives, and operating with real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free surrogate data. Practical pipelines combine KD with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and require task- and data-aware design to manage capacity mismatch, preserve robustness, and mitigate propagation of teacher errors or biases. Empirical and methodological work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance when these design choices are made carefully, while ongoing challenges remain around reliable data-free distillation, preserving long‑tail behaviors, and principled layer/representation mapping for large pre-trained models.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques form a flexible set of training paradigms that transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large 'teacher' networks into smaller, faster 'student' models. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, practitioners use logit/soft-target matching, intermediate feature or attention alignment, relational objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free procedures to shrink models while retaining much of their utility. Effective distillation typically combines careful selection of distillation targets, student preparation (architecture choice or pretraining), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). While distilled students often approach teacher performance in many settings, remaining challenges include capacity and optimization gaps, domain- or data-shift, preservation of rare-token behavior and fairness, and principled design for data-free or privacy-constrained scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Buchanan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a modular pipeline, KD transfers information via softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational objectives, and other signals, and is routinely combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic). Empirical work across speech, vision, and language shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while dramatically reducing size and inference cost, but its success is conditional on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability and distribution, architecture alignment, and careful optimization. Practical deployment therefore relies on task-aware design choices, staged schedules, and integrations (e.g., data-free distillation or multi-signal objectives) to mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and fragility under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful but Incomplete
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a flexible and practical set of techniques for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. It supports multiple transfer signals (soft targets, intermediate features, relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and integrates naturally with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). When KD is treated as the central element of a task-aware compression pipeline — i.e., when the distillation recipe is matched to data availability, student capacity, architecture heterogeneity, and deployment constraints — it yields strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. Nevertheless, distillation alone does not guarantee robustness, fairness, or preservation of low-frequency behaviors in language tasks; careful design choices, data strategies, and combination with other compression primitives are required for reliable production deployment.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, multi-signal paradigm for turning large, accurate models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. Modern practice combines soft-target (logit) matching with intermediate-representation and relational-transfer objectives, often integrated with pretraining, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Effective pipelines account for data availability (including data-free or synthetic-data regimes), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., low-frequency token behavior or robustness under distribution shift). While KD routinely preserves much of teacher performance in applied settings, open problems persist around principled teacher selection, reliably transferring rare-event and robustness properties, and optimizing heterogeneous or privacy-constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression: Evidence, Mechanisms, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a central and practical toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision, generative modeling, and natural language processing. KD succeeds because it can transfer diverse signals—soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure—and because those signals can be adapted to constraints such as data scarcity, architecture mismatch, or privacy. However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers, how to prepare or synthesize data, and how to address teacher errors and optimization instabilities. The best outcomes arise from integrated distillation pipelines that combine representation-level objectives, careful data strategies (including augmentation or synthetic samples), architecture-aware mapping, and multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules tailored to the deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Tool: Beyond Compression to Privacy, Robustness, Fairness, and Theory
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation began as a technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models, but its utility now spans privacy-preserving training, robustness transfer, fairness mitigation, domain generalization, and theoretical insights about learning. Distillation can (1) produce compact models that retain most of a teacher's performance, (2) transfer nontrivial inductive biases and robustness properties, and (3) be adapted to settings with privacy constraints or imperfect teachers. However, distillation is not a panacea: teacher errors, choice of distilled data, and sample-level effects can harm the student unless carefully managed. This perspective synthesizes empirical and theoretical evidence to argue that knowledge distillation is a central, flexible methodology for modern deep learning, while highlighting practical constraints and directions for responsible application.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable deploying large pretrained models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from high-capacity teachers to smaller students. Methods include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate features or attention maps, layer- and task-aware alignment, online and mutual distillation, and data-free approaches that synthesize surrogate inputs. Empirical evidence across vision and language tasks shows that well-designed distillation can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size, latency, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to map heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or private data. Remaining challenges center on preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior in sequence models, avoiding transfer of biases or adversarial vulnerabilities, and jointly optimizing compression for hardware and task constraints.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Beyond Compression: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Practical, Private, and Robust Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often framed narrowly as a model-compression trick to shrink large neural networks. This paper argues KD should instead be viewed as a core engineering and scientific tool for practical deployment: it enables training with limited or private data, yields task- and domain-adaptive compact models, improves robustness and fairness, and transfers intermediate representations and attention patterns that standard supervised training cannot. We synthesize evidence from recent work to show how variants of KD—self-distillation, layer-wise projection, multi-teacher schemes, teacher annealing, and data-free distillation—address concrete deployment challenges in vision and NLP, and we derive practical recommendations for combining these techniques in real systems.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Limited Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach that enables deploying large models under resource, latency, and privacy constraints by transferring knowledge from teacher to student models. KD extends beyond simple logit matching to include representation-level transfer, attention- and feature-guided objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and integration with architecture search and pretraining. While KD reliably improves efficiency and can preserve many teacher behaviors, its success depends on choices of distillation targets, teacher preparation, student architecture, and data strategies; it can also amplify teacher errors or struggle under data heterogeneity, requiring complementary techniques and careful engineering for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a system-level toolkit—combining logit matching, representation alignment, ensemble or multi-teacher signals, data-side strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation), and complementary compression techniques—KD frequently preserves much of a teacher’s performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD’s success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, and attention to robustness and bias transfer. Practical deployment therefore requires matching the distillation recipe to task requirements, student capacity, and data realities.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Toolchain for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and empirically effective paradigm for producing compact, resource-efficient models from larger teachers across computer vision, language, graph, and speech tasks. As a modular system, KD supports multiple information-transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structure), can operate with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (quantization, pruning, and architecture search). Real-world deployment requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or no access to teacher data, and how to address robustness and fairness concerns. When KD is applied as a deliberate toolchain—selecting task-aware objectives, incorporating multi-teacher or synthetic-data protocols, and combining with data- and model-level compression—practical students can approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Open problems remain around preserving rare-event behaviors, domain shift, and student-aware teacher shaping, which motivate focused research on curricula, data synthesis, and representation-aware objectives.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesized Evidence and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. A broad family of KD objectives and protocols—soft-target matching, feature and attention mimicry, relational losses, multi-teacher and online schemes—has been developed and empirically validated across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks. KD is most effective when treated as a system that aligns teacher and student capacity, chooses what signals to transfer, and composes with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search, or low-precision numerics). Successful deployment depends on data strategies (real-data distillation, augmentation, or synthetic/data-free methods), student initialization or pretraining, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy constraints. Remaining research directions include principled layer mapping for large pre-trained models, reliable distillation without original data, preserving robustness and rare-event behaviors, and theoretical understanding of optimization dynamics under capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Hunter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Design‑Sensitive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible training paradigm that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. KD operates at multiple signal levels (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational structure) and is typically combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies. Its practical success depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data provenance, and integration into broader compression pipelines; when these are addressed, KD routinely yields compact models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Conditional Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated toolkit that enables compact student models to inherit much of the performance of large teacher models. Treated as a modular, design-sensitive component of compression workflows, KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational patterns), can be adapted to constrained data regimes (real, augmented, or synthesized), and composes effectively with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). At the same time, KD is not a universal remedy: student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and distributional/robustness concerns place clear limits on its effectiveness. Responsible, production-ready compression therefore treats KD as the core of an integrated pipeline and couples it with targeted engineering choices, evaluation, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD has diversified from matching softened teacher outputs into a toolkit that also transfers intermediate features, attention and relational structure, and that can operate with real, augmented, or synthesized data. In practice KD is usually combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and tuned for deployment trade-offs (latency, memory, privacy). Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear benefits (improved sample efficiency, regularization, domain adaptation, enabling on-device use) alongside systematic limitations (capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, optimization difficulties, and challenges under data scarcity), motivating hybrid, task-aware pipelines and ongoing research into robust data-free methods, principled teacher selection, and fairness/robustness preservation.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation objectives—from matching soft output distributions to transferring intermediate representations, relational statistics, and task-specific features—and emphasizes combining KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free distillation). Successful distillation pipelines attend to teacher–student capacity alignment, layer- and signal-selection, and data provenance to preserve accuracy, robustness, and domain suitability. Remaining challenges include distillation without original data, robustness under distribution shift or adversarial attack, and automated, architecture-agnostic distillation for heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity models (teachers) into smaller, more efficient models (students). Across vision and language, practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architectural design, and quantization) and with strategies for scarce or missing data to obtain deployable models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, attention), how to align heterogeneous architectures, the role of pre-training for compact models, and mechanisms to preserve robustness and rare-token behaviors. Data-free distillation, multi-task or multi-teacher schemes, and targeted representation matching extend KD’s applicability to many real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Core for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach that should serve as the default engine in model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large teachers to smaller students, but its practical success is conditional on task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to combine distillation with complementary methods and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal signals. The approach includes aligning soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational structure, and can operate with original, augmented, or synthesized data. In practice, distillation is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline—combining architecture-aware design, pruning, and quantization—and when distillation objectives are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows substantial reductions in inference cost and memory with modest performance loss, but predictable failure modes remain around capacity mismatch, data scarcity or mismatch, propagation of teacher biases, and degraded robustness on rare or shifted inputs. Ongoing challenges include principled teacher–student curricula, reliable distillation without original data, and theoretical understanding of why and when different signals transfer successfully.

papers_seen.author: Baird
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade KD evolved from simple softened-logit matching into a broad toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distilled students often recover much of a teacher's performance when teacher–student capacity, distilled signals, and data strategies are chosen carefully, but persistent failure modes (capacity mismatch, teacher error transfer, domain shift, and degraded low-frequency behavior) require targeted remedies. Practical use treats KD as a system-level engineering problem that pairs appropriate distillation signals with student preparation, data curation or synthesis, and complementary compression techniques to produce compact, robust models suitable for resource- and privacy-constrained deployment.

papers_seen.author: Brooks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Conditional Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as part of an integrated compression pipeline—combining what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teacher and student are aligned, and appropriate data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic)—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and inference cost. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on careful choice of signals, mitigation of teacher errors and capacity mismatch, and explicit handling of data scarcity or privacy constraints. Responsible, deployment-oriented distillation therefore requires principled recipe design, evaluation on long-tail and shifted data, and often the use of complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations. Across vision, speech, language, and graph modalities, KD methods exploit soft targets, feature- and attention-level alignment, contrastive and adversarial objectives, and architecture-aware design to trade accuracy for latency, memory, or privacy. Practical success depends on choices about teacher-student design, data availability and quality, and optimization strategies; contemporary work emphasizes combining representation-level objectives, teacher-friendly or teacher-free approaches, and data-aware training to produce robust, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, multi-level approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as an integrated pipeline—combining soft-target transfer, intermediate-representation supervision, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely delivers strong efficiency–performance trade-offs across modalities. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, appropriate distillation signals, and careful handling of data, rare or edge cases, and transferred errors or biases. A production-ready KD strategy therefore combines representation-aware objectives, student-aware architecture design, and orthogonal compression steps to meet real-world constraints while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a multifaceted toolkit for shrinking large neural models while retaining much of their accuracy. Approaches include matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, transforming architectures to be resource-efficient, and designing teacher–student curricula or multi-teacher aggregations. KD is applied across supervised, self-supervised, few-shot, federated, and privacy-constrained scenarios and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align layers and capacity, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; when designed carefully, KD enables deployment of compact models for diverse NLP and vision tasks while exposing open questions about robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and versatile tool available today for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the core of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (representation alignment, data strategies, pruning/quantization, and privacy-preserving mechanisms), KD enables production-ready models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization instability, and risks of propagating teacher errors demand task-aware design, careful data handling, and hybrid engineering practices to obtain reliable results in realistic deployments.

papers_seen.author: Rodgers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Central, Practical, and Contextual
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical method for compressing large deep models into smaller students that are suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses many signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention, relational structure) and workflows (offline, online, multi-teacher, data-free). While KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, its success depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation targets and interfaces, the availability and provenance of data, and complementary compression and architecture choices. Effective use of KD therefore treats it as a configurable, task-aware component within a broader compression pipeline rather than a one-size-fits-all recipe.

papers_seen.author: Simon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that are suitable for deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Research has broadened KD from simple softened-logit matching to a toolbox that includes intermediate-feature alignment, relational or attention-based objectives, multi-teacher and staged training schedules, and data strategies ranging from augmentation to synthetic or data-free generation. When combined with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware adaptation, KD enables substantial efficiency gains while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Success hinges on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to map heterogeneous teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or mismatched data; remaining challenges include domain shift, capacity mismatch, low-frequency behavior in sequence tasks, and privacy-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable transfer of predictive power from large, expensive models to smaller, efficient ones. The literature has expanded beyond soft-label matching to include internal-representation distillation, module replacement, self-distillation, selective sample transfer, and adaptations for constraints such as privacy, communication, and low-precision inference. Applied across domains—from NLP rankers and translation to graph, vision-language, and speech systems—these methods trade off fidelity, efficiency, and robustness through a variety of algorithmic and engineering solutions.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation condenses information from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet constraints of latency, memory, data access, or privacy. A rich family of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation imitation, multi-teacher and online schemes, self-distillation, and data-free or federated variants—have been developed and combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture design to produce compact models that often retain much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on the choice of distillation targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, availability and quality of data (or synthetic alternatives), and complementary training or architectural strategies. Key limitations remain around robustness, fairness, domain shift, and principled teacher selection, and ongoing work targets federated and privacy-sensitive settings as well as methods that pre-train compact students before distillation.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, but Not Universal Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective and versatile strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed—choosing what to transfer (logits, features, relations), preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with complementary methods such as quantization or architecture search—distillation can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities. However, KD has limits: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity or absence, and optimization subtleties can reduce gains. Practical deployment therefore benefits from hybrid pipelines that adapt KD objectives to task constraints, incorporate robustness and privacy considerations, and use auxiliary compression techniques where appropriate.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transforms large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring behavioral and representational information. Across vision, language, graph, and federated settings, KD variants—ranging from softened-output matching to intermediate-feature imitation, relational objectives, and multi‑teacher or online schedules—enable practical deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation pipelines, often combined with pre-training and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), produce compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting application-specific requirements. However, effective distillation depends on student capacity, data or synthetic-data strategies, teacher quality, and attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift; these limitations motivate hybrid pipelines and careful evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational structure. The technique has diversified into a family of methods (logit matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free and federated variants) and is frequently combined with pruning, quantization, pretraining, and augmentation to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on matching distillation strategy to goals (latency, privacy, robustness) and on careful handling of teacher quality, student capacity, and available data.

papers_seen.author: Guerra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or structural relationships. Over the past decade KD has broadened from simple logit-matching to a flexible toolkit that includes feature- and attention-level supervision, multi-teacher and online protocols, data synthesis and data-free approaches, and composition with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on careful design choices—what signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize distillation data, and how to validate robustness and fairness. Persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors, preserving long-tail or rare-token behaviors in language tasks, and robustness under domain shift; addressing these requires integrated, task-aware pipelines rather than a single off-the-shelf recipe.
