papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. The literature documents a spectrum of KD objectives (soft-output matching, intermediate feature and attention imitation, relational losses), protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi-teacher, and teacher-free), and data strategies (original-data distillation, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when the distillation recipe is matched to student capacity, architecture heterogeneity, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can retain much of a teacher’s performance across modalities, but persistent challenges include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, robustness under distribution shift, and distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Gomez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) comprises a family of training strategies that transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives; remaining challenges include preserving rare-event behavior, robustness under distribution shift, principled teacher–student pairing, and reliable distillation without original data.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compression, Generalization, and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a multifaceted technique that both compresses large models for efficient deployment and provides regularizing, transfer, and adaptation benefits beyond simple model-size reduction. KD can be integrated with architectural compression, multi-teacher training, and modality transfer to produce compact models that retain or even improve task performance while enabling deployment on heterogeneous devices and privacy-sensitive settings. However, KD is not a silver bullet: teacher quality, data heterogeneity, and distilled-data artifacts can harm downstream behavior, so careful protocol design (multi-teacher aggregation, mixing hard labels, data-aware schemes, or data-free metadata approaches) and attention to internal-representation alignment are necessary to realize KD’s full potential.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation in Practical Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across modalities and tasks, distillation enables deployment of powerful pretrained models in resource-constrained settings, supports specialization (e.g., task or domain adaptation), and can be combined with complementary compression techniques (quantization, pruning, architecture search) to produce practical, production-ready models. Advances in distillation methodology — including multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, teacher meta-learning, and task-aware layer-wise alignment — address fundamental challenges of capacity mismatch, information selection, and optimization stability, leading to more robust and efficient student models. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core component of any production-focused compression pipeline for deep learning and NLP systems, and that research emphasis on better teacher–student dynamics and task-aware transfer will yield the largest practical gains.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied methodology for transferring learned behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models to achieve deployable efficiency gains. KD encompasses multiple transfer signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational/attention patterns) and is commonly integrated with complementary compression methods and data strategies to address latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on design choices about what and how to transfer, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and measures to mitigate propagated errors or robustness failures.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Tool for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Deployment in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for transferring capabilities from large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or modality-limited models. When combined with complementary strategies—domain adaptation, feature-level matching, data augmentation, and meta-learning—distillation enables practical deployment across constrained devices, heterogeneous federated systems, and domain-shifted settings. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization subtleties and mismatches between teacher and student require methodological care and, in some cases, alternative regularization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single training heuristic into a flexible, system-level approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across multiple signal types (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational structure), procedural variants (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules), and data regimes (real-data, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). When designed as part of a pipeline that includes pretraining of compact architectures and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD routinely produces models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. Success depends on careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity, deliberate handling of distillation data and domain shift, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Bounded Component of Practical Model-Compression Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, deployable models from larger teachers. When treated as a modular element of a compression pipeline—combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, and complementary primitives such as pruning or quantization—KD routinely yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs. Its reliability depends on deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, and how to handle data, privacy, and distributional concerns. KD should therefore be the default tool in compression workflows but applied with explicit mitigations for its known limits (capacity mismatch, teacher artifacts, rare-token behaviors, and robustness under shift).

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression and Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a core engineering technique that enables deployment, adaptation, privacy, and robustness for large neural models in real-world systems. By treating distillation as a family of methods—ranging from output soft-target transfer to feature- and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and privacy-aware protocols—practitioners can compress models while preserving task performance and satisfying latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. Thoughtful application of KD, combined with complementary methods (pretraining, projector design, multi-stage schedules, and careful handling of teacher imperfections), yields compact models that are practical for production while exposing clear avenues for further research.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, multi-level approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as an integrated pipeline—combining soft-target transfer, intermediate-representation supervision, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely delivers strong efficiency–performance trade-offs across modalities. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, appropriate distillation signals, and careful handling of data, rare or edge cases, and transferred errors or biases. A production-ready KD strategy therefore combines representation-aware objectives, student-aware architecture design, and orthogonal compression steps to meet real-world constraints while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multifaceted Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a single training trick but a central, practical framework for compressing large models into deployable students. When treated as a toolbox—combining soft-label transfer, representation-level alignment, data augmentation or synthesis, and integration with other compression methods—KD enables substantial reductions in memory and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, realizing those gains requires deliberate design: choosing which teacher signals to transfer, addressing optimization and capacity mismatches, and using data-aware or data-free strategies when original training data are unavailable. I argue that KD should be the core component of any production-focused compression pipeline, paired with representation-level objectives and careful data strategies to mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression: A Conditional, Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible, modality-agnostic approach to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as the default starting point for compression, KD provides multiple complementary signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational objectives) that—when matched to student capacity and combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies—produce strong efficiency–accuracy trade-offs. However, KD is not universally sufficient: practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, data availability and provenance, domain shift, teacher errors, and robustness/fairness constraints. A pragmatic compression pipeline therefore places KD at its center but integrates pretraining, architecture adaptation, data-aware distillation schedules, and explicit evaluation and mitigation of failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a multifaceted toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques include matching teacher output distributions, transferring intermediate representations or relational structure, and ensembling or online schemes. In practice KD is combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, and can serve beyond compression as an implicit regularizer, an enabler of domain adaptation, and a mechanism for privacy-aware release. Effectiveness depends on choices about teacher quality and design, student capacity and architecture mapping, the availability or synthesis of distillation data, and targeted interventions to preserve robustness and mitigate undesirable transferred behaviors. A task- and deployment-aware KD pipeline that selects what and how to transfer—sometimes staged or hybridized with complementary compression primitives—yields the most reliable real-world outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Central Role and Evolving Practices of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental and versatile approach for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. It enables compact, efficient student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, supports deployment on resource-constrained devices, and can be adapted to privacy-sensitive or distributed settings. Recent advances extend distillation beyond simple logits matching to many-to-many layer mapping, task-adaptive compression, teacher-aware training, adversarial and data-free scenarios, and robustness-aware objectives. Together these developments show that distillation is both a practical engineering tool and a rich research paradigm for addressing capacity, data availability, privacy, and robustness constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Wyatt
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical set of techniques for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple information channels (softened outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational signals, and contrastive or adversarial objectives) and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data-free generation). When designed with attention to teacher–student capacity, data availability, and task constraints, KD enables substantial efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance; however, reliable deployment requires addressing capacity mismatch, distributional robustness, bias transfer, and limited-data or privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Marks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Conditional Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, multi-signal approach that reliably reduces model size and inference cost when used as part of a task- and deployment-aware compression pipeline. KD works by transferring teacher behavior via soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data synthesis to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on choices about what to distill, how to align teacher and student, student capacity and pretraining, the provenance or synthesis of distillation data, and explicit defenses for robustness, fairness, and domain shift. Treating KD as a configurable toolkit—paired with complementary compression primitives and careful evaluation—yields the most reliable path to compact, high‑quality models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Miranda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Central, Practical, and Context‑Aware for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD offers multiple transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure) and works across modalities and deployment regimes, but it is not sufficient in isolation: its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data provenance, and targeted remedies for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. Viewing KD as the central component of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline—combined with complementary primitives such as quantization, pruning, and architecture adaptation, and guided by student-aware objectives and careful data strategies—yields the most reliable path to resource-constrained deployment.

papers_seen.author: Butler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Composable Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible method for producing compact neural models from larger teachers. KD supplies multiple transferable signals (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention/relational patterns) and, when combined with complementary compression primitives and careful data and architecture choices, enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD alone does not eliminate capacity mismatch, teacher error propagation, data scarcity, or robustness and fairness risks; reliable compression therefore treats KD as the central component of a broader, task‑aware pipeline that includes explicit evaluation and mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, modular approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or relational structure. Empirical practice shows KD yields substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy with modest accuracy loss when distillation signals, data strategies, and student architectures are aligned to deployment constraints. KD is most effective when treated as part of an integrated compression pipeline that combines distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; its recurring failure modes include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, limited or private data, domain shift, and degraded long-tail behavior. Addressing those limits requires careful selection of distillation targets, data or synthesis strategies, multi-teacher or staged schedules, and evaluation of robustness and fairness in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has evolved from a single training heuristic into a flexible set of methods that enable compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring outputs, internal representations, or relational structure from teachers to students, distillation can materially reduce model size and inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Practical deployment requires matching the distillation strategy to task and deployment constraints, combining distillation with complementary compression techniques, and addressing limits such as capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and possible propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core and Its Limits for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer information at multiple levels (output logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure), be applied with or without original training data, and be combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, the availability and nature of data, and how to handle heterogeneity or robustness concerns. A pragmatic KD protocol blends pre-training of compact architectures, appropriate choice of distillation signals, data strategies (including data-free methods when needed), and complementary compression techniques, while actively addressing teacher weighting and domain-shift risks.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Task-Aware, Multi-Tool Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single recipe but as a flexible family of methods that, when combined with task-aware design and complementary compression techniques, enables deployment of compact models with strong utility. KD can transfer final-output behavior, intermediate representations, and structured relationships; it can operate with or without original training data, be adapted for privacy-sensitive or federated settings, and be combined with quantization or pruning to meet hardware constraints. Effective practice requires attention to what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how KD is integrated into the broader compression pipeline to avoid propagation of teacher biases or degradation on rare or shifted data.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practices, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD techniques include matching softened outputs, imitating intermediate features or attention patterns, and using multi- or self-distillation schedules; they are often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet deployment constraints. KD has been effective across vision, language, speech, and retrieval tasks, but its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student. Practical pipelines therefore choose distillation signals and data strategies that suit the target task, and complement KD with additional compression and validation to mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, and brittleness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more private students by transferring information from a teacher. Research over the past decade has explored a spectrum of KD variants — from soft-label logits transfer to feature-map matching, adversarial and online schemes, few-shot and privacy-preserving compression, and theoretical analyses of when and why distillation helps. Empirical work shows KD improves deployment practicality across vision, speech, NLP, graph, and generative models, while recent studies examine robustness, data-efficiency, the role of pre-training, and the impact of teacher quality. Important open directions include principled methods for sample selection, cross-domain transfer, formal guarantees under limited data or adversaries, and integrating KD with compression primitives such as pruning and structured sparsity.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity models (teachers) into smaller, more efficient models (students). Across vision and language, practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, architectural design, and quantization) and with strategies for scarce or missing data to obtain deployable models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical success depends on choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, attention), how to align heterogeneous architectures, the role of pre-training for compact models, and mechanisms to preserve robustness and rare-token behaviors. Data-free distillation, multi-task or multi-teacher schemes, and targeted representation matching extend KD’s applicability to many real-world settings.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into compact students to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When treated as a composable system—selecting appropriate distillation signals, matching architectures or mapping layers, managing data (including synthetic or data-free inputs), and combining KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search—KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains while preserving most of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal remedy: careful attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data provenance, domain shift, and robustness or fairness is required. A practical stance treats KD as the central element of a broader compression pipeline, guided by task-aware signal design and rigorous evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and accelerates large neural models by transferring information from one or more teacher models into a smaller student. Across vision and language, KD variants extend from logit-matching to feature- and attention-level transfer, multi-teacher ensembling, online/co-distillation, privacy-aware and federated setups, and combinations with quantization or structured pruning. Practical pipelines combine KD with architecture-aware transformations, domain adaptation, and task-specific pretraining to obtain compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Despite empirical success across modalities and deployment settings, trade-offs remain in teacher selection, information type to transfer, stability for heterogeneous architectures, and theoretical interpretation of what is transferred; these motivate further research into adaptive teacher weighting, feature alignment layers, and scalable privacy-preserving distillation for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Compression Strategy — Practical Strengths, Necessary Complementary Tools, and Concrete Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven to be a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. When treated as a design problem and combined with complementary methods and data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: success depends on matching teacher and student capacity, aligning inputs and internal representations, handling limited or absent data, and explicitly managing robustness, fairness, and transferred biases. I argue KD should be the default starting point for production compression pipelines, applied with explicit attention to complementary compression primitives, data synthesis or rehearsal methods, and evaluation safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is established as a central, practical approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. A broad family of distillation signals (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure) and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free) together with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) enable substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher’s effectiveness. Success depends on task- and student-aware design choices, including what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to manage limited or private data, and how to mitigate teacher-induced errors or robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Hubbard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates through multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational structure) and routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs. However, KD alone cannot guarantee robustness, fairness, or optimal hardware utilization: reliable deployment requires task-aware choices about what to distill, how to align teachers and students, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. I argue KD should be treated as the central component of a multi-tool compression pipeline—indispensable in practice but conditional on careful system-level design to meet production constraints and mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single heuristic into a flexible, multi-signal engineering toolkit central to practical model compression. KD transfers teacher behavior to smaller students via softened outputs, intermediate-representation or attention imitation, and relational or contrastive objectives; when combined with data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized) and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design) it routinely yields compact models that recover much of teacher performance. Success in practice depends on student capacity, teacher quality, availability and selection of distillation data, and careful alignment of objectives and architectures; important open problems remain in data-free distillation, robustness under distribution shift, avoiding propagation of teacher biases and rare-case failures, and principled teacher selection.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Uses, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely applied paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient students for deployment under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. A spectrum of techniques—from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—supports a range of practical trade-offs. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while reducing footprint, but success depends on student capacity, data availability, and careful design choices; important open problems remain around robustness, principled teacher selection, and reliable distillation under heterogeneous or private data regimes.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Insufficient Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has evolved from a single training heuristic into a flexible set of methods that enable compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring outputs, internal representations, or relational structure from teachers to students, distillation can materially reduce model size and inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Practical deployment requires matching the distillation strategy to task and deployment constraints, combining distillation with complementary compression techniques, and addressing limits such as capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and possible propagation of teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while often preserving much of the teacher's effectiveness. KD methods range from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations or using adversarial generators when training data are unavailable; they have been successfully applied across vision, generative modeling, recommender systems, and large pretrained language models. However, KD’s success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to address limited or private data, robustness, and bias—so practitioners must pair KD with task-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives to get reliable, deployable results.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Dependent Engine for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a configurable toolkit—choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data or synthesis strategies to use—KD frequently yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss. Its practical success depends on pairing distillation with complementary compression methods, careful data and curriculum design, and explicit evaluation of robustness and fairness; KD is therefore best used as the core of hybrid compression pipelines rather than a universal, one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Hurley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Compression: Central, Conditional, and Pipeline‑Oriented
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible method for converting large, high‑performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely reduces latency, memory, and compute while retaining much of teacher performance when integrated with appropriate design choices. However, KD is not a standalone cure: reliable compression requires task‑aware choices about what signals to transfer, alignment of teacher and student, thoughtful data strategies, and combination with complementary compression primitives to address capacity, robustness, and fairness constraints.
